Name: Meadow Management at Adelaide Local Nature Reserve
Stump Up For Trees
Description: A community charity planting one million trees in the Brecon Beacons area of south-east Wales.

Name: Restoring Seagrass & Oysters to North West Scotland
Description: The Scottish charity, Seawilding, is working with communities to restore native oyster beds and seagrass meadows in Loch Craignish.

Name: Northey Island Saltmarsh Restoration
Description: Restoring lost saltmarsh on a remote island in Essex, cared for by the National Trust.

Name: Heal Somerset
Description: Transforming a site in Somerset from nature-poor to nature-rich, creating an inspiring place for wildlife and people.

Name: Cambridge City Chalk Streams Project
Description: Restoring Cambridge's chalk streams into thriving, resilient ecosystems and reviving wildlife habitats.

Name: Dundreggan Estate
Description: The 10,000‑acre Dundreggan Estate in Glenmoriston is Trees for Life’s pioneering rewilding site, expanding Caledonian pinewood, restoring peatlands and running a public rewilding centre for research and education.

Name: Boothby Wildland
Description: Nattergal is rewilding Boothby Graffoe estate in Lincolnshire, restoring wood pasture, wetlands and species-rich grassland for nature recovery.

Name: Eastern Moors Partnership
Description: A partnership of National Trust and RSPB managing 7,800 acres of moorland in the Peak District for waders, heathland and low-intensity grazing.

Name: South Arran MPA
Description: South Arran Marine Protected Area, Scotland’s first community‑led MPA, safeguards seagrass, maerl beds and nursery grounds around the Isle of Arran and bans bottom‑trawling to let marine life recover.

Name: The Grange Project
Description: The Grange Project is transforming former pasture into a diverse agroforestry and rewilding hub with orchards, wood pasture and community events in the Malvern Hills.

Name: Harold's Park Wildland
Description: Nattergal’s Harold’s Park estate on the Essex‑Hertfordshire border is transitioning from arable to dynamic wood‑pasture, wetlands and natural grazing for biodiversity credits and public engagement.

Name: Hepple Wilds
Description: Hepple Wilds in Northumberland is restoring hill‑ground heath, riparian woodland and juniper scrub alongside regenerative sheep farming and award‑winning gin distilling.

Name: Geltsdale
Description: RSPB Geltsdale in the North Pennines uplands combines blanket bog, hay meadows and heathland management to support hen harriers, black grouse and curlews.

Name: Hesketh Out Marsh
Description: RSPB Hesketh Out Marsh on the Ribble Estuary is one of the UK’s largest recent realignment projects, restoring saltmarsh for thousands of wintering waders and wildfowl.

Name: High Fen Wildland
Description: High Fen Wildland straddles the Suffolk‑Cambridgeshire claylands where Nattergal is restoring wood pasture, ponds and fen meadow for landscape‑scale biodiversity recovery and nature finance.

Name: Knepp Estate
Description: The pioneering 3,500‑acre rewilding project in West Sussex where free‑roaming livestock drive natural processes, supporting nightingales, turtle doves, purple emperor butterflies and thriving biodiverse wetlands.

Name: Mapperton Wildlands
Description: A 1,600‑acre rewilding initiative on the Mapperton Estate in West Dorset where White Park cattle, Exmoor ponies and beavers are helping to regenerate wood‑pasture, wetlands and species‑rich grassland.

Name: Steart Marshes
Description: WWT’s flagship 490‑ha managed realignment on the Severn Estuary transforming arable farmland into saltmarsh and freshwater wetlands that protect homes from flooding and host thousands of waterbirds.

Name: Moor Barton
Description: A 120‑acre regenerative farm and rewilding project on the edge of Dartmoor where agroforestry, pasture‑fed cattle and river restoration are bringing back wildlife and engaging volunteers.

Name: Purbeck Heaths NNR
Description: A 3,400‑ha ‘super reserve’ uniting RSPB Arne, National Trust and other partners to reconnect heathland, saltmarsh and dunes on Dorset’s Isle of Purbeck for nightjars, reptiles and pollinators.

Name: Sunart Fields
Description: Regenerative croft on the shores of Loch Sunart, Highlands, where native woodland planting, no‑dig veg and rare-breed cattle are restoring soil health and biodiversity while supplying the local community.

Name: Wicken Fen NNR
Description: National Trust’s oldest nature reserve – 880 ha of lowland fen, wet grassland and meres near Ely managed by Konik ponies and Highland cattle, home to more than 9,000 recorded species.

Name: Belmont Estate
Description: Historic 500‑ha estate in the Gordano Valley near Bristol transitioning to agroecology, wood‑pasture and wet meadow creation while offering nature education and venison from wild fallow deer.

Name: Borders Forest Trust
Description: Charity restoring native woodland at Carrifran Wildwood, Talla & Gameshope and Corehead in the Southern Uplands – over 7,000 acres of peatland, montane scrub and river habitat for eagles to return.

Name: Wild Ken Hill
Description: Norfolk coastal estate combining regenerative farming, rewilding and traditional conservation across 1,500 ha of heath, woodland, wetland and arable re‑sown with herbal leys.

Name: Creating Wilder Forests
Description: Forestry England’s national programme to restore wilder processes—natural regeneration, dynamic rivers, large herbivores—across the public forest estate’s 250,000 ha.

Name: Wilder Doddington
Description: Historic Lincoln estate dedicating 770 ha to scrub, wetland and low‑input grazing, with beaver release planned and community science mapping swift and barn‑owl recovery.

Name: Wild Tolworth
Description: Citizen Zoo project re‑imagining suburban green spaces along the Hogsmill River in Kingston, with beavers licensed in 2024 and community meadows boosting pollinators.

Name: Wild Ennerdale
Description: Partnership of Forestry England, National Trust & United Utilities letting natural processes shape 4,700 ha of valley woodland, river and lake fringes in the western Lake District.

Name: Wild Kielder
Description: Forestry England initiative restoring bogs, riparian woodland and montane scrub in 62,000‑ha Kielder Forest & Water Park, Northumberland, benefiting ospreys, redsquirrels & water voles.

Name: Conservation tasks with East Sussex Biodiversity Action Team
Dungeness
Description: Big shingle peninsula with freshwater pits, wet grassland and wildflower meadows – flagship birding on Romney Marsh.

Name: Cliffe Pools
Description: Lagoons and pools on the Thames estuary with masses of water birds and big skies.

Name: Pulborough Brooks
Description: Arun Valley wetlands and wooded heath. Family friendly trails and hides with seasonal spectacles from nightingales and dragonflies to winter flocks of waders and ducks.

Name: Pagham Harbour LNR
Description: Sheltered inlet of saltmarsh, mudflats, lagoons and shingle beach south of Chichester. Waymarked routes from the visitor centre with year round coastal birding.

Name: Broadwater Warren
Description: Restored lowland heath and woodland on the High Weald ridge near Tunbridge Wells. All ability loop plus longer trails with chances of woodlark, nightjar and adders.

Name: Medmerry
Description: Managed realignment creating vast saltmarsh and pools behind the shingle bank. 10 km of level trails for walking and cycling with avocets, harriers and migrating waders.

Name: Blean Woods
Description: Ancient coppice woodland north of Canterbury with glades and heathy rides. A stronghold for the rare heath fritillary plus nightingales, woodpeckers and spring bluebells.

Name: Fore Wood
Description: Peaceful ghyll woodland at Crowhurst with steep, fern lined ravines and spring carpets of bluebells. Short waymarked trails through coppice, oak and hornbeam.

Name: Chartwell
Description: Winston Churchill’s family home set in the Weald of Kent, with rooms preserved as he left them, hillside gardens, woodland trails and lakes offering views across the countryside.

Name: Scotney Castle
Description: Romantic moated 14th century castle ruins set within a picturesque garden and 19th century house, woodland and parkland on the Kent-Sussex border near Lamberhurst.

Name: Devil’s Dyke
Description: A spectacular dry valley on the South Downs with panoramic views, Iron Age ramparts and classic walking routes. Popular for picnics, kite-flying and paragliding.

Name: Emmetts Garden
Description: A hillside Edwardian garden famed for spring blossom, bluebells and far-reaching views over the Weald, with rock garden, wildflower meadows and family waymarked trails.

Name: Black Down
Description: The highest point in Sussex - an expanse of heath, woodland and sunken lanes above Haslemere with long vistas, wildlife and the Temple of the Winds viewpoint.

Name: Slindon Estate
Description: A 3,500-acre estate in the South Downs with ancient woodland, chalk downland, orchards and miles of tracks from the village, perfect for walking, cycling and wildlife.

Name: Petworth House and Park
Description: Grand Baroque house famed for its art and sculpture collections, set within Capability Brown’s deer park, with sweeping views, lakes and miles of waymarked paths.

Name: Sissinghurst Castle Garden
Description: World-famous garden created by Vita Sackville-West and Harold Nicolson, with intimate garden rooms, tower views, surrounding farmland and nature-rich estate in the High Weald.

Name: Standen House and Garden
Description: Arts and Crafts family home near East Grinstead with Morris & Co. interiors, hillside garden, woodlands and views over the Medway valley with year-round walks.

Name: Cissbury Ring
Description: One of Britain’s largest hillforts above Worthing with Neolithic flint mines, chalk grassland wildlife and far-reaching coastal and Wealden views along open downland.

Name: Smallhythe Place
Description: Former home of Victorian actor Ellen Terry near Tenterden, with intimate cottage rooms, rose-filled gardens, working theatre barn and exhibitions celebrating her stage career.

Name: Sheffield Park and Garden
Description: Historic landscape garden famed for autumn colour, lakes and vistas, linked to the wider estate and Bluebell Railway, with year-round walks and accessible routes.

Name: Knole
Description: A vast 15th century house set within a 1,000-acre medieval deer park in Sevenoaks, with showrooms, Gatehouse Tower, conservation studio and miles of public parkland to explore.

Name: Woolbeding Gardens
Description: A horticultural haven near Midhurst with garden rooms, follies, a contemporary glasshouse and riverside walks - open by pre-booked ticket on selected days.

Name: Otmoor
Description: Oxfordshire wetland restoration with lapwings, curlew, and starling murmurations.

Name: Stour Estuary
Description: Ancient woodland and estuarine shorelines rich in fungi, bluebells, and wintering birds.

Name: The Lodge
Description: Headquarters reserve with heathland, ancient woodland, and gardens attracting nuthatches and green woodpeckers.

Name: Bempton Cliffs
Description: Dramatic chalk cliffs hosting England’s largest mainland seabird colony including gannets and puffins.

Name: Surlingham Church Marsh
Description: Tranquil Broadland reserve with circular trails through wet woodland and reedbeds beside the Yare.

Name: Sherwood Forest
Description: Historic ancient woodland, home to the Major Oak and hundreds of veteran trees supporting wildlife.

Name: St Bees Head
Description: Dramatic sea cliffs on the Cumbrian coast, the only breeding cliff colony of seabirds in northwest England.

Name: Campfield Marsh
Description: Solway Firth coastal wetlands with saltmarsh, peat bog, and reedbeds important for barnacle geese.

Name: Winterbourne Downs
Description: Chalk grassland restoration in Wiltshire bringing back skylarks and butterflies like the Adonis blue.

Name: Brading Marshes
Description: Island wetland on the Isle of Wight, featuring reedbeds, grassland, and saline lagoons.

Name: Beckingham Marshes
Description: Restored wet grassland on the River Trent, providing nesting habitat for lapwing and redshank.

Name: Haweswater
Description: Upland valley in the Lake District where woodland and peatland restoration supports red squirrels and golden eagles.

Name: Titchwell Marsh
Description: Coastal wetland and lagoons on the North Norfolk coast supporting avocets, bearded tits, and harriers.

Name: Sandwell Valley
Description: Oasis of wetland and woodland near Birmingham supporting kingfishers, lapwings, and otters.

Name: Havergate Island
Description: Suffolk estuary island, breeding site for avocets and terns, accessible only by pre-booked boat trips.

Name: Arne
Description: Iconic heathland and woodland on Poole Harbour with diverse species including sika deer and Dartford warbler.

Name: Bowling Green Marsh
Description: Estuarine wetland at the Exe Estuary, ideal for viewing waders and ducks from accessible hides.

Name: Langford Lowfields
Description: Gravel pits restored to reedbeds and lagoons for bitterns and warblers along the River Trent.

Name: Leighton Moss
Description: Lancashire’s largest reedbed and a haven for bitterns, bearded tits, and otters.

Name: Lakenheath Fen
Description: Created from farmland into vast reedbeds and poplar woodland, home to bitterns, cranes, and otters.

Name: Middleton Lakes
Description: River Tame wetlands of reedbeds and meadows, ideal for kingfishers, bitterns, and dragonflies.

Name: Lodmoor
Description: Coastal wetland with reedbeds and saline lagoons supporting avocets, terns, and marsh harriers.

Name: Garston Wood
Description: Ancient woodland in Dorset supporting bluebells, dormice, and great spotted woodpeckers.

Name: Marshside
Description: Coastal grassland on the Ribble Estuary hosting breeding waders and large wintering flocks of geese.

Name: Aylesbeare Common
Description: Lowland heath supporting silver-studded blue butterflies and nightjars; part of the East Devon Pebblebed Heaths.

Name: Rainham Marshes
Description: Urban-edge reserve along the Thames, a mix of grazing marsh, scrapes, and boardwalk trails.

Name: Strumpshaw Fen
Description: Broadland reedbed reserve renowned for swallowtail butterflies, bitterns, and marsh harriers.

Name: Saltholme
Description: Wetland mosaic of lakes and grassland on Teesside, with family-friendly hides and paths.

Name: Blacktoft Sands
Description: Freshwater lagoons on the Humber estuary famous for marsh harriers, avocets, and bearded tits.

Name: Dearne Valley Bolton Ings
Description: Restored industrial wetland supporting wildfowl, waders, and reedbed specialists in South Yorkshire.

Name: Fairburn Ings
Description: Restored open-cast mine transformed into lagoons, reedbeds, and woodland alive with waterfowl.

Name: Valley Wetlands
Description: Valley Wetlands is home to one of the most important reedbeds in Wales, which alongside the surrounding marshes, make this patch perfect for a rich variety of wetland birds, plants and bugs.

Name: Buckenham Marshes
Description: Broadland grazing marshes supporting winter flocks of wigeon and pink-footed geese.

Name: Hodbarrow
Description: Coastal lagoon on the Cumbrian coast with tern islands, wildflowers, and panoramic views of the Duddon Estuary.

Name: Frampton Marsh
Description: Coastal freshwater and saltmarsh habitats attracting avocets, godwits, and ruffs.

Name: Nagshead
Description: Ancient oak woodland in the Forest of Dean, known for pied flycatchers and wood warblers.

Name: Dove Stone
Description: Upland reservoir landscape with moorland and woodland habitats, supporting peregrines and red grouse.

Name: Dearne Valley Old Moor
Description: Wetland and meadow complex within the South Yorkshire coalfield, home to bittern and kingfisher.

Name: Exminster & Powderham Marshes
Description: Twin wetland reserves on the Exe Estuary supporting overwintering ducks and breeding waders.

Name: Berney Marshes
Description: Broadland grazing marsh supporting breeding waders, wildfowl, and roosting pink-footed geese.

Name: Boyton Marshes
Description: Coastal grazing marsh in Suffolk adjacent to Hollesley Marshes, home to avocets and redshank.

Name: Labrador Bay
Description: Coastal cliffs and grasslands with rare cirl buntings and sweeping sea views.

Name: Ouse Washes
Description: Seasonal floodplain between river embankments attracting thousands of ducks and waders in winter.

Name: Fowlmere
Description: Small chalk stream-fed wetland with clear pools supporting kingfishers and water voles.

Name: Tottenham Marshes (Lee Valley)
Description: Lea Valley floodplain meadows and wetlands with regular habitat tasks via Lee Valley volunteering.

Name: WWT London Wetland Centre (Barnes)
Description: Flagship urban wetland in Barnes with structured corporate and individual volunteering.

Name: Richmond Park (The Royal Parks)
Description: Large National Nature Reserve with practical conservation and ranger-style volunteering.

Name: Rodley Nature Reserve
Description: Volunteer-managed wetland in west Leeds, created from a former water treatment works.

Name: Ashton Court Estate
Description: 850-acre park on Bristol’s edge with deer park, grassland and woodland volunteering.

Name: Chorlton Water Park
Description: Local nature reserve with lake, woodland and grassland on Manchester’s fringe; TCV sessions common.

Name: Saltram Park
Description: National Trust estate on Plymouth’s edge with woodland and estuary habitats; conservation volunteer days.

Name: Whitlingham Country Park
Description: Broads-edge park on Norwich fringe with woodland and lakes; conservation and litter action days.

Name: Gosforth Nature Reserve
Description: Urban-edge reserve with woodland, reedbeds and lake on Newcastle’s northern fringe; regular habitat workdays.

Name: Ferry Meadows (Nene Park)
Description: Large country park in Peterborough with rivers, lakes and meadows - structured corporate days.

Name: Paxton Pits Nature Reserve
Description: Gravel pit lakes, reedbeds and riverside meadows near St Neots with strong volunteer programme.

Name: WWT Washington Wetland Centre
Description: Sunderland wetlands with structured volunteer roles and corporate conservation days.

Name: Kingsbury Water Park
Description: Lakes and wetlands in the Tame Valley offering habitat management and access volunteering.

Name: Rushcliffe Country Park
Description: Green Flag award park near Nottingham with habitat work, orchard care and community days.

Name: Fletcher Moss Park & Parsonage Gardens
Description: Riverside park in Didsbury with wetlands, gardens and community conservation days.

Name: Watermead Country Park
Description: Linked lakes and meadows along the River Soar and Wreake with active volunteer groups.

Name: Stover Country Park
Description: Devon’s popular country park with lake, heathland and woodland; regular conservation tasks.

Name: Sutton Park National Nature Reserve
Description: Expansive heathland, wetlands and woodlands in north Birmingham; ranger-supported volunteer tasks.

Name: Caldecotte Lake
Description: Linked lakes and grasslands with orchards and bat roosts on MK’s southern edge; conservation workdays.

Name: Hartlebury Common NNR
Description: Lowland heath with rare invertebrates and reptiles; path, scrub and habitat work parties.

Name: Stony Stratford Nature Reserve
Description: Ouse Valley wetlands with boardwalks and meadows on MK’s northwest fringe; active volunteer team.

Name: Ryton Pools Country Park
Description: Lakes, meadows and woods east of Coventry; ranger-supported conservation volunteering.

Name: Howe Park Wood
Description: Ancient woodland SSSI in south-west MK with rides, glades and regular habitat tasks.

Name: Abberton Reservoir
Description: Abberton Reservoir is a pumped storage freshwater reservoir in eastern England near the Essex coast, with an area of 700 hectares.  Most of its water is pumped from the River Stour.

Name: Abbot's Wood
Description: Abbot's Wood, managed by Forestry England, is a mixed woodland in East Sussex offering walking trails, an accessible path, and a children's play area. It is noted for its diverse butterfly population, including the Pearl-bordered Fritillary, alongside open spaces and a pond.

Name: Abbotts Hall Farm
Description: Abbotts Hall Farm is a 282 hectare nature reserve in Great Wigborough in Essex.  It is the head office of the Essex Wildlife Trust, which manages the site.

Name: Abernethy Forest
Description: Abernethy Forest is a remnant of the ancient Caledonian pine forest in the Cairngorms National Park. It hosts rare species like capercaillie and Scottish crossbill, alongside red squirrels and pine martens. The RSPB manages the reserve, focusing on habitat restoration and protecting its unique biodiversity.

Name: Abney Park Cemetery
Description: Abney Park Cemetery, a Grade II* listed woodland memorial park and nature reserve, is one of London's 'Magnificent Seven'. Located in Stoke Newington, Hackney, it functions as a significant ecological and historical site for the community.

Name: Acorn Bank
Description: Acorn Bank, near Penrith, Cumbria, features extensive traditional fruit orchards and one of the largest medicinal and culinary herb collections in northern England. The tranquil estate includes Crowdundle Beck, a historic watermill, and gardens with woodland walks, offering visitors a peaceful natural experience.

Name: Adcombe Wood
Description: Adcombe Wood is an ancient woodland with a diverse range of trees including oak, ash, and hazel. It features a varied ground flora, stream, and coppiced areas. The site is a habitat for dormice, bats, and various bird species.

Name: Addison and Hedgefield
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 14 hectares.

Name: Affpuddle Forest
Description: Affpuddle Forest, near Affpuddle in Dorset, is a mixed woodland providing a quiet walking experience. The site features broadleaf and conifer trees, with some areas managed for timber. Informal paths allow visitors to explore and observe local wildlife.

Name: Ainsdale Sand Dunes NNR
Description: Ainsdale Sand Dunes NNR is a coastal dune system in Merseyside, covering 500 hectares. It protects rare wildlife, including natterjack toads and sand lizards. The reserve features diverse habitats like dunes, slacks, and pine woodland, supporting a wide array of plant and insect species.

Name: Aira Force & Ullswater
Description: Aira Force waterfall cascades 65ft amidst ancient woodland in the Ullswater valley, Lake District. Conservation efforts protect red squirrel habitats and riparian areas. Visitors explore walking trails and an arboretum.

Name: Albany Park River Restoration
Description: Albany Park River Restoration enhances the River Lea in Enfield, north London. It improves river health and biodiversity through habitat creation, natural channel design, and increased public access. The project forms part of a larger initiative to restore Enfield's rivers.

Name: Aldbury Nowers
Description: Aldbury Nowers is a 19.7 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in the Chiltern Hills, north-east of Tring in Hertfordshire.

Name: Alde Mudflats
Description: Alde Mudflats is a 22 hectare nature reserve west of Iken in Suffolk.  It is owned by the Crown Estate and managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Alderfen Broad
Description: Alderfen Broad is a 21.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-east of Norwich in Norfolk, England.

Name: Alderley Edge
Description: Alderley Edge is a dramatic red sandstone escarpment in Cheshire, offering panoramic views. It is a geological SSSI, known for its ancient copper mines and unique mineralisation. The site is also linked to the legend of the Wizard of Alderley.

Name: Aldouran Glen
Description: Aldouran Glen is an ancient Atlantic Rainforest near Leswalt, Dumfries & Galloway. This steep-sided glen offers a rich habitat for wildlife and fungi. The woodland features well-maintained paths for visitors to explore its diverse ecosystem.

Name: Alexandra Park Oldham
Description: Alexandra Park in Oldham is a Grade II* listed Victorian park, opened in 1865. It features a boating lake, conservatory, children's play area, and various sports facilities. The park offers walking paths and formal gardens, providing a community green space. Ecologically, it contains small areas of clough woodland and is part of a network of habitats around Oldham town centre, including Glodwick Lows Local Nature Reserve and Snipe Clough. It is also connected to the Northern Roots Project, aiming to create a large urban farm and eco-park.

Name: Alice Holt Forest
Description: Alice Holt Forest is a managed woodland in Hampshire, bordering Surrey, offering extensive walking and cycling trails, play areas, and a visitor centre. This popular site provides diverse habitats for wildlife and supports timber production and environmental education.

Name: Allan Bank
Description: Allan Bank is a National Trust property near Grasmere, Lake District, linked to William Wordsworth and Canon Hardwicke Rawnsley. The estate features a house, woodlands, and walled garden, offering public access and views across the Grasmere valley.

Name: Allen Banks and Staward Gorge
Description: Allen Banks and Staward Gorge is an extensive area of woodland in the North Pennines, home to a wide range of wildlife. The River Allen flows through the gorge, creating a diverse habitat. It features a Victorian viewing tower and walking trails.

Name: Aller and Beer Woods
Description: Aller and Beer Woods is a 56.9 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Allerthorpe Common
Description: Allerthorpe Common is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and nature reserve in the East Riding of Yorkshire, England.  It is located close to the town of Pocklington.

Name: Allt-yr-Yn
Description: Allt-yr-Yn is a 3.5-hectare urban nature reserve in Newport, South Wales. It features ancient woodland, grassland, and ponds, providing habitat for diverse wildlife. The site is actively managed for biodiversity, offering public walking trails.

Name: Alpine Meadow
Description: Alpine Meadow is a 0.4 hectare nature reserve near Berkhamsted in Hertfordshire in the United Kingdom.

Name: Altar Stones
Description: Altar Stones is a 3.7-hectare nature reserve in Markfield in Leicestershire.

Name: Alvecote Pools Nature Reserve
Description: Alvecote Pools is a 128.7-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and nature reserve situated alongside the River Anker on the border of Warwickshire and Staffordshire. Formed by mining subsidence, it features a mosaic of shallow pools, fens, reedbeds, and woodlands, making it regionally important for over 100 bird species, dragonflies, beetles, and spiders.

Name: Amberley Wildbrooks
Description: Amberley Wild Brooks or Amberley Wildbrooks is a 327.5-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Storrington in West Sussex.

Name: Amwell Nature Reserve
Description: Amwell Nature Reserve, near Hertford, is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, internationally recognised for its diverse wildlife. Managed by Lee Valley Regional Park Authority and Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust, it offers excellent birdwatching, especially for wintering wildfowl and Bittern, alongside dragonflies and unique flora.

Name: Amwell Quarry
Description: Amwell Quarry or Amwell Nature Reserve is a 37 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Great Amwell in Hertfordshire.  The planning authority is East Hertfordshire District Council.

Name: Ancaster Valley
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 10 hectares.

Name: Ancells Farm
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Ancells Farm is a 12-hectare nature reserve in Fleet in Hampshire.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Anderby Marsh
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 24 hectares.

Name: Andrew's Wood
Description: Andrews Wood,, is a nature reserve managed by the Devon Wildlife Trust.  It is also a 23.

Name: Anglesey Abbey
Description: Anglesey Abbey is a former priory, country house, and extensive gardens in Lode, Cambridgeshire. The site includes a working watermill, a landscaped parkland, and a significant collection of art and artefacts. Visitors explore the house, formal gardens, and wider estate.

Name: Ardley Wood Quarry
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Ardley Cutting and Quarry is a 40.1-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-west of Bicester in Oxfordshire.

Name: Arger Fen and Spouse's Vale
Description: Arger Fen is a 49.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of Sudbury in Suffolk, England.

Name: Arkaig Community Forest
Description: Arkaig Community Forest, in partnership with Woodland Trust Scotland, co-manages the Loch Arkaig Pine Forest, a significant area of native Caledonian pinewood and other woodlands covering over 1,000 hectares on the south side of Loch Arkaig in the Scottish Highlands. The charity works to restore native pinewoods and manages them for community benefit and sustainable income.

Name: Arle Grove
Description: Arle Grove is a 5-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.  The site is listed in the 'Cotswold District' Local Plan 2001–2011 as a Key Wildlife Site.

Name: Arlington Court
Description: Arlington Court is a Regency house and estate in North Devon, situated on the edge of Exmoor. It features a picturesque Victorian garden, extensive ancient woodlands, and is home to a designated wildlife reserve with over 20 miles of footpaths, a bird hide, and a heronry. The estate also houses the National Trust Carriage Museum.

Name: Arnold's Meadow
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 3 hectares.

Name: Arnside Knott
Description: Arnside Knott is a prominent limestone hill offering panoramic views of Morecambe Bay and the Lake District Fells. Managed by the National Trust, this site features ancient woodlands, wildflower-rich grasslands, and diverse wildlife. Public footpaths allow access to its summit.

Name: Arreton Down
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Arreton Down is a chalk hill in the central part of the Isle of Wight in southern England.  It is public access land, with 29.

Name: Ash Ranges
Description: Ash Ranges is a 1,392-hectare nature reserve west of Pirbright in Surrey.  It is owned by the Ministry of Defence and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Asham Meads
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 23 hectares.

Name: Ashford Warren and Hoads Wood
Description: Ashford Warren and Hoads Wood is a 34.5-hectare nature reserve north of Ashford in Kent.

Name: Ashleworth Ham
Description: Ashleworth Ham is a 104.73-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Ashridge Estate
Description: From rolling chalk hills to ancient woodlands, the Ashridge Estate boasts a diverse landscape and a rich history. Covering 5,000 acres, it supports varied wildlife, including fallow deer, and features significant ancient trees. Visitors explore diverse habitats.

Name: Ashtead Common
Description: Ashtead Common is a 200-hectare ancient woodland in Surrey, managed by the City of London Corporation. A National Nature Reserve and SSSI, it features historic wood pasture, veteran trees, and diverse wildlife, offering public walking trails.

Name: Ashtead Park
Description: Ashtead Park is a 24.2-hectare Local Nature Reserve in Ashtead in Surrey.

Name: Ashton Court
Description: Ashton Court is a mansion house and estate to the west of Bristol in England.  Although the estate lies mainly in North Somerset, it is owned by the City of Bristol.

Name: Ashwell Quarry and Quarry Springs
Description: Ashwell Quarry and Quarry Springs is a three hectare nature reserve managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust near Ashwell in Hertfordshire.  Ashwell Quarry is owned by a local farmer, and Quarry Springs by Hertfordshire County Council.

Name: Askham Bog
Description: Askham Bog is small area of peat bog and Site of Special Scientific Interest situated within the Vale of York in North Yorkshire, England.  It lies to the south-west of York, north of Copmanthorpe and near Askham Richard and Askham Bryan.

Name: Aston Clinton Ragpits
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Aston Clinton Ragpits is a 2.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Aston Clinton in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Astonbury Wood
Description: Astonbury Wood is a nature reserve of Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust.  It is an ancient woodland, near Stevenage in Hertfordshire, England.

Name: Attenborough Nature Reserve
Description: Attenborough Nature Reserve is a nature reserve at Attenborough, Nottinghamshire, England, located 5 mi south west of Nottingham city centre.  It is owned and managed by Nottinghamshire Wildlife Trust, supported by Broxtowe Borough Council, following the completion of purchase from Cemex UK in December 2020.

Name: Attingham Park
Description: Attingham Park is an elegant Regency mansion and historic parkland near Shrewsbury, Shropshire. The estate features a deer park, walled garden, and an impressive collection of art and furniture. Visitors can explore the mansion, grounds, and play areas, offering a rich historical experience.

Name: Aubrey Buxton
Description: Aubrey Buxton Nature Reserve is a 9.7-hectare nature reserve west of Elsenham in Essex.

Name: Audrey's Meadow
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Audrey's Meadow is a 2-hectare nature reserve in Newbury in Berkshire.  It is owned by West Berkshire Council and managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Aughrim Quarry
Description: Aughrim Quarry, near Belfast, is a former quarry site where a heather transplant pilot project was undertaken in 2017. Volunteers helped clear scrub to restore habitats. This project, part of a larger Landscape Partnership scheme, aimed to re-establish native heather in the area.

Name: Ausewell Wood
Description: Ausewell Wood is a large ancient woodland in the Dart Valley, bordering Dartmoor National Park. It is jointly managed by the Woodland Trust and National Trust and is a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). It features diverse habitats including oak and conifer woodland, open heathland, and riverside meadows, hosting rare wildlife such as redstarts, lesser spotted woodpeckers, pied flycatchers, and the elusive hazel dormouse. The site also holds historical significance with Scheduled Monuments, stone circles, and old mine workings.

Name: Avebury
Description: Avebury is a Neolithic henge monument and stone circle complex in Wiltshire, featuring large standing stones, ancient earthworks, and processional avenues. This archaeological landscape showcases early human settlement and rituals, managed by the National Trust.

Name: Aversley Wood
Description: Aversley Wood is an ancient woodland in Cambridgeshire, managed by the Woodland Trust. It features oak, ash, and hazel coppice, supporting diverse ground flora. Public footpaths provide access. Parking is available.

Name: Avery's Pightle
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Avery's Pightle is a 1.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Enborne in Berkshire.

Name: Avon Valley Woods
Description: Avon Valley Woods, managed by The Woodland Trust, is a beautiful stretch of ancient woodland in South Devon, covering around 139 hectares near Woodleigh. It features a diverse mix of steep, valley-sided ancient woodland and areas of new woodland, brimming with wildlife and a wide variety of tree species. Visitors can explore a network of paths and observe local wildlife, with the River Avon running through the site.

Name: Axmouth to Lyme Regis Undercliffs NNR
Description: A unique coastal landslip wilderness in Dorset and East Devon, part of the Jurassic Coast World Heritage Site. Rich in diverse flora and fauna, the reserve features a dynamic landscape of ancient woodlands, scrub, and grasslands formed by historic geological movements.

Name: Aykley Wood
Description: Aykley Wood is an ancient semi-natural woodland and local nature reserve in Durham. It features a significant number of mature oak trees, providing an important green space and habitat for wildlife within the city.

Name: Baal Hill Wood
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 16 hectares.

Name: Babbacombe & Oddicombe Cliffs
Description: Babbacombe and Oddicombe Cliffs form a scenic stretch of coastline in South Devon. Public footpaths offer expansive views over Lyme Bay. The National Trust maintains these steep coastal habitats for wildlife and public access.

Name: Babcary Meadows
Description: Babcary Meadows is a 13.6 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Babcary in Somerset, notified in 1988.

Name: Bacombe Hill
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Bacombe and Coombe Hills is a 76.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Upper Bacombe in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Baddesley Clinton
Description: Baddesley Clinton is a moated manor house, home to the Ferrers family for 500 years. The site features priest holes, a walled garden, and ancient woodland walks, offering insights into its rich history and architecture.

Name: Badgeworth SSSI, Gloucestershire
Description: Badgeworth SSSI is a 3. 08-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire notified in 1954 and renotified in 1983.

Name: Baggy Point
Description: Baggy Point, a headland in North Devon, offers dramatic clifftop walks and panoramic sea views along the South West Coast Path. It supports diverse marine birds and coastal flora; grey seals are often visible. The site is managed for conservation.

Name: Baker's Pit Nature Reserve
Description: Baker's Pit Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and former china clay quarry in the parish of Ludgvan, west Cornwall managed by the Cornwall Wildlife Trust.  The reserve is on the moorland of Noon Diggery and is south of the Castle-an-Dinas hillfort and Roger's Tower, a folly built within the hillfort.

Name: Balloo Wetland Nature Reserve
Description: Balloo Wetland, near Bangor, is a nature reserve featuring a mosaic of habitats, including ponds, reedbeds, wet grassland, and woodland. It supports a variety of wildlife, such as otters, kingfishers, and various invertebrates. A boardwalk offers visitor access.

Name: Balls Wood
Description: Balls Wood is a 58.5-hectare nature reserve managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust in Hertford Heath in East Hertfordshire.

Name: Ballyaghagan Nature Reserve
Description: Ballyaghagan Nature Reserve protects ancient woodland and wildflower meadows near Belfast. It preserves one of the area's few remaining ancient woodland fragments, featuring notable wildflowers in spring and early summer. It is home to diverse bird and invertebrate species.

Name: Ballynahone Bog
Description: Ballynahone Bog is a significant lowland raised bog in Northern Ireland. It supports rare plants like bog-rosemary and great sundew, along with diverse insect life. The site forms part of the Moyola River catchment area, providing crucial habitat for various wildlife species.

Name: Balmacara Estate
Description: Balmacara Estate is a crofting estate near Kyle of Lochalsh, Scotland, on Loch Alsh. The diverse landscape features coastal areas, lochs, moorland, and Coille Mhòr, an ancient Atlantic oak forest. The estate is actively managed for conservation and sustainable crofting.

Name: Bamff Wildland
Description: Bamff Wildland is a rewilding project in Perthshire, Scotland. It focuses on the reintroduction and monitoring of European beavers, observing their transformative impact on the landscape. The estate actively supports biodiversity and habitat restoration.

Name: Banovallum House
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 1 hectares.

Name: Bardney Limewoods NNR
Description: Bardney Limewoods NNR is a complex of ancient woodlands between Lincoln and Horncastle in Lincolnshire. It preserves the largest remaining small-leaved lime woods in Britain, rich in biodiversity. The reserve offers habitats for various flora and fauna, including rare invertebrates.

Name: Barkway Chalk Pit
Description: Barkway Chalk Pit is a small former chalk quarry and nature reserve in North Hertfordshire, managed by North Hertfordshire District Council. It is a Regionally Important Geological Site (RIGS) due to its chalk exposure, displaced by the Anglian ice sheet. The site features chalk grassland and scrub, supporting wildflowers like bee orchid and common spotted orchid, and butterflies such as the grizzled skipper and brown argus.

Name: Barkway Chalk Pit
Description: Barkway Chalk Pit is a small nature reserve in Barkway in North Hertfordshire.  It was managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Barle Valley
Description: Barle Valley is a 1,540 acres Site of Special Scientific Interest within Exmoor National Park, situated in the counties of Devon and Somerset through which the River Barle flows.  It was notified in its current form under the Wildlife and Countryside Act in 1988.

Name: Barlow Burn
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 20 hectares.

Name: Barn Elms Wetland Centre SSSI
Description: Barn Elms Wetland Centre SSSI, located in London, is a nationally important site for wildlife. It encompasses a variety of wetland habitats and supports diverse bird species and other wildlife in an urban environment. It is managed to conserve its ecological value.

Name: Barnsley Warren
Description: Barnsley Warren is a 61.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954 and renotified in 1984.

Name: Barnwell Meadows
Description: Barnwell Meadows is a traditional hay meadow in the heart of Cambridge, managed by Cambridge Past, Present & Future. It supports diverse wildflowers, grasses, and insects, offering a glimpse into the area's agricultural past. Visitors enjoy peaceful walks and observe wildlife.

Name: Baron's Haugh
Description: Baron's Haugh is an RSPB reserve in Motherwell, North Lanarkshire, Scotland. It features a diverse wetland habitat alongside the River Clyde, attracting numerous waterfowl, waders, and other bird species throughout the year. Visitors can enjoy several trails and hides.

Name: Barossa
Description: Barossa is a 498-hectare nature reserve north of Camberley in Surrey.  It is owned by the Ministry of Defence and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Barrington Hill Meadow
Description: Barrington Court estate in Somerset features diverse landscapes, including extensive meadows that support a range of local wildlife. These grasslands are managed to enhance biodiversity, providing habitats for insects and ground-nesting birds within the historic grounds.

Name: Barrow Blow Wells
Description: Barrow Blow Wells is a local nature reserve with an area of over 2.7 ha located in Barrow-upon-Humber, North Lincolnshire, England.

Name: Barrow Haven Reedbed
Description: Barrow Haven Reedbeds is a local nature reserve with an area of over 12.7 ha located in Barrow-upon-Humber, North Lincolnshire, England.

Name: Barton Broad
Description: Barton Broad is a large lake that forms part of the River Ant which gives its name to a 164-hectare nature reserve north-east of Norwich in Norfolk.  The reserve is owned and managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Barton Meadows
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 32 hectares.

Name: Bassenthwaite Lake NNR
Description: Bassenthwaite Lake NNR is a shallow lake in the Lake District National Park, Cumbria. It hosts diverse habitats like reedbeds, woodlands, and open water, supporting a variety of wildlife including rare fish and otters.

Name: Basted Mill
Description: Basted Mill Public Open Space is located near Borough Green, Kent. It features diverse habitats including an old mill pond, meadows, and woodland, providing a haven for wildlife. Public access paths are available.

Name: Baston Fen
Description: Baston Fen is nature reserve of the Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust, near the village of Baston and about 5 miles north of Market Deeping, in Lincolnshire, England.  It is uncultivated fenland, which is a habitat for particular plants and wildlife.

Name: Bath Skyline
Description: The Bath Skyline, a six-mile National Trust route, overlooks Bath. It features ancient woodlands, Iron Age hill forts, hidden valleys, and wildflower meadows, supporting diverse wildlife habitats.

Name: Bathampton Meadows
Description: Bathampton Meadows is a riverside flood plain near Bath, offering tranquil green space and city skyline views. Popular for walking and cycling, the meadows support diverse wildlife, including birds and wildflowers, and are managed for conservation.

Name: Bawdeswell Heath
Description: Bawdeswell Heath, near Dereham, Norfolk, is a medieval heathland fragment. It features wet and dry heath, acid grassland, and woodland. Diverse flora and fauna thrive, including common lizards and adders. Site management maintains its character.

Name: Bay Pond
Description: Bay Pond is a 7-hectare nature reserve in Godstone in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Beacon Hill
Description: Beacon Hill is a peaceful woodland and recovering heathland site in Monmouthshire, Wales, located within the Wye Valley National Landscape. Managed by Natural Resources Wales, it offers stunning views and public footpaths, protecting diverse habitats and supporting varied wildlife, including Nightjars. Gwent Wildlife Trust is actively involved in conservation efforts and events at the site.

Name: Beacon Hill Country Park
Description: Beacon Hill Country Park in Leicestershire features ancient 600-million-year-old rocks and panoramic views across Charnwood Forest. The park contains mature woodlands, heathland, wildflower meadows, walking trails, and reconstructed Bronze Age log houses.

Name: Beam Parklands
Description: Beam Parklands is a multi-award-winning 53-hectare wetland park in the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham, managed by The Land Trust. Created as part of the Thames Gateway regeneration, it serves as a crucial flood defense and provides diverse habitats including open water, reedbeds, wet woodland, and grasslands for wildlife. The River Beam flows through the site, offering a valuable green space for local communities.

Name: Beckenham Place Park
Description: Beckenham Place Park in South London hosts the River Ravensbourne, a site of significant river restoration work. Thames21, in partnership with local groups, improves habitats and naturalises the river course, with ongoing volunteer tasks contributing to its ecological recovery.

Name: Beddington Farmlands
Description: Beddington Farmlands, a nature reserve in south London, is built on a former landfill site. Managed for biodiversity since the 1980s, it provides a crucial habitat for various wildlife, particularly birds. It serves as a significant area for ecological restoration.

Name: Bedford Purlieus National Nature Reserve
Description: Bedford Purlieus is a 211-hectare ancient woodland in Cambridgeshire, UK, and one of the largest ancient woodlands in lowland England. It is a National Nature Reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest, renowned for its exceptional diversity of trees, plants (including over 460 vascular plant species), and invertebrates. It is also home to over 40 species of breeding birds, including the Lesser Spotted Woodpecker. The site is managed by Forestry England for conservation and research.

Name: Bedfords Park
Description: Bedfords Park is a nature reserve located in Havering, offering panoramic views across London. It features woodlands, ponds, and meadows, supporting a variety of wildlife including red deer. The site has a visitor centre and promotes environmental education.

Name: Bedfords Park
Description: Bedfords Park is public open space of 215 acres or approximately 87½ hectares near Havering-atte-Bower in the London Borough of Havering in England.  It is one of three large parklands around Havering-atte-Bower; the others are Havering Country Park and Pyrgo Park.

Name: Bedgebury National Pinetum and Forest
Description: Home to a world-leading collection of conifers, the National Pinetum is a centre for research and conservation. The wider forest offers walking, cycling, and family activities, supporting biodiversity and public engagement.

Name: Bedgebury National Pinetum and Forest
Description: Bedgebury National Pinetum and Forest, located in the High Weald AONB, is a world-leading collection of conifers and a significant center for conifer conservation and research. Managed primarily by Forestry England, it offers diverse wildlife habitats, extensive trails for recreation, and serves as a living laboratory for conservation efforts.

Name: Bedgebury Pinetum
Description: Bedgebury National Pinetum and Forest, located in Kent, is a renowned arboretum housing a world-leading collection of conifers and other trees. It offers extensive walking and cycling trails, alongside a popular adventure play area.

Name: Beechenhurst - Forest of Dean
Description: Beechenhurst Lodge is a popular visitor centre within the Forest of Dean, Gloucestershire. It offers a café, adventure play, sculpture trail, and easy access walks. Visitors can find information and explore Go Ape Tree Top Adventure.

Name: Beinn Eighe and Loch Maree Islands National Nature Reserve
Description: Beinn Eighe and Loch Maree Islands National Nature Reserve, established in 1951, is the UK's first National Nature Reserve. Located in Wester Ross, Scotland, it encompasses a vast area from loch-side to mountain top, including the Beinn Eighe ridge and over 60 islands in Loch Maree. It is famed for its ancient Caledonian pine forests, diverse upland habitats, and a wealth of Scottish wildlife such as golden eagles, pine martens, and black-throated divers.

Name: Beinn Eighe NNR
Description: Beinn Eighe and Loch Maree Islands National Nature Reserve, established 1951 in Wester Ross, Scottish Highlands, is the UK's first National Nature Reserve. This approximately 4,800-hectare site features ancient Caledonian pinewood, mountain habitats and diverse wildlife.

Name: Belfairs Woodland Centre
Description: Great Wood and Dodd's Grove is a 36.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Leigh-on-Sea in Essex.

Name: Belhus Chase
Description: Belhus Chase is a 55.44-hectare (136.99 acres) site near Aveley in Essex, within the Thames Chase Community Forest. This new woodland, acquired by the Woodland Trust in 1998, features a mix of mature native broadleaves and younger plantings, creating a parkland atmosphere. It offers walking routes through diverse habitats, providing a green space for wildlife and visitors, and is connected to the historic Belhus Estate.

Name: Belsize Wood
HostOrg: Camden Council (managed with The Conservation Volunteers - Camden Green Gym)
Description: Belsize Wood is a 0.7 hectare Local Nature Reserve in Belsize Park, London Borough of Camden. It is managed by Camden Council, with active involvement from Camden Green Gym volunteers who undertake woodland management, coppicing, path clearance, and litter picking. The site offers a peaceful retreat and habitat for wildlife in London.

Name: Belton Estate
Description: Belton Estate, a National Trust property in Lincolnshire, features a Grade I listed country house surrounded by a 1,300-acre deer park. The estate includes formal gardens, ancient woodland, and parkland. Visitors can explore varied landscapes and observe wildlife.

Name: Belvide Reservoir
Description: Belvide Reservoir is a Site of Special Scientific Interest in South Staffordshire. Managed as a private bird reserve, it focuses on wildlife conservation and bird observation. The site hosts a bird ringing station, recording over 200 species annually. Access requires a permit.

Name: Bemersyde Moss
Description: Bemersyde Moss is a Scottish Wildlife Trust nature reserve and a Site of Special Scientific Interest at Bemersyde in the Scottish Borders area of Scotland.  Located near the River Tweed, this reserve features a mix of marshlands, willow scrub, and open water, creating a vital habitat for diverse wildlife.

Name: Ben Lawers NNR
Description: Ben Lawers National Nature Reserve in Perthshire, a site of international importance for arctic-alpine flora. Seven Munros offer challenging walks with dramatic views. The reserve is managed for nature conservation and protects a unique plant community.

Name: Ben Lomond
Description: Ben Lomond is Scotland's most southerly Munro, offering stunning views across Loch Lomond & The Trossachs National Park. The National Trust for Scotland manages conservation efforts, focusing on path maintenance, erosion control, and supporting native wildlife.

Name: Beningbrough
Description: Beningbrough Hall is a Georgian mansion near York, managed by the National Trust. It features extensive gardens, including a walled garden and a dedicated Wilderness Project area for nature exploration and play. The hall houses artworks from the National Portrait Gallery.

Name: Benmore Botanic Garden
Description: Benmore, within Argyll Forest Park, features an impressive avenue of towering Californian giant redwoods. This botanical garden near Dunoon showcases a wide variety of trees and shrubs, including a unique Chilean rainforest glade, offering diverse plant collections.

Name: Benshaw Moor
Description: Benshaw Moor is nature reserve of the Northumberland Wildlife Trust, near Elsdon, in Redesdale, Northumberland, England.  It is a large site with varied habitats.

Name: Bentley Community Woodland
Description: Bentley Community Woodland is a former colliery site in Doncaster, transformed into a green space with native trees, shrubs, ponds, and wildflower meadows. It enhances local biodiversity and is managed with community volunteer involvement.

Name: Bernwood Forest
Description: Bernwood Forest, a former royal hunting ground, consists of various woodlands across Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire. It provides diverse habitats for rare butterflies and wildlife. Visitors can enjoy walking, cycling, and horse riding on established trails, with public access maintained for recreation.

Name: Bernwood Forest
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Bernwood Forest is a forest in England.  Historically it was one of several forests of the ancient Kingdom of England and was a Royal hunting forest.

Name: Bernwood Meadows
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Bernwood Meadows is a 7.5-hectare nature reserve near Oakley in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Berry Head
Description: Berry Head is an iconic headland and National Nature Reserve, home to the UK's most southerly guillemot colony. Features include a Napoleonic fort and spectacular views across Torbay. It offers opportunities for wildlife spotting.

Name: Berry Head National Nature Reserve
Description: Berry Head is a limestone headland and National Nature Reserve on the South West Coast Path, offering extensive views across Torbay. This Site of Special Scientific Interest features Napoleonic War fortifications and supports significant seabird colonies, including guillemots and kittiwakes.

Name: Betchworth Quarry and Lime Kilns
Description: Betchworth Quarry and Lime Kilns is a 27-hectare nature reserve north of Betchworth in Surrey.  Betchworth Quarry only is managed by Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Bevercotes Wood
Description: Bevercotes Wood is a Sherwood Community Woodland near Newark, transforming former arable land into a diverse habitat. It offers surfaced paths for walking, cycling, and horse riding, alongside quiet areas for reflection, providing space for people and wildlife.

Name: Bevere Fish Pass
Description: Bevere Fish Pass is a significant fish pass near Worcester on the River Severn. It allows migratory fish, such as shad and salmon, to bypass Bevere Weir and access upstream spawning grounds. The pass is a key part of the Unlocking the Severn project.

Name: Bicester Wetland Reserve
Description: Bicester Wetland Reserve, a former Thames Water sewage sludge disposal site, offers a mosaic of habitats including ponds, scrapes, and reedbed. It supports diverse wildlife, notably wading birds like lapwing and curlew, and various invertebrates. The reserve aims to increase biodiversity within its varied landscapes.

Name: Biddulph Grange Garden
Description: Biddulph Grange Garden in Staffordshire features a Victorian stumpery, a unique garden design utilising upturned tree roots and stumps for dramatic effect. The site also includes various themed gardens, reflecting global horticultural styles from the 19th century.

Name: Big Pool Wood
Description: Big Pool Wood is a Nature reserve located near Gronant, Flintshire, Wales.  The site is part of the Dee Estuary SSSI & SAC due to the unique wildlife and organisms found in the area.

Name: Big Waters
Description: Big Waters is nature reserve in Tyne and Wear, England, a pond formed by former mine workings.  It is the largest body of open water in the region, and is designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Bigbury Camp
Description: Bigbury Camp is a univallate hill fort in the parish of Harbledown and Rough Common in Kent in England.  The fort is a Scheduled Ancient Monument, with a list entry identification number of 1005169.

Name: Bigbury-on-Sea & Burgh Island Coast
Description: Bigbury-on-Sea, a coastal village in South Devon, offers sandy beaches, rock pools, and views of Burgh Island. The island is accessible via a tidal causeway or sea tractor, featuring an Art Deco hotel. The area is popular for watersports, walks, and wildlife observation.

Name: Birch Moss Covert Nature Reserve
Description: Birch Moss Covert Nature Reserve is a nature reserve managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.  It is located on Carrington Moss, north of Sinderland Lane, which runs off the A56 road at Broadheath, Greater Manchester.

Name: Birkrigg Common
Description: Birkrigg Common, a limestone grassland, provides panoramic views of Morecambe Bay and the Furness Peninsula. A Site of Special Scientific Interest, it hosts diverse flora, fauna, and ancient cairns. Managed for conservation and public access.

Name: Birling Gap and the Seven Sisters
Description: Birling Gap and the Seven Sisters form a dramatic coastal landscape of chalk cliffs and shingle beach. Rapid erosion reveals new fossils. The area provides habitat for diverse wildlife and offers popular cliff-top walks.

Name: Birmingham EcoPark
HostOrg: Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust
Description: The Birmingham EcoPark is an environmental education centre in the Small Heath area of Birmingham, England, operated by the Wildlife Trust for Birmingham and the Black Country.  Each year there are thousands of visitors to the site.

Name: Bishop Middleham Quarry
Description: Bishop Middleham Quarry is a disused quarry, about 4 kilometres north-west of Sedgefield, County Durham, England.  Quarry-working here ceased in 1934, and the site has since been colonised by vegetation.

Name: Bishop Wood
Description: Bishop Wood, a diverse woodland in North Yorkshire, features mature oak, birch, and hazel trees, alongside conifers. It supports roe deer, woodpeckers, and various butterfly species. This ancient site provides important habitats for fungi and invertebrates.

Name: Bishop Wood
Description: Bishop Wood is a large ancient woodland in North Yorkshire, featuring diverse broadleaf and conifer tree species and significant wildlife habitats. It offers walking trails and is known for its rich ground flora. Historically managed for timber, the site provides a tranquil environment for visitors.

Name: Bishop's Wood
Description: Bishop's Wood is a 33.7-hectare ancient woodland near Selby, North Yorkshire. The site features a diverse mix of tree species and supports rich wildlife, including ground flora. It offers walking trails and is part of a wider landscape.

Name: Bishopswood Meadows
Description: Bishopswood Meadows is a nature reserve situated within the Blackdown Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty in the county of Somerset, England.  The reserve comprises five fields totalling 9.

Name: Bisley and West End Commons and Reidon Hill
Description: Bisley and West End Commons is a 37.2-hectare Local Nature Reserve west of Woking in Surrey.

Name: Black Bourn Valley
Description: Black Bourn Valley, formerly called Grove Farm, is an 88 hectare nature reserve between Thurston and Elmswell in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Black Brook Nature Reserve
Description: Black Brook is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust, about 7 miles north-east of Leek, in Staffordshire, England.  It is moorland, part of Leek Moors, and most of it is in a Special Area of Conservation.

Name: Black Devon Wetlands
Description: Black Devon Wetlands is a key wildlife reserve near the Firth of Forth in Scotland. It features a mosaic of wetland habitats, including reedbeds, lagoons, and wet grassland. It provides a vital stopping point for migrating birds and supports many resident species. Visitors can observe diverse birdlife from hides.

Name: Black Firs and Cranberry Bog
Description: Black Firs and Cranberry Bog is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust, adjacent to Balterley Heath and about 1 mile north of the village of Betley, in Staffordshire, England.  It is an important peatland site; it is designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest, and a Ramsar site.

Name: Black Firs Wood Nature Reserve
Description: Black Firs Wood Nature Reserve is a 1.15-hectare nature reserve managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Black Lake Nature Reserve
Description: Black Lake is a nature reserve in Delamere Forest, Cheshire, England.  It lies in the southwestern corner of the forest, just south of the Manchester–Chester railway.

Name: Black Moss Covert Nature Reserve
Description: Black Moss Covert Nature Reserve is a 2.1 hectare nature reserve in England managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Black Mountain Quarry Biodiversity Transition
Description: The Black Mountain Quarry Biodiversity Transition project enhances biodiversity through habitat management, grassland restoration, scrub control, tree planting, and pond creation. This former quarry within the Belfast Hills offers a mosaic of habitats for various wildlife species.

Name: Black Plantation
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 14 hectares.

Name: Black Rocks
Description: Black Rocks is a prominent gritstone outcrop near Cromford, Derbyshire. It offers panoramic views over the Derwent Valley. Adjacent woodlands provide walking, cycling, and horse riding trails. The site is popular for rock climbing.

Name: Blacka Moor
HostOrg: Wildlife Trust for Sheffield and Rotherham
Description: Blacka Moor Nature Reserve is a nature reserve located on Hathersage Road between Sheffield and Hathersage in the Peak District National Park in the United Kingdom.  The site is managed by the Wildlife Trust for Sheffield and Rotherham.

Name: Blackburn Flow
Description: Blackburn Flow is a significant peatland restoration project, likely referring to work at Butterburn Flow, a key site within the Border Mires on the Cumbria/Northumberland border. As part of the Great North Bog initiative, it aims to rewet 450 hectares of peatland to reduce carbon emissions and enhance wildlife habitats.

Name: Blackcap
Description: Blackcap offers spectacular views over the South Downs National Park and chalk grasslands near Lewes. This site features ancient trees and diverse flora and fauna, characteristic of a chalk downland environment.

Name: Blackhall Rocks
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 32 hectares.

Name: Blackleach Country Park
Description: Blackleach Country Park is a Green Flag park in Salford, Greater Manchester. It features a large reservoir, woodland, and grassland, providing habitat for diverse wildlife including waterfowl and woodland birds. Visitors enjoy walking, fishing, and birdwatching.

Name: Blackmoor Copse
Description: Blackmoor Copse is a woodland in southeast Wiltshire, England, managed as a nature reserve by the Wiltshire Wildlife Trust.  The copse lies within Pitton and Farley parish, about 5+1⁄2 miles east of Salisbury.

Name: Blackpool Sands & Strete Gate Coast
Description: This stretch of the South Devon coast features Strete Gate and Blackpool Sands, a shingle beach. The area, part of Start Bay, is known for its diverse geology, coastal habitats, and scenic views. The National Trust cares for segments of the coastline, providing access for visitors.

Name: Blagrove Common
Description: Blagrove Common is a 4. 0-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest in Green End near Sandon in Hertfordshire.

Name: Blair-nam-Faoileag NNR
Description: Blair-nam-Faoileag National Nature Reserve protects a vast area of blanket bog, forming part of the internationally important Flow Country of Caithness and Sutherland. This peatland landscape supports diverse wildlife.

Name: Blakeney National Nature Reserve
Description: Blakeney National Nature Reserve in Norfolk features Blakeney Point, home to England's largest grey seal colony. It serves as a vital nesting ground for various bird species and holds international importance for wildlife. Visitors can explore the shingle beach.

Name: Blakey Topping
Description: Blakey Topping is a distinctive conical hill in the North York Moors National Park. This landmark offers panoramic views across the Pickering valley and features unique geological formations, including sandstone outcrops. It forms part of a wider landscape managed for its natural beauty and heritage.

Name: Blashford Lakes
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Blashford Lakes is a 159-hectare nature reserve north of Ringwood in Hampshire, England, which is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.  The site is part of the River Avon System Nature Conservation Review site, Grade I, Avon Valley Ramsar site, River Avon Special Area of Conservation and Special Protection Area, and of Avon Valley, which is a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Blaxhall Common
Description: Blaxhall Common is a nature reserve in the parish of Blaxhall in the East Suffolk District of Suffolk.  The reserve is owned by Blaxhall Parish Council and managed by Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Blenheim Farm
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Blenheim Farm is a 1-hectare nature reserve near Charlbury in Oxfordshire.  It is owned and managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Blickling Estate
Description: Blickling Estate in Norfolk features a Jacobean house, historic gardens, and extensive parkland with ancient trees. Managed by the National Trust, it offers woodland walks, lakeside paths, and diverse natural habitats near Aylsham.

Name: Blindley Heath
Description: Blindley Heath SSSI is a 26.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in the hamlet Blindley Heath, on the southern outskirts of Godstone in Surrey.

Name: Bloody Oaks Quarry
Description: Bloody Oaks Quarry is a 1.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-west of Great Casterton in Rutland.

Name: Blue Bell Hill
Description: Blue Bell Hill is a chalk hill between Maidstone and Rochester in the English county of Kent.  It overlooks the River Medway and is part of the North Downs.

Name: Blue House Farm
Description: Blue House Farm is a 242.8-hectare nature reserve and farm in North Fambridge, on the north bank of the River Crouch between Burnham-on-Crouch and South Woodham Ferrers in Essex.

Name: Bluebank Pools
Description: Bluebank Pools, on the Chesterfield Canal near Staveley, is a former subsidence flash. It now thrives as a vibrant wetland, teeming with diverse wildlife and offering a significant habitat for various species.

Name: Blythe Alive - River Blythe SSSI
Description: Blythe Alive focuses on restoring the River Blythe SSSI and its surrounding habitats. The project enhances biodiversity and climate change resilience by removing weirs, reconnecting the river with its floodplain, and creating new wetlands and ponds. It also involves community engagement.

Name: Bodnant Garden
Description: Bodnant Garden is a National Trust property near Tal-y-bont, Conwy, Wales. It features formal gardens, grand terraces, wooded glades, and an arboretum with champion trees. The garden offers stunning views of the Conwy Valley and Snowdonia.

Name: Bog Meadows
Description: Bog Meadows, situated off the Falls Road in West Belfast, is a vital urban nature reserve. It offers a mosaic of reedbeds, meadows, ponds, and woodland, providing sanctuary for diverse wildlife including water rail, snipe, and various dragonflies.

Name: Bolam Lake
Description: Bolam Lake Country Park, located between Belsay and Whalton, offers extensive footpaths, lakeside walks, and open grasslands. The site supports diverse wildlife, including red squirrels and birds, across its managed woodlands and meadows, providing recreational and nature study.

Name: Bolberry Down
Description: Bolberry Down offers dramatic coastal views near Salcombe. This area features rare wildflowers, birds, and insects, making it a valuable habitat. Visitors can walk the South West Coast Path and enjoy the rugged coastline.

Name: Bold Forest Park
Description: Bold Forest Park in St Helens is a significant regeneration project transforming 450 hectares of former industrial land into new woodlands, wetlands, and grasslands. It offers walking, cycling, and horse riding opportunities and is part of the larger Mersey Forest initiative.

Name: Bolderwood
Description: Bolderwood, located in the New Forest, features ancient woodlands and walking trails. Visitors can observe fallow deer from a purpose-built viewing platform at the deer sanctuary. The area offers various routes through mature trees and picnic facilities.

Name: Bolt Head to Bolt Tail
Description: This dramatic stretch of South Devon coastline between Bolt Head and Bolt Tail offers spectacular views and diverse wildlife. Walk the South West Coast Path, exploring jagged cliffs and secluded coves rich in maritime history.

Name: Boltby Forest
Description: Boltby Forest, a 632.1-hectare mixed woodland managed by Forestry England, is situated in the Cleveland Hills within the south-west corner of the North York Moors National Park. Dominated by Sitka spruce, it also features broadleaves and ancient woodlands, supporting diverse flora and fauna, including Lake Gormire SSSI. The forest offers extensive walking and cycling trails, with the Cleveland Way skirting its eastern edge, and provides views across the Vale of Mowbray.

Name: Bonny Wood
Description: Bonny Wood is a 20 hectare nature reserve east of Barking Tye in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Bonsai Bank
Description: Bonsai Bank is a flower-rich chalk grassland area within Denge Wood, known for its diverse orchid populations, including the rare Lady Orchid. It features stunted conifers, which gave it its name, and supports a rich ground flora on its sloping terrain.

Name: Booton Common
Description: Booton Common is an 8.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-west of Norwich in Norfolk, England.

Name: Borough Hill
Description: Borough Hill, a Local Nature Reserve near Daventry, comprises heathland, grassland, and scrub. It supports rare plants and diverse butterflies. The site includes an Iron Age hillfort and Roman villa remains, with views across Northamptonshire.

Name: Borrowdale Rainforest Project
Description: The Borrowdale Rainforest Project, a National Trust initiative, aims to restore and expand temperate rainforests across the Borrowdale valley in the Lake District. It focuses on regenerating ancient woodlands and enhancing biodiversity.

Name: Bossington Beach
Description: Bossington Beach, part of the Holnicote Estate in Somerset, is a shingle beach forming a natural barrier with saltmarshes. It offers views across the Bristol Channel and is a starting point for coastal walks.

Name: Bough Beech
Description: Bough Beech reservoir and surrounding woodland in west Kent is a Site of Special Scientific Interest. Formerly managed by Kent Wildlife Trust until July 2020, it is now managed by Sutton and East Surrey Water. It offers important habitats for wildfowl, waders, and gulls, with bird hides available for observation.

Name: Bouldnor Forest
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 38 hectares.

Name: Boundary Wood
Description: Boundary Wood is a newly established woodland site near Mansfield, Nottinghamshire, managed by Forestry England. It features a mix of broadleaf and conifer trees with accessible paths, contributing to local biodiversity and community green space.

Name: Bourne Mill
Description: Bourne Mill is a Grade I listed 16th-century watermill in Colchester, Essex, owned by the National Trust. Originally built as a fishing lodge in 1591, it was later converted into a fulling mill and then a corn mill. The site features a historic building with a working waterwheel, a large spring-fed millpond, and surrounding wetlands and woods. It is a haven for diverse wildlife, including kingfishers, various waterfowl, bats, dragonflies, and damselflies.

Name: Bourne Wood
Description: Bourne Wood, near Farnham in Surrey, is an ancient woodland on the Greensand Ridge. Managed by Forestry England, it offers walking paths through mature trees and open heathland, popular with locals and dog walkers. It serves as a haven for diverse wildlife.

Name: Bovey Heath
Description: Bovey Heath is a 32 hectare area of heathland between Bovey Tracey and Heathfield in south Devon, England.  Although primarily heathland habitat, the site has some wet mature oak woodland, and is home to rare species such as the Dartford warbler, European stonechat, European nightjar and the narrow headed ant.

Name: Bovey Valley Woods
Description: Bovey Valley Woods, within Dartmoor National Park, is an ancient woodland patchwork along the River Bovey. Managed by The Woodland Trust, it provides critical habitat for dormice, otters, and rare bats, featuring significant geological formations.

Name: Bow Creek Ecology Park
Description: Bow Creek Ecology Park is a wildlife haven in East London, at the confluence of Bow Creek and the River Thames. It features diverse wetland and brownfield habitats, supporting birds, insects, and plants, with peaceful walking routes and viewing platforms.

Name: Bowdown Woods
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Bowdown and Chamberhouse Woods is a 67.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Thatcham in Berkshire.

Name: Box Farm Meadows SSSI
Description: Box Farm Meadows is a 8.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1985.

Name: Box Hill
Description: Box Hill is a prominent North Downs summit in Surrey, England, offering panoramic views across the Surrey Hills. Managed by the National Trust, it features woodlands, chalk grasslands, and walking trails.

Name: Brackfield Wood
Description: Brackfield Wood is The Woodland Trust's First World War Centenary Wood for Ireland, nestled within the stunning Faughan Valley Woodlands, a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). It is home to native tree species and diverse wildlife, including red squirrel, otter, and Atlantic salmon in the River Faughan. The site offers a network of footpaths for walking and nature observation, providing views of the River Faughan, and connects with other woods in the Faughan Valley.

Name: Bradfield Woods
Description: Bradfield Woods is an 81.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between Bury St Edmunds and Stowmarket in Suffolk.

Name: Bradley Canal Restoration & Habitat Link
Description: This project restores a disused canal stretch in Bilston, West Midlands, creating a vital 'green corridor' linking existing green spaces. It aims to improve access to green and blue spaces and provide new walking and cycling routes.

Name: Bradwell Shell Bank
Description: Bradwell Shell Bank is a nature reserve on the coast of the Dengie Peninsula near Bradwell-on-Sea in Essex.  It is managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Braeburn Park
Description: Braeburn Park is a 22.3-hectare nature reserve in Crayford in the London Borough of Bexley.

Name: Bramley Bank
Description: Bramley Bank is a 10.3 hectare local nature reserve in Upper Shirley in the London Borough of Croydon.

Name: Bramshill Forest
Description: Bramshill Forest in Hampshire features ancient woodland, conifer plantations, and heathland. It provides habitat for rare species like the Dartford warbler, nightjar, and sand lizard. The forest offers various walking trails for visitors to explore its diverse landscapes.

Name: Brancaster Beach
Description: Brancaster Beach, on the Norfolk coast, is a vast National Trust sandy expanse popular for walking and birdwatching. The SS Vina shipwreck is visible at low tide. This site protects diverse coastal wildlife and offers expansive views.

Name: Brancaster Staithe
Description: Brancaster Staithe is a harbour village on the North Norfolk coast, managed by the National Trust. It features extensive saltmarsh and mudflats, home to diverse wading birds like oystercatchers and curlews. The area is popular for sailing and provides vital habitat.

Name: Brandlehow Woods
Description: Brandlehow Woods is an ancient woodland on the western shore of Derwent Water in the Lake District. The National Trust acquired it in 1902, making it their first property. It provides public access and walking routes near the lake.

Name: Brandon Country Park
HostOrg: West Suffolk Council and Forestry England
Description: Brandon Country Park, within Thetford Forest, Suffolk, covers 30 acres of parkland and 300 acres of woodland. It features an arboretum, lake, mausoleum, visitor centre, and a tea room. Miles of trails are available for walking, cycling, and riding.

Name: Brandon Marsh nature reserve
Description: Brandon Marsh is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and nature reserve in Warwickshire, England.  It is situated adjacent to the River Avon, near the village of Brandon, a few miles east of Coventry.

Name: Brankley Pastures
Description: Brankley Pastures is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is about 2.

Name: Branscombe to Beer Cliffs
Description: Branscombe to Beer Cliffs is a dramatic coastal area in East Devon, managed by the National Trust. It features striking cliffs, secluded beaches, and ancient woodlands. Part of the Jurassic Coast World Heritage Site, it offers diverse wildlife and geological formations.

Name: Brassey SSSI
Description: Brassey is a 2.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954 and renotified in 1983.

Name: Brean Down
