Description: Brean Down is a prominent limestone headland in Somerset, offering panoramic views over the Bristol Channel. It features an Iron Age hill fort and a 19th-century fort. The site is known for its diverse wildlife and coastal habitats, providing historical walks and natural beauty.

Name: Breckland
Description: Breckland in Norfolk and Suffolk is a 39,433 hectare Breckland_Forest Special Protection Area under the European Union Directive on the Conservation of Wild Birds.  The SPA partly overlaps the 7,544 hectare Breckland Special Area of Conservation.

Name: Bredhurst Wood
Description: Bredhurst Woods is a 600-acre (approximately 240-hectare) ancient woodland surrounded by chalk grassland, located on the North Downs in Kent. It is a Local Wildlife Site and part of the Kent Downs Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. Primarily managed by the Bredhurst Woodland Action Group (BWAG) in collaboration with Kent Wildlife Trust, the site features diverse oak, hornbeam, and sweet chestnut trees, and supports a rich biodiversity including fungi, invertebrates, butterflies (such as Adonis blue), and dormice.

Name: Brenchley Wood
Description: Brenchley Wood is a 15-hectare nature reserve south of Paddock Wood in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust, and it is part of the High Weald Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Name: Breney Common
Description: Breney Common is a nature reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest, noted for its biological characteristics, in mid Cornwall, England, UK.  It is located mainly in Lanlivery civil parish, with the Saints' Way footpath running through it.

Name: Brentmoor Heath and Folly Bog
Description: Brentmoor Heath is a 28.6-hectare Local Nature Reserve east of Camberley in Surrey.

Name: Brettenham Heath
Description: Brettenham Heath is a National Nature Reserve in Norfolk, located north-east of Thetford. It is an important area of heathland, woodland, and acid grassland, forming part of the Breckland Special Area of Conservation and Special Protection Area. The reserve supports breeding woodlark, nightjar, and stone-curlew, along with reptiles such as slow-worm, common lizard, and adder. It is home to a diverse flora with over 240 plant species recorded.

Name: Brickfield Meadow
Description: Brickfield Meadow is a 1.4-hectare nature reserve north of Maresfield in East Sussex.

Name: Briddlesford Woods
Description: Briddlesford Woods is an ancient woodland and Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) on the Isle of Wight, managed by the People's Trust for Endangered Species (PTES). It is a significant habitat for red squirrels, dormice, and various bird species, featuring a mix of oak, ash, and hazel.

Name: Bridestones, Crosscliff and Blakey Topping
Description: Bridestones, Crosscliff and Blakey Topping presents dramatic moorland in the North York Moors National Park. Wind and ice shaped the spectacular rock formations, including the Bride and Groom. The site features ancient woodland, heather moorland, and rich biodiversity, offering walking trails and scenic views. Managed by the National Trust.

Name: Bridgham Heath
Description: Bridgham Heath, a fragment of Breckland heathland in Norfolk, features dry acid grassland, heather, and small copses. It supports diverse insects, common lizards, and various bird species, actively managed for conservation.

Name: Brierdene LNR
Description: Brierdene LNR, also known as Brierdene Wildlife Site, is a coastal denemouth and designated Site of Nature Conservation Importance (SNCI) in Whitley Bay, North Tyneside. It encompasses woodland, grassland, and freshwater habitats, supporting diverse wildlife. The dene connects directly to the beach, offering varied coastal and woodland environments. It is actively managed by the Friends of Brierdene, with support from Northumberland Wildlife Trust.

Name: Brimham Rocks
Description: Brimham Rocks, a biological SSSI in North Yorkshire, features unique rock formations sculpted over 320 million years by natural erosion. This moorland landscape offers free access and supports diverse wildlife.

Name: Brinsley Headstocks
Description: Brinsley Headstocks is a 5.17-hectare Local Nature Reserve near Eastwood, Nottinghamshire. The site preserves former colliery structures and offers diverse habitats, including grassland and wetlands, supporting varied wildlife. It is managed for both heritage and biodiversity.

Name: Broad Colney Lakes
Description: Broad Colney Lakes is an 11 hectare nature reserve previously managed by Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust in London Colney in Hertfordshire.  It has recently been sold to an anonymous buyer but reports in The Herts Advertiser says "the selected buyer has stated that the site will continue to be used for fishing, with the woodland managed for the benefit of wildlife.

Name: Broadham Down
Description: Broadham Down is a 16-hectare nature reserve east of Chilham and west of Canterbury in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Broadstreet, Backside and Rydes Commons
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 158 hectares.

Name: Broadwater Lake
Description: Mid Colne Valley is a 132 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Harefield in the London Borough of Hillingdon and Denham in South Buckinghamshire.  Its main importance lies in its extensive diversity of birdlife in lakes in former gravel pits.

Name: Broaks Wood
Description: Broaks Wood is a mature ancient woodland in Essex, featuring hornbeam, ash, and oak trees, and notably a unique Giant Redwood Grove. It contains an ancient stream, medieval fishpond remains, and seasonal ponds. Wildflowers like wood anemone, bluebell, and ramsons thrive here, and it is managed by Forestry England with conservation as a priority.

Name: Brockham Limeworks
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 45 hectares.

Name: Brockhampton Estate
Description: Brockhampton Estate is a medieval manor house and estate set in a secluded valley near Bringsty, Herefordshire. The property features ancient orchards, woodlands, and a working farm. Visitors can explore the timber-framed house, a moat, and 1,000 acres of parkland.

Name: Brockholes (nature reserve)
Description: Brockholes is a nature reserve near Preston, Lancashire, England, just off Junction 31 of the M6 motorway.  It is owned by the Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside.

Name: Brockholes Nature Reserve
Description: Brockholes is a nature reserve near Preston, Lancashire, England, just off Junction 31 of the M6 motorway.  It is owned by the Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside.

Name: Brodsworth Community Woodland
Description: Brodsworth Community Woodland is a former colliery site in South Yorkshire. TCV supports its management, with ongoing activities including path maintenance, tree planting, and coppicing. The woodland offers views across the Dearne Valley.

Name: Bromeswell Green
Description: Bromeswell Green is a 7.2-hectare nature reserve in Bromeswell, east of Woodbridge in Suffolk.

Name: Brompton Cemetery
Description: Brompton Cemetery is a Grade I listed garden cemetery established in 1840 in West London. It features over 20,000 monuments, including notable figures like Emmeline Pankhurst, and a diverse range of trees and wildlife. Managed by The Royal Parks, it is a site of special historic interest.

Name: Brooke House
Description: Brooke House in Ashbocking, north of Ipswich in Suffolk is the headquarters of the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.  The house was left to the trust by Mary Brooke.

Name: Brookes Nature Reserve
Description: Belcher's and Broadfield Woods is a 14.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between Halstead and Braintree in Essex.

Name: Brookheys Covert Nature Reserve
Description: Brookheys Covert Nature Reserve is a Site of Special Scientific Interest and nature reserve managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.  It is located at SJ 742 904 in Greater Manchester.

Name: Brookwood Lye
Description: Brookwood Lye is a 22-hectare nature reserve in Brookwood in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Brotheridge Green Nature Reserve
Description: Brotheridge Green Nature Reserve is a nature reserve of the Worcestershire Wildlife Trust at Brotheridge Green, about 2.5 miles west of Upton-upon-Severn, in Worcestershire, England.

Name: Brough Law
Description: Brough Law is a Cheviot grassland site within Northumberland National Park undergoing peatland restoration. Volunteers remove non-native conifers and plant sphagnum moss to restore natural habitat and biodiversity. This project enhances the peatland ecosystem.

Name: Broughton Down
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Broughton Down is a 45.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Broughton in Hampshire.

Name: Brown End Quarry
Description: Brown End Quarry is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust, near the village of Waterhouses in Staffordshire, England.  It is designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest, and a regionally important geological site.

Name: Brown's Folly
Description: Browne's Folly, or Brown's Folly, is a folly tower sitting within a 39.9 hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest near the English village of Bathford in Somerset, notified in 1974: the site itself is known as the Farleigh Down Stone Quarry and is managed as a nature reserve by the Avon Wildlife Trust.

Name: Brownsea Island
Description: Brownsea Island, a National Trust property in Poole Harbour, Dorset, is a red squirrel sanctuary and wildlife haven. It features diverse habitats, walking trails, and a lagoon. Access is by ferry, supporting its conservation efforts.

Name: Brownsham & Mouthmill
Description: Brownsham and Mouthmill, part of North Devon Coast AONB, feature ancient temperate rainforest and dramatic coastal cliffs. The area includes wildflower meadows and a hanging valley with a rock arch and waterfall. Brownsham Mill is a Grade II listed building.

Name: Brownstone and Mansands
Description: Brownstone and Mansands features dramatic cliffs and a shingle beach along the Devon coast. This National Trust managed area offers quiet coves and coastal path walks, rich in wildlife, located between Brownstone and Mansands, near Kingswear.

Name: BrueCREW River Restoration Bruton
Description: BrueCREW is a community group in Bruton, Somerset, focused on restoring, enhancing, and protecting the River Brue. They remove obstructions, create habitats, and manage invasive species to improve biodiversity for people and wildlife.

Name: Buckland Abbey & Tavy Valley
Description: Buckland Abbey is a historic 700-year-old abbey in the Tavy Valley, Devon, initially a Cistercian monastery. It later became home to Sir Richard Grenville and Sir Francis Drake. The site features gardens, orchards, and ancient woodlands.

Name: Buckland Park Lake
Description: Buckland Park Lake, a 50-acre site in Surrey, features a large spring-fed lake and diverse woodland, including Ancient Semi-Natural Woodland. Once a chalk quarry, it supports varied flora and fauna, offering birdwatching and walking trails.

Name: Bucklebury Common
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Bucklebury Common is an elevated common consisting of woodland with a few relatively small clearings in the English county of Berkshire, within the civil parish of Bucklebury centred 3 miles northeast of Thatcham and encircling the settled localities of Upper Bucklebury and Chapel Row.  It is one of the largest commons in Southern England covering 350 hectares.

Name: Budby South Forest
Description: Budby South Forest is a significant remnant of Sherwood Forest's ancient woodland. This RSPB reserve features open heathland, acid grassland, and mature trees, supporting species such as nightjars, woodlarks, and various heathland plants. Management focuses on restoring and maintaining diverse habitats.

Name: Bull Cross, The Frith And Juniper Hill
Description: Bull Cross, The Frith and Juniper Hill is a 42.33-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954.

Name: Bull's Wood
Description: Bull's Wood is a 12 hectare nature reserve east of Cockfield in Suffolk, England.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust, and is part of the Thorpe Morieux Woods Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Bumble Hole & Warrens Hall Local Nature Reserves
Description: Bumble Hole and Warrens Hall Local Nature Reserves sit at a historic canal junction in the West Midlands. The site features restored canals, diverse wildlife habitats, and walking trails, offering a valuable green space for nature enthusiasts.

Name: Burgess Field
Description: Burgess Field Nature Park is a nature reserve of approximately 30-35 hectares (74-75 acres) on Oxford's northern edge, located between Port Meadow and the railway line, close to the River Thames. It features open grassland, scrub, and mature trees. Habitats include rough open grassland, small copses, and a wildflower meadow, supporting diverse wildlife like birds, butterflies, and deer.

Name: Burham Down
Description: Burham Down is a 110-hectare nature reserve between Maidstone and Chatham in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Burham Marsh
Description: Burham Marsh nature reserve is an 11 hectare tidal Reed bed on the River Medway 5 miles northwest of Maidstone.  It is just east of Snodland but being on the east bank of the river it is accessed via Burham.

Name: Burner's Heath and Swallows Pond
Description: Burner's Heath and Swallows Pond is a 5-hectare nature reserve in Pirbright in Surrey.  It is owned by Surrey County Council and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Burnham Beeches
Description: Burnham Beeches is a National Nature Reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest in Buckinghamshire. Managed by the City of London Corporation, it features ancient woodland, heathland, and ponds, supporting diverse wildlife. It is popular for walking and nature observation.

Name: Burnhope Pond
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 14 hectares.

Name: Burntollet Wood
Description: Burntollet Wood spans a steep valley slope overlooking the River Faughan. Mature broadleaf trees dominate, supporting diverse wildlife. Walking trails lead through this ancient woodland, designated an Area of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Burton and Chingford Ponds
Description: Burton Park SSSI is a 57.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Pulborough in West Sussex.

Name: Burton Bradstock & Hive Beach
Description: Burton Bradstock is a National Trust site on the Jurassic Coast in Dorset, offering Hive Beach for swimming, fossil hunting, and rockpooling. The soft sandstone cliffs are part of the South West Coast Path and are subject to erosion. A café is available.

Name: Burwell Fen
Description: Burwell Fen is a significant expansion area of Wicken Fen, forming part of a 60-year vision to restore wetland habitats. Managed by the National Trust, it actively contributes to fenland landscape restoration and biodiversity near Burwell and Reach, Cambridgeshire.

Name: Bury Lodge Wetlands
Description: Bury Lodge Wetlands in Enfield is a restoration project led by Thames21, in partnership with Enfield Council. The wetlands were created to improve water quality in the Salmons Brook by intercepting and treating polluted surface water runoff from the A10 and surrounding urban areas. This also helps reduce flood risk and enhances biodiversity. Community volunteering events regularly support these ecological enhancements.

Name: Buscot and Coleshill Estates
Description: Buscot and Coleshill Estates encompass traditional villages, farmland, and historic properties in Oxfordshire. The National Trust manages this diverse landscape, offering visitors walking trails, gardens, and preserved rural heritage.

Name: Bushy Park - Water Gardens & Pheasantry
Description: Bushy Park's historic Water Gardens feature canals, ponds, and cascades, creating diverse habitats for birds and amphibians. The nearby Pheasantry area supports various ground-nesting birds and woodland species.

Name: Bushy Park SSSI
Description: Bushy Park is London's second largest Royal Park, covering 445 hectares. It features woodlands, formal gardens, and diverse wildlife, including free-roaming herds of deer. The park holds Site of Special Scientific Interest status.

Name: Butcher's Wood
Description: Butcher's Wood is a 7-hectare (17-acre) ancient semi-natural woodland at the northern extremity of the South Downs National Park in West Sussex. It is situated just outside of the village of Hassocks, between Burgess Hill to the north and Brighton to the south. The wood features diverse broadleaf trees and valuable ground flora, including extensive bluebells and wood anemones, and offers a network of permissive paths for visitors.

Name: Butterdon Wood
Description: Butterdon Wood is a 16-acre woodland in Moretonhampstead, Devon, serving as the outdoor base for Running Deer School. It provides a natural environment for specialist education, offering activities in traditional rural skills, bushcraft, conservation, and supporting young people with special educational needs.

Name: Cabilla and Redrice Woods
Description: Cabilla and Redrice Woods is a nature reserve of the Cornwall Wildlife Trust, about 3 miles east of Bodmin, in Cornwall, England.  It is an extensive area of mixed woodland.

Name: Cable Street Community Garden
Description: Cable Street Community Gardens provides green spaces in Tower Hamlets, East London, where residents grow food, enjoy nature, and connect. A network of garden sites host regular events and workshops, promoting biodiversity and community engagement for local residents.

Name: Cadishead and Little Woolden Moss
Description: Cadishead and Little Woolden Moss is a nature reserve of the Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside, an area of Chat Moss which is being restored to its former state of peatland.

Name: Caer Brân
Description: Caer Brân is an important multi-period hillfort site in west Cornwall, a Scheduled Monument, with archaeological remains from both the Bronze Age and Iron Age periods. Visible remnants of ring cairns and an unfinished Iron Age hillfort are within its ramparts. The site offers panoramic views and supports diverse flora and fauna, which Cornwall Heritage Trust works to protect.

Name: Caerlaverock NNR
Description: Caerlaverock NNR protects expansive saltmarsh and mudflats on the Solway Firth, a critical wintering ground for barnacle geese and other wildfowl. The site supports diverse coastal habitats, offering birdwatching and walking opportunities.

Name: Cairngorms Connect
Description: Cairngorms Connect is a partnership of land managers working across 600 square kilometres of the Cairngorms National Park in Scotland. The project focuses on restoring habitats, enhancing species, and improving ecological processes over a 200-year timescale.

Name: Calf of Man
Description: Calf of Man is a 2.50-square-kilometre island, off the southwest coast of the Isle of Man.

Name: Calke Abbey
Description: Calke Abbey, a National Trust property in Derbyshire, showcases a preserved country estate with a focus on natural decay. It features ancient oak trees, a deer park, walled gardens, and historic collections, offering insights into its unique past.

Name: Calshot Marshes
Description: Calshot Marshes, a coastal reserve in Hampshire, features saltmarsh, reedbed, and freshwater lagoons. It provides habitat for bird species. The site is managed to mitigate coastal squeeze and adapt to sea-level rise.

Name: Calvert Jubilee
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Calvert Jubilee is a 22 hectares nature reserve in Calvert near Steeple Claydon in Buckinghamshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Cambourne Nature Reserve
Description: Cambourne Nature Reserve is a 170-hectare site featuring woodlands, wetlands, and grasslands. Three large lakes and ponds support diverse wildlife, including birds, insects, and mammals. Managed by Wildlife BCN, the reserve provides walking trails and birdwatching.

Name: Cambus o'May
Description: Cambus o'May is an ancient Caledonian pinewood forest between Ballater and Dinnet, north of the River Dee. Restoration returns it to a natural state, rich in native Scots pine through non-native species removal. Waymarked trails are available.

Name: Camley Street Natural Park
Description: Camley Street Natural Park is an urban nature reserve in St Pancras in central London and within the London Borough of Camden.  It is a local nature reserve.

Name: Canna & Sanday
Description: Canna and Sanday are Inner Hebridean islands, a National Scenic Area owned by the National Trust for Scotland. They form a crofting community, known for birdlife, unique geology, and historical sites. Sanday connects by a bridge.

Name: Cannock Chase Forest
Description: Cannock Chase Forest offers a range of activities including walking, cycling, Go Ape, and a children's play area. Managed by Forestry England, it features diverse woodlands, open heathland, and heritage trails. The site provides various trails suitable for all ages and abilities.

Name: Cannop Ponds
Description: Cannop Ponds are two large ponds, just north of Parkend in the Forest of Dean, Gloucestershire, England.  The ponds, and surrounding area, are a popular tourist destination.

Name: Canons Park
Description: Canons Park in Harrow is a Green Flag award-winning park featuring formal gardens, woodlands, and a lake. It serves as a vital ecological corridor, linking local green spaces and supporting diverse wildlife. The park offers recreational opportunities for the community.

Name: Canvey Wick
Description: Canvey Wick is a unique brownfield site, renowned for its diverse invertebrate population, including rare bees and moths. It offers grassland and scrub habitats on former oil refinery land, now a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Canvey Wick
Description: Canvey Wick is a former oil refinery site on Canvey Island, Essex, now a nationally important nature reserve. Recognised for its biodiversity, it supports rare invertebrates, plants, grassland, scrub, and wetland habitats.

Name: Cape Cornwall
Description: Cape Cornwall is a prominent headland near St Just in Penwith, Cornwall, marking England's only cape. It is a former tin mine site offering coastal walks, wildlife viewing, and views of the Brisons rocks, where Atlantic currents divide.

Name: Captain's Wood
Description: Captain's Wood is a 62 hectare nature reserve in Sudbourne in Suffolk.  It is owned and managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Carding Mill Valley & The Long Mynd
Description: Carding Mill Valley, within the Shropshire Hills AONB, is managed by the National Trust. It features a deep valley with a stream, leading to the heather-clad Long Mynd moorland. The site offers walking trails, diverse wildlife, and panoramic views.

Name: Cardinham Woods
Description: Cardinham Woods, near Bodmin in Cornwall, provides walking and mountain biking trails. Visitors can explore historical features like a clapper bridge and charcoal platforms. Facilities include a cafe, cycle hire, and a children's play area within the woodland setting.

Name: Carlton and Oulton Marshes
Description: Carlton and Oulton Marshes is a 151 hectare nature reserve in Lowestoft in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Carmel National Nature Reserve
Description: Carmel National Nature Reserve, near Llandeilo in Carmarthenshire, features Britain's only turlough, a disappearing lake on limestone. It fills and empties seasonally, supporting rare plants like fen violet when dry and attracting wildfowl when full in winter.

Name: Carn Galver & Bosigran
Description: This rugged coastal area on the Penwith Peninsula features dramatic granite cliffs, ancient field systems, and prehistoric hut circles. Views of the Atlantic and Pendeen Lighthouse are prominent, exploring Cornish Mining World Heritage Site history.

Name: Carnewas & Bedruthan Steps
Description: Carnewas and Bedruthan Steps presents a dramatic Cornish coastline, featuring distinctive sea stacks and sandy beaches. Visitors explore clifftop paths, discovering diverse geology and wildlife, with access to the South West Coast Path. A shop and tea-room serve visitors.

Name: Carngafallt
Description: Carngafallt, a mid-Wales reserve, features ancient upland oakwood, moorland, and rush pastures. It supports breeding curlew, lapwing, and other wading birds. Red kites are common. The site is managed for wildlife, with walking trails.

Name: Carnmoney Hill
Description: Carnmoney Hill is a local nature reserve with ancient woodland, wildflower meadows, and open grassland. It offers panoramic views of Belfast Lough and is home to diverse wildlife, including red squirrels and long-eared owls. Managed for conservation and public access.

Name: Carsington Water
Description: Carsington Water is a reservoir, operated by Severn Trent Water, between Wirksworth and Kniveton in Derbyshire, England.  The reservoir takes water from the River Derwent at Ambergate during winter months, pumping up to the reservoir by 10.

Name: Cartmel Fell
Description: Cartmel Fell offers far-reaching views across the Lyth Valley and Morecambe Bay. This area, managed by the National Trust, includes ancient woodlands, pastures, and several historic farmsteads. Public footpaths allow access for walkers.

Name: Carvers Rocks
Description: Carvers Rocks is a Derbyshire nature reserve featuring diverse habitats: wet mire, acidic grassland, heathland, and woodland. It supports varied plants like heather, alongside birds such as tree pipit and woodcock. Invertebrates thrive in wet areas, with historic mine workings adding character.

Name: Cassiobury Park
Description: Cassiobury Park is the principal public park in Watford, Hertfordshire, in England.  It was created in 1909 from the purchase by Watford Borough Council of part of the estate of the Earls of Essex around Cassiobury House which was subsequently demolished in 1927.

Name: Cassiobury Park LNR
Description: Cassiobury Park Local Nature Reserve, managed by Watford Borough Council with the Wildlife Trust, offers diverse habitats including woodland, river, and grassland. It is home to various bird species and invertebrates, providing a valuable urban green space.

Name: Castern Wood
Description: Castern Wood is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is an ancient woodland, with scrub and grassland, on the eastern slopes of the Manifold Valley, about 1 mile south of Wetton, in Staffordshire, England.

Name: Castle Drogo
Description: Castle Drogo is the last castle built in England, completed in 1930. This granite structure overlooks the Teign Gorge, offering historical interiors and diverse collections. The estate features gardens, woodland walks, a shop and cafe.

Name: Castle Marshes
Description: Castle Marshes is a 71 hectare nature reserve west of Lowestoft in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Castle Ward
Description: Castle Ward Estate, in County Down, Northern Ireland, features an 18th-century mansion with contrasting Classical and Gothic architecture. Situated on Strangford Lough, its demesne includes gardens, woodlands, and coastal habitats.

Name: Caswell Wood
Description: Caswell Wood is a small ancient woodland in Wiltshire, dominated by mature ash, oak and hazel coppice. Explore the public footpath, which runs through the heart of the wood, connecting with local footpaths and bridleways.

Name: Catfield Fen
Description: Catfield Fen is a nationally and internationally important wetland site within the Broads SAC. Designated as an SSSI and Ramsar site, it is arguably the UK's most species-rich wetland. The site is a private reserve and not open to the public.

Name: Catherton Common
Description: Catherton Common is a nature reserve of the Shropshire Wildlife Trust, between Cleehill and Cleobury Mortimer in Shropshire, England.  It is heathland, designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Cattersty Gill Nature Reserve
Description: A local nature reserve.

Name: Cave Hill Country Park
Description: Cave Hill Country Park is an iconic green space in Belfast, Northern Ireland. It features walking trails, caves, and offers panoramic views over the city and Belfast Lough. The park is known for its biodiversity and historical significance, including Napoleon's Nose.

Name: Cawfields & the Whin Sill
Description: Cawfields Quarry, a Roman Wall site and Dark Sky Discovery location, sits near Haltwhistle. The Whin Sill, a prominent dolerite intrusion, forms a key geological ridge in Northumberland. Its unique basalt grasslands support specific flora, targeted for conservation by the Hadrian's Wall Wetlands project.

Name: Centenary Wood
Description: Centenary Wood in Grimethorpe, Barnsley, commemorates the WWI centenary, established in 2014. This developing broadleaf woodland features extensive paths for walking, supports local wildlife, and includes memorial sculptures and a vibrant wildflower meadow for visitors.

Name: Centre for Wildlife Gardening
Description: The Centre for Wildlife Gardening is a 0.22-hectare nature reserve and educational facility in Peckham in the London Borough of Southwark.

Name: Centre of the Earth
HostOrg: Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust
Description: The Centre of the Earth is a purpose-built environmental education centre in Birmingham, England, run by the Wildlife Trust for Birmingham and the Black Country.

Name: Chaceley Meadow SSSI
Description: Chaceley Meadow is a 1.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954 and renotified in 1993.

Name: Chafford Gorges Nature Park
Description: The Chafford Gorges Nature Park is a 200-acre nature reserve located in Chafford Hundred, England, and managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust.  It includes two Sites of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Chambers Farm Wood
Description: Chambers Farm Wood, Lincolnshire, combines ancient woodland and modern conifer forest. It offers diverse habitats, including ancient oak and lime, conifer plantations, and open spaces. The site provides waymarked walking trails and a butterfly garden, managed for timber, recreation, and biodiversity.

Name: Chancellor's Farm
Description: Chancellor's Farm is a 34.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest just north of Priddy in the Mendip Hills, Somerset, notified in 1984.

Name: Chappetts Copse
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Chappetts Copse is a 12-hectare nature reserve east of West Meon in Hampshire.  It is owned and managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Charlecote Park
Description: Charlecote Park is a Victorian country house near Wellesbourne, Warwickshire, featuring a historic deer park and landscaped gardens by the River Avon. Managed by the National Trust, it offers a tranquil setting for exploring grounds and observing diverse wildlife.

Name: Charley Woods
Description: Charley Woods is a 26.8 hectares nature reserve north of Copt Oak in Leicestershire.

Name: Charmouth & Westhay Cliff
Description: Charmouth and Westhay Cliff are part of the National Trust's Golden Cap Estate on the Jurassic Coast in West Dorset. This section features fossil-rich beaches and eroding cliffs, revealing significant geological history for visitors.

Name: Charnwood Lodge
Description: Charnwood Lodge is a 134.2-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Charnwood Forest, east of Coalville in Leicestershire.

Name: Chasewater Country Park
Description: Chasewater Country Park, located in Staffordshire, spans approximately 360 hectares (900 acres), including 90 hectares of water. It is designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) for its rare plants and invertebrates. The reservoir, originally built as a canal feeder, is the largest in the West Midlands and provides water for the Birmingham Canal Network. The park offers diverse habitats, watersports, walking, and a heritage railway.

Name: Chawridge Bank
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Chawridge Bourne is a 9.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Berkshire, England Part of the site is a 5-hectare nature reserve called Chawridge Bank, which is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Cheddar Complex
Description: The Cheddar Complex is a 441.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Cheddar around the Cheddar Gorge and north east to Charterhouse in the Mendip Hills, Somerset, England, notified in 1952.

Name: Cheddar Gorge (National Trust)
Description: Walk among ancient trees, see incredible views and spot wildlife from the top of Cheddar Gorge. The National Trust manages the upper parts of the Gorge, offering trails and diverse habitats.

Name: Cheddar Wood
Description: Cheddar Wood is an 86.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest at Cheddar in the Mendip Hills, Somerset, England, notified in 1967.

Name: Chedworth Nature Reserve
Description: Chedworth Nature Reserve is a 6-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.  The site is listed in the 'Cotswold District' Local Plan 2001-2011 as a Key Wildlife Site.

Name: Cherry Hinton Chalk Pits
Description: Cherry Hinton Chalk Pits, a Cambridgeshire SSSI managed by Wildlife BCN, features grassland, scrub, and woodland. The site supports diverse plant and insect species, and is known for rare orchids and butterfly populations.

Name: Cherryburn
Description: Cherryburn, in Northumberland, is the birthplace of artist Thomas Bewick. This traditional cottage and farmyard features a small museum showcasing Bewick's wood engravings, a print room, and heritage gardens. It offers insight into rural 18th-century life.

Name: Chessel Bay
Description: Chessel Bay Local Nature Reserve on the River Itchen in Southampton is a vital high-tide roost for waders and wildfowl like curlew and shelduck. Its mudflats and saltmarsh habitats support diverse marine life. Public footpaths offer access.

Name: Cheviot Summit
Description: The Cheviot Summit site is part of a large-scale peatland restoration project within Northumberland National Park. This initiative aims to improve water quality, enhance biodiversity, and increase carbon storage in the upland peatlands.

Name: Chichester Harbour National Landscape
Description: Chichester Harbour National Landscape, a large natural harbour in Southern England, is a protected Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. The Chichester Harbour Conservancy manages the landscape, focusing on conservation, recreation, and planning within this cherished coastal area.

Name: Chiddingfold Forest
Description: Chiddingfold Forest is a large woodland on the Surrey/Sussex border, managed by Forestry England. It is a working forest producing timber sustainably. The site supports diverse wildlife, including wood white butterflies and nightjars. Visitors can enjoy walking, cycling, and horse riding trails.

Name: Chigborough Lakes
Description: Chigborough Lakes is an 18.6-hectare nature reserve in Maldon in Essex.

Name: Chimney Meadows
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Chimney Meadows is a 49.6-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between Abingdon-on-Thames and Faringdon in Oxfordshire.

Name: Chimswell Wood
Description: Chimswell Wood is a young broadleaf woodland, planted in November 1998 as part of the 'Woods on your Doorstep' project near Haverhill. It features a pond, open grassland, and a network of accessible paths, providing a local green space for walks.

Name: Chinbrook Meadows
Description: Chinbrook Meadows is a public park in the London Borough of Lewisham. It features newly created reedbeds as part of ongoing river restoration efforts within the Ravensbourne catchment. Thames21 collaborates with the local council on environmental projects, regularly hosting volunteering events for community participation.

Name: Chineham Wood
Description: Chineham Wood, an ancient woodland in Basingstoke, Hampshire, is managed by Chineham Parish Council. Designated as a Site of Importance for Nature Conservation (SINC), it features mature oak, ash, and hazel coppice, supporting diverse wildlife. Spring wildflowers, including bluebells and wild garlic, provide seasonal interest for quiet walks.

Name: Chinnor Hill
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Chinnor Hill is a 26.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Chinnor in Oxfordshire.

Name: Chinthurst Hill
Description: Chinthurst Hill is a 17.2-hectare Local Nature Reserve south of Guildford in Surrey.

Name: Chirk Castle
Description: Chirk Castle is a medieval Welsh border castle, built for Edward I. With over 700 years of continuous habitation, the estate features ancient parkland, formal gardens, and a Site of Special Scientific Interest woodland.

Name: Chislehurst Commons
HostOrg: The Trustees of Chislehurst and St Paul's Cray Commons
Description: Chislehurst and St Paul’s Cray Commons span 180 acres (73 hectares) in south-east London. Managed by Trustees under a 1888 Act of Parliament, the site features diverse habitats including woodland, grassland, and heathland. It supports varied wildlife like bats and adders. The charity relies on volunteers and donations to maintain the area for public enjoyment.

Name: Chitty's Common
Description: Chitty's Common is a 5-hectare nature reserve in Guildford in Surrey.  It is owned by Surrey County Council and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Chobham Common
Description: Chobham Common is a 655.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Chobham in Surrey.

Name: Cholsey Marsh
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Cholsey Marsh is a 19-hectare nature reserve near Cholsey in Oxfordshire, England.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Chopwell Colliery
Description: Chopwell Colliery was a coal mine situated at Chopwell, in Gateshead, Tyne and Wear.  The pit was first sunk in 1781, and was closed on 25 November 1966.

Name: Chopwell Meadows
Description: Chopwell Colliery was a coal mine situated at Chopwell, in Gateshead, Tyne and Wear.  The pit was first sunk in 1781, and was closed on 25 November 1966.

Name: Chopwell Wood
Description: Chopwell Wood is a 360-hectare woodland in Gateshead, Tyne and Wear, managed by Forestry England. It offers walking, cycling, and horse riding trails through a mix of conifers and broadleaves. The site supports diverse wildlife and provides educational and recreational opportunities.

Name: Christopher Cadbury Wetland Reserve
Description: The Christopher Cadbury Wetland Reserve is a nature reserve of the Worcestershire Wildlife Trust.  It is situated near Upton Warren, between Bromsgrove and Droitwich Spa in Worcestershire, England.

Name: Chudleigh Knighton Heath
Description: Chudleigh Knighton Heath, near Chudleigh Knighton, Devon, is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, so designated because of its rare lowland heath vegetation.  It is a habitat for many rare species including the ant, Formica exsecta.

Name: Chûn Castle
Description: Chûn Castle is a large Iron Age hillfort near Penzance in Cornwall, England, United Kingdom.  The fort was built about 2,500 years ago, and fell into disuse until the early centuries AD when it was possibly re-occupied to protect the nearby tin mines.

Name: Church Farm Marshes
Description: Church Farm Marshes is a 56 hectare nature reserve in Thorington in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Church Wood
Description: Church Wood is a large ancient woodland in Kent, forming part of the Blean Complex. It features mature sweet chestnut coppice and oak standards, providing habitat for rare heath fritillary butterflies, various bird species, and diverse flora. Public footpaths allow access.

Name: Churchtown Farm
Description: Churchtown Farm is a community nature reserve one mile south of Saltash, Cornwall, England.  It is leased from Antony Estate and managed by Cornwall Wildlife Trust, and includes diverse habitats such as grassland, estuarine mudflats, wetland, woodland, disused quarries and hedgerows.

Name: Clanger Wood
Description: Clanger Wood is an ancient woodland, once part of Selwood Forest, near Westbury, Wiltshire. It features diverse trees like oak, ash, and hazel, supporting wildlife including dormice. Public footpaths offer access for walkers.

Name: Clapgate Pits
Description: Clapgate Pits is a disused quarry near Broughton, Lincolnshire.  This 1.

Name: Clapton Moor
Description: Clapton Moor is a 40-hectare Avon Wildlife Trust nature reserve and part of the Gordano Valley, Clapton Moor, Middle Bridge and rhynes Site of Nature Conservation Interest in Somerset, England.  Clapton Moor is located in the Gordano Valley region of North Somerset.

Name: Claremont Landscape Garden
Description: Claremont Landscape Garden features a serpentine lake, grotto, and turf amphitheatre, showcasing one of the earliest surviving English landscape gardens. The historic design integrates mature trees and expansive lawns within its picturesque grounds, offering a significant example of garden evolution.

Name: Clarke's Pool Meadow SSSI
Description: Clarke's Pool Meadow is a 1.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1997.

Name: Clattinger Farm
Description: Clattinger Farm is a 60.3 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Wiltshire, notified in 1971.

Name: Clayton Vale
Description: Clayton Vale is an urban nature reserve within Manchester's Medlock Valley. It features mature woodlands, wildflower meadows, and river habitats. The site offers walking and cycling paths, providing a vital green space for wildlife and local community recreation.

Name: Cleaver Heath Nature Reserve
Description: Cleaver Heath Nature Reserve is a nature reserve in Heswall, on the Wirral Peninsula, managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.  It forms part of the Heswall Dales Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Cleethorpes Sands Local Nature Reserve
Description: Cleethorpes Sands Local Nature Reserve encompasses diverse coastal habitats including sand dunes, saltmarsh, and intertidal flats. Located on the Humber Estuary, it supports a rich array of bird species, particularly waders and waterfowl, making it a vital site for avian conservation.

Name: Clent Hills
Description: The Clent Hills offer far-reaching views across Worcestershire and beyond, providing a popular escape for walkers. This National Trust property features woodlands, parkland, and heathland habitats.

Name: Cley Hill
Description: Cley Hill, a prominent chalk hill in Wiltshire, offers panoramic views across the landscape. This Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) supports rare wildflowers and butterflies, and holds historical significance as a potential Iron Age hillfort.

Name: Cley Marshes
Description: Cley Marshes is a 176-hectare nature reserve on the North Sea coast of England just outside the village of Cley next the Sea, Norfolk.  A reserve since 1926, it is the oldest of the reserves belonging to the Norfolk Wildlife Trust, which is itself the oldest county Wildlife Trust in the United Kingdom.

Name: Clifton Country Park
Description: Clifton Country Park in Salford is a local nature reserve with woodlands, meadows, and lakes. Visitors enjoy walking, cycling, and horse riding trails. The park also features a children's play area, a cafe, and a local history museum at Clifton House.

Name: Cliveden Estate
Description: Cliveden Estate features 375 acres of formal gardens, woodlands, and Thames River frontage in Buckinghamshire. This historic site includes a grand stately home, various plant collections, a maze, and panoramic views of the surrounding landscape.

Name: Cloatley Manor Farm Meadows
Description: Cloatley Manor Farm Meadows is a 12.1 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Wiltshire, notified in 1997.

Name: Cloud Wood
Description: Breedon Cloud Wood and Quarry is a 63.3 hectares biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-east of Worthington in Leicestershire.

Name: Clout's Wood
Description: Clout's Wood is an 11.78 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Wiltshire, notified in 1951.

Name: Clovelly Coast & Gallantry Bower
Description: Clovelly Coast and Gallantry Bower features dramatic clifftop views over the Bristol Channel, part of the North Devon Coast Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. This area offers diverse coastal habitats and walking paths along a stunning stretch of the Devon coastline.

Name: Clowes Wood
Description: Clowes Wood is an ancient woodland, with a mix of broadleaf and coniferous trees located near Whitstable in Kent. It features oak, birch, and rowan, along with larch and pine. The reserve supports varied birdlife and ground flora, offering peaceful trails for visitors.

Name: Clowes Wood
Description: Clowes Wood is an ancient woodland and heathland in Warwickshire, part of the historic Forest of Arden. It features diverse habitats including oak and birch trees, offering walking opportunities near Packwood House.

Name: Clumber Park
Description: Clumber Park is a significant remnant of Sherwood Forest in Nottinghamshire, featuring extensive parkland, a serpentine lake, a walled kitchen garden, and an iconic chapel. Managed by the National Trust, it offers various walking and cycling routes amidst diverse landscapes.

Name: Clyde Valley Woodlands NNR
Description: The Clyde Valley Woodlands NNR comprises ancient woodlands along the steep river valleys of the Clyde, Avon, and Nethan. The site is important for diverse woodland plants, birds, and fungi, and contains numerous historical features for visitors to explore.

Name: Cockaynes Wood
Description: Cockaynes Wood is a 20.2-hectare nature reserve between Wivenhoe and Alresford in Essex, United Kingdom.

Name: Cockey Down
Description: Cockey Down is a 15.2 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Wiltshire, notified in 1971.

Name: Cockshoot Broad
Description: Cockshoot Broad is a 5-hectare nature reserve north-east of Norwich in Norfolk.  It is managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Coed y Bwl
HostOrg: Wildlife Trust of South and West Wales
Description: Coed y Bwl is a Site of Special Scientific Interest in Glamorgan, south Wales.  The site is managed by The Wildlife Trust of South and West Wales.

Name: Coed y Cerrig NNR
Description: Coed y Cerrig National Nature Reserve protects a wet valley woodland near Abergavenny, Gwent. Trails explore diverse habitats, including ancient woodland and fen areas, important for conservation. The reserve features rich ground flora and various fungi, offering opportunities to observe seasonal changes and wildlife.

Name: Coedydd Aber NNR
Description: Coedydd Aber National Nature Reserve is a steep-sided valley near Abergwyngregyn, Gwynedd, featuring ancient woodland and a spectacular waterfall. It supports diverse wildlife, including bats and dormice. Walking trails offer scenic views.

Name: Colekitchen Down
Description: Colekitchen Down is a 3-hectare nature reserve north of Gomshall in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Coleton Fishacre Garden & Coast
Description: Coleton Fishacre is an Art Deco country retreat near Kingswear, Devon, built in the 1920s. Its gardens feature exotic plants, streams, and woodland, leading to a private cove. The property offers coastal walks and views across the Froward Point.

Name: College Lake
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: College Lake is a 65 hectare nature reserve in a former chalk quarry in Pitstone in the Aylesbury Vale district of Buckinghamshire.  It is one of the flagship reserves of the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust, and it has an information centre, education facilities, a café, toilets and a shop.

Name: Colley Hill
Description: Colley Hill is a chalk grassland site on the North Downs in Surrey, offering panoramic views over the Weald. Managed by the National Trust, it features diverse flora and fauna, including rare orchids. Numerous walking trails and picnic spots are available for visitors.

Name: Colliers Wood
Description: Colliers Wood is a 14.5-hectare nature reserve in Moorgreen, Nottinghamshire, managed by Broxtowe Borough Council. Created on former colliery land, it features woodlands, ponds, and meadows, supporting wildlife and offering public paths.

Name: Collingwood
Description: Collingwood is a 3-hectare nature reserve south of Hawkhurst in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Collinpark Wood SSSI
Description: Collinpark Wood is a 66.69-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1966, revised in 1974 and renotified in 1983.

Name: Colne Estuary
Description: Colne Estuary is a 2915 hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Brightlingsea in Essex.  It is also a Nature Conservation Review site, a National Nature Reserve, a Ramsar wetland site of international importance, a Special Protection Area, a Special Area of Conservation, and a Geological Conservation Review site.

Name: Colne Point
Description: Colne Point is a 276.4-hectare nature reserve south-west of St Osyth in Essex.

Name: Combs Wood
Description: Combs Wood is a 15.1 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the southern outskirts of Stowmarket in Suffolk.

Name: Compton Castle Estate
Description: Compton Castle is a medieval fortified manor house near Paignton, Devon, home to the Gilbert family for nearly 600 years. This rare, surviving example of a medieval fortified manor is nestled within a sheltered valley. Visitors can explore the historic rooms and gardens, and the estate is actively involved in nature conservation projects, including planting over 10,000 trees to create new wooded habitats and improving areas of the countryside for nature.

Name: Conningbrook Lakes Country Park
Description: Conningbrook Lakes Country Park is a 34.3-hectare nature reserve in Kennington, Ashford in Kent.

Name: Contin Pine Marten Habitat
Description: Contin's woodlands are a confirmed pine marten habitat, evidenced by the 2022 survey. Visitors can explore various walking trails, including one providing access to the marten habitat. Facilities include a car park and accessible toilet.

Name: Conwy
Description: RSPB Conwy is an urban wetland nature reserve on the east bank of the River Conwy. It provides vital habitats for diverse bird species throughout the year, featuring reedbeds, lagoons, and saltmarsh. Visitor facilities and educational activities are available.

Name: Cooksbridge Meadow
Description: Cooksbridge Meadow is a 9-hectare nature reserve south of Fernhurst in Sussex.  It is managed by the Sussex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Coombe Hill
Description: Coombe Hill is the highest point in the Chilterns with far-reaching views across the Aylesbury Vale. The site features the Boer War memorial and is home to a variety of chalk grassland wildflowers and butterflies. Managed by the National Trust.

Name: Coombe Hill Canal
Description: Coombe Hill Canal lies in the Vale of Gloucester, south west England, north of Leigh and runs west 2.75 miles from Coombe Hill Basin to the River Severn near Wainlode Hill.

Name: Coombes Valley
Description: RSPB Coombes Valley is a woodland nature reserve in a quiet Staffordshire valley. It features ancient woodlands, meadows, and streams, providing habitat for diverse wildlife, including breeding pied flycatchers and redstarts. Visitors can explore waymarked trails and observe nature.

Name: Copinsay
Description: Copinsay is an RSPB reserve, a small island east of Orkney, known for its significant seabird colonies including puffins, guillemots, razorbills, and kittiwakes. The island is also home to a lighthouse and a diverse range of plant life.

Name: Copperas Wood
Description: Copperas Wood is a 13.8-hectare nature reserve between Ramsey and Wrabness in Essex.

Name: Copt Hall
Description: Copt Hall Marshes is an extensive area of coastal grazing marsh, bordering the Blackwater Estuary in Essex. The reserve supports a range of breeding and overwintering wildfowl and waders. Ditches and ponds provide habitat for amphibians and dragonflies.

Name: Copythorne Common
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Copythorne Common is a 17-hectare nature reserve west of Southampton in Hampshire.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Corehead & The Devil's Beef Tub
Description: Corehead, near Moffat, is a 600-hectare site in the Devil's Beef Tub, southern Scotland. Borders Forest Trust manages this land for native woodland restoration and peatland conservation, aiming to enhance biodiversity and ecological processes.

Name: Corfe Barrows Nature Park
Description: Corfe Barrows Nature Park comprises around nine natural areas, covering an area of 90 hectares, within the Borough of Poole that are being managed for the benefit of wildlife and people.  It was designated as a nature park in June 2016.

Name: Cornard Mere
Description: Cornard Mere is an 8.5-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Little Cornard in Suffolk.

Name: Cornmill Meadows Dragonfly Sanctuary
Description: Cornmill Meadows Dragonfly Sanctuary is a vital mosaic of wetland habitats within Lee Valley Regional Park. Over 20 species of dragonflies and damselflies thrive here. Boardwalks and trails provide access for wildlife observation, enhancing local biodiversity.

Name: Corrieshalloch Gorge NNR
Description: Corrieshalloch Gorge National Nature Reserve, near Ullapool, features a dramatic deep canyon carved by the River Droma over thousands of years. A Victorian suspension bridge offers views of the 45m Falls of Measach. Ancient woodland thrives on its steep sides.

Name: Corrimony
Description: Corrimony is an RSPB reserve located seven miles west of Drumnadrochit, near Loch Ness. It features native woodland, open moorland, and a loch, providing habitat for species such as black grouse, red kites, and red deer. An 8.5-mile waymarked trail is available for visitors.

Name: Cors Caron NNR
Description: Cors Caron National Nature Reserve is a vast raised bog in Ceredigion, West Wales. This ancient landscape hosts diverse wildlife, offering accessible boardwalks and a viewing hide. The Afon Teifi river meanders through the reserve.

Name: Cors Crymlyn
Description: Cors Crymlyn (also known as Crymlyn Bog) is a National Nature Reserve, Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), Special Area of Conservation (SAC), and Ramsar site, located near Swansea, South Wales. It is the largest lowland fen in Wales and one of the most important wetland sites in Europe, providing crucial habitat for various rare plants and invertebrates, including the fen raft spider.

Name: Cors Ddyga
Description: Cors Ddyga is an extensive low-lying wetland and working floodplain in Anglesey, Wales. Home to threatened wildlife like marsh harriers, bitterns, and otters. Restoration has created reedbeds, wet grassland, and fens, supporting a rich diversity of species.

Name: Cossington Meadows
Description: Cossington Meadows is an 88.9 hectares nature reserve west of Cossington in Leicestershire.

Name: Cotehele Estate
Description: Cotehele is a medieval house with terraced gardens, situated on the banks of the River Tamar in Cornwall. The estate includes a working mill, orchards, and extensive woodland walks, offering insights into Tudor life and craftsmanship.

Name: Coton Country Park
Description: Coton Country Park, 120 hectares west of Cambridge, offers footpaths and cycle routes through diverse habitats. Managed by Cambridge PPF for public access and wildlife, it features meadows, woodland, and ponds. It connects directly to the Coton footpath to Grantchester.

Name: Coton Reserve
Description: Coton Reserve is a 35-hectare site near Coton village, west of Cambridge. Managed by CambridgePPF, it transforms former arable land into wildflower meadows, woodland, and wetlands. This project provides vital green space for wildlife and public access.

Name: Cotswold Water Park
Description: The Cotswold Lakes is the United Kingdom's largest marl lake system, straddling the Wiltshire–Gloucestershire border, north-west of Cricklade and south of Cirencester.  There are 180 lakes, spread over 42 square miles.

Name: Cottage Farm
Description: Cottage Farm, Ulster Wildlife's first nature reserve, is a hidden gem located near Omagh along the River Strule. This diverse site features ancient woodland, bog, species-rich grassland, hedgerows, and ponds. Formerly a dairy farm, it is undergoing restoration, including the removal of invasive scrub and non-native plants from the bog, to enhance its vital habitats. The reserve supports a wide array of wildlife, including various birds, butterflies, moths, damselflies, and mammals such as badger, otter, and red squirrel, and is used for education and research.

Name: Cotterill Clough Nature Reserve
Description: Cotterill Clough is a 5.6-hectare nature reserve near Manchester Airport.

Name: Cotton Dell
Description: Cotton Dell is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is a wooded valley area near the village of Cotton and about 0.

Name: Coulsdon Common
Description: Coulsdon Common, a 130-acre site in Coulsdon, features woodlands and open grasslands. Managed by the City of London Corporation, it provides habitats for diverse wildlife. Visitors enjoy walking and nature observation. It is a registered common.

Name: Coulsdon Common
Description: Coulsdon Common is a 126-acre public open space in south London, part of the City of London Commons and the South London Downs National Nature Reserve. It features ancient woodland, grassland, and chalk grassland, supporting diverse wildlife like roe deer and orchids. Managed for conservation and public access, it offers walking, cycling, and horse riding.

Name: Coulters Dean
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Coulters Dean is a 2.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of Buriton in Hampshire.

Name: Cowden Pound Pastures
Description: Cowden Pound Pastures is a 5.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Cowden in Kent.

Name: Cragside
Description: The National Trust's Cragside estate in Northumberland is home to a diverse landscape, featuring lakes, waterfalls, and a historic Victorian house. It serves as a vital red squirrel sanctuary.

Name: Craig Cerrig Gleisiad a Fan Frynych NNR
Description: Craig Cerrig Gleisiad a Fan Frynych NNR is a mosaic of habitats in the Brecon Beacons. It features an impressive glacial cwm with a lake, rocky outcrops, and moorland. The reserve supports arctic-alpine plants and various bird species.

Name: Craigellachie NNR
Description: Craigellachie NNR, near Aviemore, is an upland nature reserve in the Cairngorms National Park. It features ancient woodland, heather moorland, and a lochan. The reserve supports diverse wildlife, including peregrine falcons, ospreys, and red squirrels.

Name: Cranham Marsh
Description: Cranham Marsh is an English 15.3 hectare Local Nature Reserve and a Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation in Cranham in the London Borough of Havering.

Name: Credenhill Park Wood
Description: Credenhill Park Wood is an Iron Age hill fort in Herefordshire. Managed by the Woodland Trust, this site features ancient trees, diverse wildlife, and offers extensive views across the surrounding landscape near Hereford.

Name: Cribb's Meadow
Description: Cribb's Meadow is a 4.2-hectare nature reserve east of Wymondham in Leicestershire.

Name: Cricklepit Mill
Description: Cricklepit Mill is a visitor centre of the Devon Wildlife Trust, located in Exeter, in Devon, England.  It is the headquarters of Devon Wildlife Trust, and one of two visitor centres of the Trust; the other is Wembury Marine Centre near Plymouth.

Name: Crimdon Dunes
Description: Crimdon Dunes is a significant dune system in County Durham, forming part of the Durham Coast Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and National Nature Reserve. It is known for its nationally and internationally important flora and fauna, including rare butterflies, orchids, and hosts the UK's most northerly breeding colony of little terns. The area is also notable for its unique geological features, being part of the Permian magnesian limestone system.

Name: Crinan Wood
Description: Crinan Wood is an ancient Atlantic oakwood on the banks of the Crinan Canal in Argyll and Bute, Scotland. It represents a prime example of this rare habitat, home to diverse flora, fauna, rare ferns, lichens, and mosses. The wood's unique ecosystem thrives in a mild, wet Atlantic-influenced climate.

Name: Croes Robert Wood
Description: Croes Robert Wood is a nature reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest, noted for its biological characteristics, in Monmouthshire, south east Wales.  Gwent Wildlife Trust, the owners of the site, manage the woodland through methods of coppicing and charcoal burning to encourage its notable flora and fauna.

Name: Croft Castle and Parkland
Description: Croft Castle and Parkland features a medieval castle, church, and gardens. The site includes ancient oak trees, an Iron Age hill fort, and an 18th-century walled garden, offering woodland trails and views of the Herefordshire landscape.

Name: Croft Pasture
Description: Croft Pasture is a 6.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the outskirts of Croft in Leicestershire.

Name: Crom Estate
Description: Crom Estate, situated on Upper Lough Erne in County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland, is a 2,000-acre conservation area. It features ancient woodlands, islands, and diverse wildlife, including pine martens and otters. Visitors explore historic ruins, nature trails, and bird hides. The estate is managed by the National Trust.

Name: Cromers Wood
Description: Cromers Wood is a 28-hectare nature reserve between Milstead and Sittingbourne in Kent.  It is managed by Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Crooksbury Common
Description: Crooksbury Common is a significant area of lowland heath and woodland in Surrey. It features ancient oak and pine trees, with heather and gorse covering open areas. The site is home to diverse wildlife, including reptiles and rare invertebrates. It serves as an important habitat for conservation efforts in the region.

Name: Crooksbury Hill
Description: Crooksbury Hill is a 17.2-hectare nature reserve within Puttenham and Crooksbury Commons east of Farnham in Surrey.

Name: Croome
Description: Croome is the first landscape designed by Lancelot ‘Capability’ Brown. The estate features miles of walks, architectural follies, and the historic RAF control tower. The parkland and garden are managed by the National Trust, with Croome Court by Croome Heritage Trust.

Name: Crossness Nature Reserve
Description: Crossness Nature Reserve is a 25.5-hectare local nature reserve in the London Borough of Bexley, adjacent to the historic Crossness Pumping Station. It is part of the Erith Marshes Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation and is one of the few remaining areas of grazing marsh in London, featuring the largest reedbeds in Bexley. The reserve provides a valuable habitat for a diverse array of wildlife, including water voles, rare invertebrates like the Shrill Carder bee, and numerous bird species. It is owned and managed by Thames Water.

Name: Crowsheath Wood
Description: Crowsheath Wood is an 8.1-hectare nature reserve in Downham, between Billericay and South Woodham Ferrers in Essex.

Name: Croxall Lakes
Description: Croxall Lakes is a nature reserve located between the villages of Croxall and Alrewas, Staffordshire, in the United Kingdom.  The nature reserve comprises two lakes and grassland between them.

Name: Crymlyn Bog NNR
Description: Crymlyn Bog is one of the largest areas of lowland bog in the UK, supporting a variety of wildlife including otters and rare invertebrates. The site is a National Nature Reserve and a Ramsar site, featuring diverse habitats from open water to fen woodland.

Name: CS Lewis Nature Reserve
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: CS Lewis Nature Reserve is a 3-hectare nature reserve in Risinghurst, a suburb of Oxford in Oxfordshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Cucknell's Wood
Description: Cucknell's Wood is a 11-hectare nature reserve south-east of Shamley Green in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Culloden Wood
Description: Culloden Wood offers walking routes through native woodland and plantations. Historically significant, it borders the famous Culloden battlefield and features ancient burial cairns. Visitors explore diverse flora and fauna here.

Name: Culpeper Community Garden
Description: Culpeper Community Garden is an award-winning Islington green space, offering individual plots and communal areas. It provides gardening opportunities for local people, run by volunteers. An oasis of peace, it is one of London's few successful community-managed open spaces.

Name: Culzean Country Park
Description: Extensive woodlands within Culzean Country Park offer diverse habitats. Visitors explore walking trails amongst mature trees, spotting local wildlife. The park features a blend of formal gardens, rugged coastline, and natural woodland areas.

Name: Cumbernauld
Description: Cumbernauld is a town in North Lanarkshire, Scotland.  It lies within the historic county of Dunbartonshire.

Name: Cutsdean Quarry
Description: Cutsdean Quarry is a 0.83-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire, England.

Name: Cwm Du Glen
Description: Cwm Du Glen is a designated Local Nature Reserve near Pontardawe, Glamorgan, managed by Neath Port Talbot Council. It features a deep glen with a stream, waterfalls, ancient woodland, and diverse flora and fauna, supporting oak, ash, hazel, and various bird species. It is also known as Cwm Du Glen and Glanrhyd Plantation.

Name: Cwm Idwal NNR
Description: Cwm Idwal is a glacial amphitheatre in Eryri (Snowdonia) National Park, Wales. It features the pristine Llyn Idwal and notable rock formations like the Devil's Kitchen. This National Nature Reserve is significant for its geology and rare arctic-alpine plant species.

Name: Cwm Ivy Marsh
Description: Cwm Ivy Marsh on the Gower Peninsula is a successful managed realignment scheme, transforming farmland into saltmarsh and freshwater habitats. It protects against coastal flooding, providing a haven for diverse wildlife like otters, birds, and insects.

Name: Daisy Nook Country Park
Description: Daisy Nook Country Park is a 96-acre site in Oldham and Tameside, featuring woodlands, waterways, and a canal. It offers river and canal walks, fishing, a cafe, and children's play areas, serving as a popular destination for local recreation and nature activities.

Name: Dalby Forest
Description: Dalby Forest, in the North York Moors, offers extensive walking and cycling trails, diverse wildlife habitats, and picnic facilities. This Forestry England site provides recreational opportunities and hosts events, contributing to woodland access and nature appreciation for visitors.

Name: Dalston Eastern Curve Garden
Description: Dalston Eastern Curve Garden is a vibrant community green space in East London, built on a disused railway line. It provides a peaceful urban oasis for relaxation, hosts diverse community events, and supports educational activities, operating as a non-profit project.

Name: Danbury Common
Description: Danbury Common is a 70.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Danbury in Essex, England.

Name: Danbury Commons and Blakes Wood
Description: Danbury Commons and Blakes Wood features ancient woodlands, heathland, and common land near Danbury, Essex. Visitors explore footpaths, discover diverse flora and fauna, and enjoy panoramic views.

Name: Danbury Ridge
Description: Danbury Ridge Nature Reserves are a group of nature reserves totalling 101 hectares near Danbury in Essex, England.  They are managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust, and most of them are in Sites of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Dancersend with Pavis Woods
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Dancersend is an 81.3-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Aston Clinton in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Danemead
Description: Danemead is a 5.6-hectare nature reserve west of Hoddesdon in Hertfordshire, managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Danes Moss Nature Reserve
Description: Danes Moss Nature Reserve is a 13.4-hectare nature reserve south of Macclesfield, Cheshire, England.

Name: Daneway Banks SSSI
Description: Daneway Banks is a 17-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954 and renotified in 1983.  It lies half a mile west of Sapperton and is part of a group of wildlife sites in the Frome Valley that includes Siccaridge Wood and Sapperton Canal reserves.

Name: Dark Peak Moorlands
Description: Kinder Scout is a vast, high moorland plateau in the Dark Peak, Peak District National Park. Managed by the National Trust, it features unique peat bogs, dramatic gritstone landscapes, and is crucial for blanket bog restoration. It offers extensive walking routes and significant wildlife habitats.

Name: Darland Banks
Description: Darland Banks is a 29.1-hectare Local Nature Reserve on the southern outskirts of Gillingham in Kent.

Name: Darnley Mausoleum and Woods
Description: Darnley Mausoleum and Woods is an ancient woodland reserve in Kent, home to the Grade I listed Darnley Mausoleum from the 1780s. Diverse trees like sweet chestnut, oak, and beech provide habitats. Paths allow exploration of wildlife, including rare invertebrates.

Name: Darsham Marshes
Description: Darsham Marshes is a 20 hectare nature reserve south of Darsham in Suffolk, England.  It is owned and managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Dawcombe
Description: Dawcombe is a 23-hectare nature reserve north-west of Reigate in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Dawlish Warren & Exe Estuary
Description: Dawlish Warren is a sand spit and nature reserve at the River Exe mouth in Devon. The Exe Estuary is a vital wetland ecosystem, supporting overwintering birds and diverse habitats. Both sites hold designations as SSSI and NNR.

Name: Daws Hall
Description: Daws Hall is a tranquil nature reserve and education centre near Lamarsh, Essex, managed by the Daws Hall Trust. It features diverse habitats including meadows, woodlands, and a stretch of the River Stour, supporting a variety of wildlife.

Name: Decoy Heath
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Decoy Pit, Pools and Woods is a 17.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Aldermaston in Berkshire.

Name: Dedham Vale & Stour Valley National Landscape - Haverhill Headwaters
Description: Dedham Vale and Stour Valley National Landscape, on the Essex-Suffolk border, features low-lying landscapes. The Haverhill Headwaters mark the Stour River's source, flowing through ancient woodlands, meadows, and arable land, supporting diverse habitats and species within this protected area.

Name: Deepdene Terrace
Description: Deepdene Terrace is a historical landscape and nature reserve in Dorking, Surrey. Owned by Mole Valley District Council, it features ornamental gardens, woodland, and an arboretum. Conservation and maintenance are carried out by the Friends of Deepdene, offering visitors a tranquil space for walks and nature observation.

Name: Deeping Lakes
Description: Deeping Lakes Nature Reserve, also known as Deeping Gravel Pits is a local nature reserve with an area of over 160 acres located south-east of Deeping St James in Lincolnshire, England.  It includes part of the Deeping Gravel Pits SSSI and is placed within a Higher Level Stewardship scheme.

Name: Deeping Lakes Nature Reserve
Description: Deeping Lakes Nature Reserve, also known as Deeping Gravel Pits is a local nature reserve with an area of over 160 acres located south-east of Deeping St James in Lincolnshire, England.  It includes part of the Deeping Gravel Pits SSSI and is placed within a Higher Level Stewardship scheme.

Name: Deer's Leap Wood
HostOrg: Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust
Description: Deer's Leap Wood is a nature reserve of the Wildlife Trust for Birmingham and the Black Country, in West Midlands, England.  There is woodland with a variety of tree species; also a pond and a meadow area.

Name: Delamere Forest
Description: Delamere Forest is Cheshire's largest woodland, offering diverse habitats and recreational activities. It provides walking, cycling, and adventure trails, supporting various wildlife. The forest features accessible routes for visitors.

Name: Denaby Ings
Description: Denaby Ings are a nature reserve on the River Dearne, encompassing an area of 23 hectares north of Denaby Main, Doncaster, South Yorkshire, near the town of Mexborough.  The Trans Pennine Trail passes here.

Name: Dene Park
Description: Dene Park is an ancient woodland reserve in Kent, featuring diverse tree species like hazel and hornbeam, and a rich ground flora including bluebells and wood anemones. The site includes a stream and pond, supporting varied wildlife habitats.

Name: Denham Lock Wood
Description: Denham Lock Wood is a 6.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest next to the Grand Union Canal, and near Denham in the London Borough of Hillingdon.

Name: Deptford Creek
Description: The Creekside Discovery Centre in Deptford manages a 0.5-hectare natural habitat and the intertidal area of Deptford Creek, a unique urban ecosystem and one of London's most biodiverse landscapes. It provides environmental education, guided walks, and programmes for schools and community groups, fostering connection with its rich freshwater and saltwater flora and fauna.

Name: Dering Wood
Description: Dering Wood is an ancient semi-natural woodland near Pluckley, Kent, covering approximately 125-147 hectares (308-310 acres). Managed by the Woodland Trust, it features diverse tree species like sessile oak, hornbeam, and sweet chestnut, supporting a variety of wildlife including nightingales, dormice, and notable butterfly species. The site is actively managed for conservation and public access, preserving its ecological and historic value.

Name: Derwent Gorge and Horsleyhope Ravine
Description: Derwent Gorge and Horsleyhope Ravine is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and part of the Derwent Gorge and Muggleswick Woods National Nature Reserve (NNR). It comprises ancient semi-natural woodlands along the River Derwent and its tributary, Horsleyhope Burn, near Consett. The site features steep-sided ravines and diverse flora, including dry acid sessile oak woods and lime-rich ash and wet alder woodlands, supporting rare plants and protected species. It is a vital area for wildlife conservation in County Durham and Northumberland.

Name: Dews Farm Sand Pits
Description: Dews Farm Sand Pits is a 1.2-hectare nature reserve near Harefield in the London Borough of Hillingdon.

Name: Dick Buck's Burrows
Description: Dick Buck's Burrows is a mature broadleaved woodland, dominated by oak, sweet chestnut, sycamore and beech, located two miles southwest of Cromer in Norfolk. The site features a waymarked path linking to the Weavers Way and offers public access. Managed by the Woodland Trust.

Name: Dickleburgh Moor
Description: Dickleburgh Moor is a fen habitat in Norfolk. It supports diverse flora including marsh orchids, bog pimpernel, and sundew. Management includes scrub clearance and water level control to maintain the wetland environment.

Name: Dimminsdale
Description: Dimminsdale is a 37 hectare geological and biological Site of Special Scientific Interest partly in Derbyshire and partly in Leicestershire.  It is located east of Calke in Derbyshire.

Name: Dinefwr
Description: Dinefwr is a National Nature Reserve encompassing an ancient park, medieval castle, and historic house near Llandeilo. It hosts a herd of rare White Park Cattle. Visitors can explore woodlands, wetlands, and open parkland, supporting diverse wildlife. The estate offers walking trails and tranquil natural beauty.

Name: Dingle Marshes
Description: Dingle Marshes is a 93-hectare wildlife reserve on the North Sea coast of the English county of Suffolk.  The reserve is located between Dunwich and Walberswick, approximately 4 miles south-west of Southwold.

Name: Dinnington Community Woodland
Description: Dinnington Community Woodland is a popular local park in Rotherham. TCV South Yorkshire manages the site for nature conservation and community benefit. It offers valuable green space for the local community and supports diverse wildlife habitats.

Name: Distillery Farm Meadows
Description: Distillery Farm Meadows is an 18.7 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Wiltshire, notified in 1988.

Name: Ditchling Beacon
Description: Ditchling Beacon is the highest point in East Sussex, England, with an elevation of 248 m.  It is south of Ditchling and to the north-east of Brighton.

Name: Ditchling Down
Description: Ditchling Down, part of South Downs National Park, East Sussex, features chalk grassland with expansive views across the Weald and towards the coast. It is home to diverse wildlife, including rare butterflies. Walking trails and paragliding areas are present, maintained by the National Trust.

Name: Divis & Black Mountain
Description: Divis and the Black Mountain is a vast upland site overlooking Belfast. It offers extensive walking trails, diverse habitats, and panoramic views across Northern Ireland. Home to varied wildlife, the site provides a rugged natural escape on the city's edge.

Name: Doe Lea
Description: Doe Lea Local Nature Reserve, 14 hectares of grassland and woodland, offers accessible paths, a circular walk, benches, and a bird hide. Once an opencast coal mine, the site supports significant biodiversity, recording over 30 bird species. Weekly volunteer tasks maintain the area.

Name: Dolebury Warren
Description: Dolebury Warren is a 90.6-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest and ancient monument near the villages of Churchill and Rowberrow in North Somerset, part of South West England.

Name: Dollar Glen
Description: Dollar Glen is a woodland glen and burn with steep slopes and diverse trees. Home to the 15th-century Castle Campbell, it features waterfalls along the fast-flowing Burn of Dollar. Footpaths offer stunning views of the Ochil Hills and access to the historic castle.

Name: Dollis Brook
