Description: Thames21 and partners restore Dollis Brook, a North London tributary of the River Brent. The project enhances natural river features, creates habitats, and reduces flood risk with sustainable drainage systems. Community engagement is key.

Name: Donna Nook National Nature Reserve
Description: Donna Nook is a point on the low-lying coast of north Lincolnshire, England, north of the village of North Somercotes and south of Grimsby.  The area, a salt marsh, is used by a number of Royal Air Force stations in Lincolnshire for bombing practice and shares its name with RAF Donna Nook.

Name: Dover's Hill
Description: Dover's Hill offers panoramic views across the Vale of Evesham, from the Malvern Hills to the Black Mountains. This National Trust site hosts the annual 'Cotswold Olimpick Games' and is a key part of the Cotswolds AONB.

Name: Dowdeswell Reservoir
Description: Dowdeswell Reservoir is in the parish of Dowdeswell in Gloucestershire.  The former water treatment works are in the parish of Charlton Kings.

Name: Downe Bank
Description: Downe Bank is a nature reserve owned and managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust in the North Downs, close to Downe in the London Borough of Bromley.  It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest together with the neighbouring High Elms Country Park.

Name: Downhill Demesne
Description: Downhill Demesne features a clifftop walk with views of the Causeway Coast and Mussenden Temple. The historic estate includes gardens and woodland. The site offers exploration of its natural and architectural heritage, alongside wildlife observation opportunities within its coastal environment.

Name: Downs Banks
Description: Downs Banks is a scenic area of ancient woodland and heathland in Staffordshire, offering walking trails and wildlife habitats. Managed by the National Trust, it provides a tranquil escape near Stone with varied flora and fauna.

Name: Doxey Marshes
Description: Doxey Marshes is a 150 hectares nature reserve located within two miles of Stafford town centre, and is managed by Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  Designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest for its wet grassland habitat and its breeding wading birds and wildfowl, it is particularly noted for its populations of breeding snipe.

Name: Draycott Sleights
Description: Draycott Sleights is a 61.95 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest at Draycott in the Mendip Hills, Somerset, England, notified in 1987.

Name: Droitwich Canals Reedbed Restoration
Description: The Droitwich Canals, restored in 2010, connect the Worcester & Birmingham Canal with the River Severn. A vital wildlife corridor, it supports otters, kingfishers, and dragonflies. Ongoing conservation efforts, particularly at the 5.5-hectare Coney Meadow reedbed nature reserve, maintain and enhance its crucial reedbed and wetland habitats.

Name: Drovers Estate
Description: Drovers Estate features ancient woodlands, downland, and arable fields in Sussex. It supports over 100 lichen species, rare butterflies, and several bat species like serotine and brown long-eared bats. Visitors can enjoy woodland trails and views across the Sussex Weald.

Name: Drumnaph Wood
HostOrg: Woodland Trust and Carntogher Community Association
Description: Drumnaph Wood is a significant ancient native woodland, forming part of the larger Drumnaph Community Nature Reserve near Maghera, County Londonderry. Situated at the gateway to the Sperrin Hills, it features diverse habitats including ancient woodland, newly planted woodland, wildflower meadows, wetlands, and bog. The reserve supports a rich variety of flora and fauna, including diverse tree species, ground flora, and various bird and mammal populations, and is known for its bluebells in spring and butterflies in summer.

Name: Dry Sandford Pit
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Dry Sandford Pit is a 4.2-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-west of Abingdon-on-Thames in Oxfordshire.

Name: Dryhill
Description: Dryhill Local Nature Reserve, near Sundridge in Kent, is a former ragstone quarry now reclaimed by nature. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and the first geological Local Nature Reserve in Kent, known for its exceptional rock formations and fossils. The reserve features acidic grassland and heathland, supporting rare plants, invertebrates, and reptiles, with sheep grazing helping to maintain these habitats. Elevated, it offers panoramic views.

Name: Duck Gutter
Description: Duck Gutter Nature Reserve in South Yorkshire is a wet grassland and fen habitat. It supports diverse plants such as water violets and marsh orchids, and breeding wading birds like snipe and redshank. The reserve features open water, ditches, and reedbeds, managed to maintain its wetland ecosystem.

Name: Duckpool & Sandymouth Bay
Description: Sandymouth Bay and nearby Duckpool are National Trust sites on the North Cornwall coast. The bay features a pebble ridge, extensive sand, and rock pools at low tide. Popular for surfing and walks along the South West Coast Path. A café and facilities are available during peak seasons.

Name: Dudley No. 2 Canal Windmill End
Description: The Dudley No. 2 Canal, managed by the Canal & River Trust, is part of the Birmingham Canal Navigations. At Windmill End, it meets the Netherton Tunnel Branch Canal and is adjacent to Bumble Hole Nature Reserve. This area is a tranquil haven with grassland, ponds, wildflowers, and birds, offering opportunities for walking, cycling, and wildlife spotting. It also features historic industrial remnants like Cobbs Engine House.

Name: Dudmaston Estate
Description: Dudmaston Estate offers Comer Woods, a popular area for walking and cycling trails. The wider estate features an 18th-century hall, historic gardens, and extensive parkland. Visitors can explore diverse art and natural history collections.

Name: Duffield Frith
Description: Duffield Frith comprises ancient royal forest remnants across Derbyshire, historically encompassing Kedleston Estate. The area, once a vast hunting ground, now features fragmented woodlands and parkland, preserving glimpses of its medieval past. It reflects diverse land management.

Name: Dulwich Upper Wood
Description: Dulwich Upper Wood is a Local Nature Reserve in South London, one of four remnants of the Great North Wood. Managed by TCV, it features ancient woodland with oak, hornbeam, and ash, supporting diverse wildlife. The site offers a tranquil escape, promoting biodiversity.

Name: Duncliffe Wood
Description: Duncliffe Wood is an ancient woodland spanning over 92 hectares near Shaftesbury, Dorset. It offers diverse broadleaf habitats and open glades on a prominent hilltop. Managed by the Woodland Trust, the site provides marked trails for visitors to explore, supporting local wildlife populations and offering panoramic views.

Name: Dundreggan Rewilding Centre
Description: Dundreggan Rewilding Centre, near Loch Ness, offers an immersive experience into rewilding. It features a tree nursery and accessible trail, showcasing efforts to restore Scotland's wild forest and biodiversity. The centre opened in 2023.

Name: Dunham Massey
Description: Dunham Massey is an ancient deer park, historic house, and garden located in Altrincham, Greater Manchester. It features a herd of fallow deer, a winter garden, and a grand Edwardian house. The estate offers accessible routes and seasonal attractions.

Name: Dunkeld - The Hermitage
Description: The Hermitage is a picturesque woodland garden near Dunkeld, Perthshire, featuring towering Douglas firs, scenic walks, and Ossian's Hall overlooking the Black Linn Falls. Part of Tay Forest Park, it offers accessible trails along the River Braan.

Name: Dunkery & Horner Wood
Description: Dunkery & Horner Wood, a National Nature Reserve on Exmoor, is part of the Holnicote Estate. It features ancient oak woodlands, including Horner Wood, and Dunkery Beacon, Exmoor's highest point. The site supports diverse wildlife.

Name: Dunnerdale Fells, Duddon Valley
Description: Dunnerdale Fells, within the Duddon Valley in the Lake District National Park, features ancient woodlands and high fells. The River Duddon flows through this secluded landscape, supporting diverse wildlife. The area offers various walking opportunities.

Name: Dunnet Head
Description: Dunnet Head is mainland Great Britain's most northerly point, offering panoramic coastal views. Its cliffs and heathland host puffins, guillemots, razorbills, and kittiwakes. Marine wildlife like seals and dolphins are often seen. It is a vital seabird breeding ground.

Name: Dunollie Wood
Description: Dunollie Wood is an ancient woodland situated on a hillside overlooking Oban Bay, offering views towards Mull and Lismore. This small, historically significant site features mature oak trees and diverse ground flora including bluebells. The Woodland Trust manages it for conservation and public access.

Name: Dunsdon National Nature Reserve
Description: Dunsdon National Nature Reserve is a nature reserve of the Devon Wildlife Trust, near Dunsdon and about 3.5 miles north-west of Holsworthy, in Devon, England.

Name: Dunstable Downs and Whipsnade Estate
Description: Dunstable Downs and Whipsnade Estate features rolling chalk grassland with extensive views over the Vale of Aylesbury. Located within the Chilterns Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, it supports diverse wildlife and is a popular destination for walking and kite flying.

Name: Dunwich Forest
Description: Dunwich Forest is an area of forest and lowland heath around 1 mile north-west of the village of Dunwich in the English county of Suffolk.  The forest covers an area of approximately 9 square kilometres and was originally planted by the Forestry Commission.

Name: Dunwich Heath and Beach
Description: Dunwich Heath and Beach is a Suffolk coastal site managed by the National Trust. It features lowland heath, shingle beach, and offers diverse habitats for rare plants and birds such as woodlarks and nightjars. Visitors can explore walking trails.

Name: Dutton Park Farm Nature Reserve
Description: Dutton Park Farm Nature Reserve is an 18-hectare nature reserve northwest of Weaverham, Cheshire, England.  It is managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Dyfi Osprey Project
Description: The Dyfi Osprey Project is a conservation project at the Cors Dyfi nature reserve near Derwenlas, in the county of Powys, Wales, under the management of the Montgomeryshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Dyfi: Ynyslas NNR
Description: Ynyslas National Nature Reserve, within the Dyfi Biosphere, features a diverse landscape of dunes, saltmarsh, peatland, and estuary. The Nature Hub serves as a visitor centre, providing information, refreshments, and essential facilities for exploring this significant natural area.

Name: Dymock Woods SSSI
Description: Dymock Woods is a 53-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1990.  The site is listed in the 'Forest of Dean Local Plan Review' as a Key Wildlife Site.

Name: Dyrham Park
Description: Dyrham Park is a 17th-century baroque house, garden, and ancient deer park near Bath. The estate covers 270 acres, featuring parkland and a formal garden against the Cotswold Edge. A herd of fallow deer inhabits the park.

Name: Eaglehead and Bloodstone Copses
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Eaglehead and Bloodstone Copses is a 10.3-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest which is south of Ashey on the Isle of Wight.

Name: Eames Farm Thorney Island Wetland
Description: Eames Farm is a 132.5-hectare Local Nature Reserve on Thorney Island within Chichester Harbour National Landscape (AONB). It is owned by Chichester Harbour Conservancy, West Sussex County Council, and the Ministry of Defence, and managed by Chichester Harbour Conservancy. It protects saltmarsh, mudflats, reedbeds, and grazing marsh, forming an internationally important wetland and organic farm. The site supports diverse bird species, rare plants like Grass-poly, and insects. It is part of the Chichester and Langstone Harbours Ramsar site and Special Protection Area. The site is private land with no public access, though public footpaths exist around Thorney Island.

Name: Eartham Woods
Description: Eartham Woods, within the South Downs National Park, offers extensive trails for walking, cycling, and horse riding. Managed by Forestry England, this ancient woodland features diverse tree species, including impressive mature beech stands, and is recognised for its rich wildlife and archaeological interest.

Name: East Blean Wood
Description: East Blean Woods is a 151.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Herne Bay in Kent.

Name: East Ham Nature Reserve
Description: East Ham Nature Reserve is a former graveyard transformed into a Local Nature Reserve in the London Borough of Newham. Newham Green Gym volunteers maintain diverse habitats, including woodland, wildflower meadows, and ponds, supporting local wildlife.

Name: East Riddlesden Hall
Description: East Riddlesden Hall is a 17th-century manor house with a barn, gardens, and a lake, nestled in the Aire Valley. The site includes a children's play area, cafe, and shop, offering year-round activities and events in West Yorkshire.

Name: East Town Park
Description: East Town Park in Haverhill spans 50 acres of meadows and woodlands, featuring diverse wildlife habitats, nature trails, and conservation areas. It holds Green Flag status and offers an easy access trail, a five-kilometre railway walk, and osier beds. Visitors can observe various wildlife, including snowdrops, yellow aconites, lizards, damselflies, frogs, toads, butterflies, and dragonflies. The park also includes a children's play area, skate park, cafe, and WCs.

Name: East Village Waterglades
Description: East Village Waterglades in Stratford, London, is a vital green space within a residential area. TCV volunteers manage these wetland habitats, ensuring they remain biodiverse and accessible. The site supports various plant species and provides a home for diverse urban wildlife.

Name: East Winch Common
Description: East Winch Common is a 26.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of King's Lynn in Norfolk, England.

Name: East Wood, Tidenham
Description: East Wood and is a 0.82-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire, England.

Name: East Wretham Heath
Description: East Wretham Heath is a 141.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of Thetford in Norfolk, England.

Name: Eastbrookend Country Park
HostOrg: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
Description: Eastbrookend Country Park in Dagenham spans 76.1 hectares (188 acres). It is a Local Nature Reserve and a Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation, featuring diverse habitats including open grassland, woodlands, marsh, and lakes, supporting a wide variety of wildlife. The park offers walking trails, a café, and a children's play area, and connects to The Chase Nature Reserve.

Name: Eastwood Nature Reserve
Description: Eastwood Nature Reserve is a 4.7-hectare nature reserve in Stalybridge, Tameside, England.

Name: Eaves Wood
Description: Eaves Wood is an ancient semi-natural woodland in Silverdale, featuring limestone grassland and diverse habitats. Managed by the National Trust, it supports a rich array of wildflowers, butterflies, and birds, contributing to local biodiversity.

Name: Ebbor Gorge
Description: Ebbor Gorge is a dry limestone gorge and National Nature Reserve within the Mendip Hills National Landscape. Managed by Natural England, it features ancient woodland, walking trails, and diverse wildlife. The site is noted for its geological formations and prehistoric archaeological interest.

Name: Ebernoe Common
Description: Ebernoe Common is a 233.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Ebernoe, north of Petworth in West Sussex.

Name: Eday
Description: Eday is one of the larger North Isles of Orkney, a low-lying island with a rich natural and historical heritage. The RSPB reserve covers the north-west part of the island, including the cliffs of Red Head, a nationally important seabird colony.

Name: Eddleston Water Project
Description: The Eddleston Water Project is a long-term initiative restoring the river's natural function, mitigating flood risk, and enhancing biodiversity in the Eddleston catchment. It uses nature-based solutions like tree planting, pond creation, and meander restoration to tackle climate change impacts.

Name: Edgbaston Reservoir
Description: Edgbaston Reservoir is a large urban water body in Birmingham, West Midlands. Managed by the Canal & River Trust, it serves as a vital canal feeder and a significant habitat for diverse wildlife. The reservoir provides a green oasis and recreational space within the city.

Name: Edgehills Bog
Description: Edgehills Bog is a 0.66-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire in the Forest of Dean.

Name: Edmondsley Wood
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 13 hectares.

Name: Elan Valley
Description: The Elan Valley in Mid Wales is a key site for the Celtic Rainforests LIFE project. Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water manages this estate, leading efforts to restore precious Atlantic woodlands. The area offers opportunities for both volunteering and fundraising.

Name: Elland Gravel Pits
Description: Elland Gravel Pits is a Yorkshire Wildlife Trust nature reserve. This former quarry site is now a haven for wildlife, featuring open water, reedbeds, scrub, and woodland. It supports various bird species, dragonflies, and amphibians.

Name: Elstead Group of Commons
Description: Elstead Group of Commons is a 180-hectare nature reserve east of Elstead in Surrey.  It is composed of Royal, Elstead and Ockley Commons, which are owned by the Ministry of Defence and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust, and Bagmoor Common, which is owned and managed by the Trust.

Name: Elvaston Castle Country Park
Description: Elvaston Castle Country Park is home to Elvaston Castle, a gothic revival masterpiece (not open to the public) set within approximately 321 acres of parkland and formal gardens. Opened in 1970, it was England's first country park, offering nature trails, a children's play area, and hosting various events. It is managed by Derbyshire County Council.

Name: Emer Bog and Baddesley Common
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Emer Bog and Baddesley Common is a 50-hectare nature reserve north of North Baddesley in Hampshire.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Emmett Hill Meadows
Description: Emmett Hill Meadows is a 5.1 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Wiltshire, notified in 1987.

Name: Epping Forest
Description: Epping Forest is London's largest open space, stretching 12 miles from East London to Epping in Essex. It is a unique remnant of an ancient forest, a Site of Special Scientific Interest, and a Special Area of Conservation, containing over 50,000 ancient trees.

Name: Erddig
Description: Erddig, near Wrexham, features over 1,200 acres of parkland, ancient woodlands, and riverside walks. This historic estate provides habitats for diverse wildlife among centuries-old trees, actively conserving its natural and historical landscape.

Name: Eridge Rocks
Description: Eridge Green is a 8.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-east of Crowborough in East Sussex.

Name: Esher Common
Description: Esher Common is a large open common in Surrey, featuring diverse habitats including extensive heathland, ancient woodland, and acid grassland. Ponds and wet areas support varied birdlife, reptiles, and butterflies. The site is managed for conservation and public enjoyment.

Name: Eskdale Foothills
Description: Eskdale, located in the western Lake District, is a valley shaped by glaciers and water, home to ancient woodlands, traditional farms, and rare wildlife. The National Trust manages land here, working with farmers on sustainable grazing and conservation projects.

Name: Etherow Country Park
Description: Etherow Country Park, one of England's first country parks, sits on the Peak District's edge. Established in 1968, it features extensive open woodland, two reservoirs, and the River Etherow. Visitors can enjoy fishing, sailing, and a children's play area.

Name: Everdon Stubbs
Description: Everdon Stubbs is an ancient woodland, known for its extensive bluebell displays in spring. The reserve features diverse mature trees and ground flora. It supports a variety of woodland birds and invertebrates.

Name: Eyebrook Reservoir SSSI
Description: Eyebrook Reservoir is a critical site for wildlife, particularly waterbirds. Designated as a Site of Special Scientific Scientific Interest (SSSI), it supports significant populations of wildfowl and waders throughout the year. The reservoir is owned by Tata Steel UK and primarily operates as a trout fishery, with public viewing available from footpaths along its perimeter.

Name: Fackenden Down
Description: Fackenden Down is a 14-hectare nature reserve north of Sevenoaks in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Fairburn Ings
Description: Fairburn Ings, a former opencast coal mine near Castleford, West Yorkshire, is now a thriving wetland habitat. It attracts diverse birdlife, including avocets and kingfishers. The reserve features visitor trails, hides, and an accessible visitor centre for year-round nature observation.

Name: Fairlands Valley Park
Description: Fairlands Valley Park in Stevenage, Hertfordshire, is a large recreational area featuring lakes for watersports and fishing. The park includes a splash park, adventure play areas, walking routes, and a cafe, providing diverse activities for visitors. It serves as a vital green space for both leisure and local wildlife.

Name: Fairmile Common
Description: Fairmile Common is a diverse mosaic of acid grassland, heathland, woodland, and scrub in Surrey. It provides habitats for ground-nesting birds, invertebrates, and reptiles. Managed by Surrey Wildlife Trust, it is part of a larger network of interconnected wildlife sites.

Name: Falls of Clyde (Scotland)
Description: The Falls of Clyde are a series of linns or waterfalls on the River Clyde, near Lanark, Scotland.  They are renowned for their beauty and have frequently been painted by artists.

Name: Falls of Clyde (waterfalls)
Description: The Falls of Clyde are a series of linns or waterfalls on the River Clyde, near Lanark, Scotland.  They are renowned for their beauty and have frequently been painted by artists.

Name: Falstone Forest
Description: Falstone Forest is a key part of Kielder Forest Park in Northumberland's North Tyne Valley. Managed by Forestry England, this extensive conifer forest provides numerous walking and cycling trails. It supports timber production, offers habitats for diverse wildlife, and welcomes visitors year-round.

Name: Fames Rough
Description: Fames Rough is a 23-hectare nature reserve south-west of Chipstead in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust and is part of the Chipstead Downs Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Far Ings National Nature Reserve
Description: Far Ings national nature reserve is an area of over 90 ha on the southern shore of the Humber Estuary in North Lincolnshire, England.  It is immediately west of the town of Barton-upon-Humber and the village of Barton Waterside.

Name: Farlington Marshes
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Farlington Marshes is a 119.7-hectare Local Nature Reserve near Portsmouth in Hampshire.

Name: Farncombe Wood
Description: Farncombe Wood is a 1-hectare nature reserve in Farncombe in Surrey.  It is owned and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Farningham Wood
HostOrg: Sevenoaks District Council and Farningham Parish Council
Description: Farningham Wood is a 68-hectare (168-acre) ancient woodland and biological Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Kent, jointly owned and managed by Sevenoaks District Council and Farningham Parish Council. Designated as a Local Nature Reserve in 1987, it features diverse tree species, including oak, ash, and hornbeam, and is home to rare plants such as the Small-Leaved Lime and the nationally rare Deptford Pink. Public footpaths allow access for walking and nature observation, with a car park located at the end of Calfstock Lane.

Name: Farthing Downs
Description: Farthing Downs, a chalk grassland and ancient woodland site, stretches 3km across Greater London and Surrey. Popular for walking and horse riding, it offers views across the North Downs and is a Site of Special Scientific Interest for its rare chalk grassland plants.

Name: Fedian
Description: Fedian is a 12.5-hectare nature reserve in County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland. It features species-rich wet grassland and rush pasture, with an area of deciduous woodland. The site supports notable birdlife and various wildflowers, including several orchid species.

Name: Felbrigg Hall
Description: Felbrigg Hall is a 17th-century country house in Norfolk, East Anglia. Its 520-acre estate features a walled garden, lake, and the 'Great Wood', offering various waymarked walks. The estate provides a habitat for diverse local wildlife.

Name: Fell Foot
Description: Fell Foot is a Victorian park on the southern shore of Windermere, offering lake access for paddleboarding and wild swimming, plus family-friendly facilities, a cafe, and boat hire. It features formal gardens and open spaces ideal for picnics and recreation.

Name: Fen Drayton Lakes
Description: Fen Drayton Lakes is an RSPB nature reserve in Cambridgeshire, a network of lakes, meadows, and wetlands within the Great Ouse valley. Formerly a sand and gravel quarry, it is now an important habitat for a huge variety of wildlife, including overwintering wildfowl, wading birds, otters, dragonflies, and common terns. Reedbeds support warblers and bearded tits.

Name: Fens Pools Nature Reserve
Description: Fens Pools Nature Reserve, part of the larger Buckpool and Fens Pool Local Nature Reserve, is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in the West Midlands. It comprises three main pools (Grove, Middle, and Fens Pool) originally constructed by the Stourbridge Canal Company as reservoirs. The reserve is renowned for its diverse habitats, including open water, swamps, fens, and grasslands, supporting a significant population of great crested newts, amphibians, and various bird and insect species. It is situated between Pensnett and Brierley Hill.

Name: Fermyn Woods Country Park
Description: Fermyn Woods Country Park is a Green Flag award-winning park in Northamptonshire, near Brigstock. It features woodland and meadows, walking trails, cycling routes, a play area, and a cafe. Managed by Fermyn Wood Trust and North Northamptonshire Council.

Name: Filsham Reedbed
Description: Filsham Reedbed is an 18.5-hectare Local Nature Reserve on the western outskirts of St Leonards-on-Sea in East Sussex.

Name: Finch Foundry
Description: Finch Foundry in Sticklepath, Devon, is England's last working water-powered forge. It showcases traditional tool-making with water-driven hammers and grinding wheels. Visitors can explore historic workshops and learn about rural industrial heritage on the Dartmoor edge.

Name: Findhorn Hinterland
Description: Findhorn Hinterland Trust manages land, woods, dunes, and wetlands near Findhorn, Moray, Scotland. It restores biodiversity and connects people with nature through education and land-based skills. The Trust promotes conservation and community engagement within the local environment.

Name: Finemere Wood
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Finemere Wood is a 45.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Quainton in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Fineshade Wood
Description: Fineshade Wood offers extensive walking and cycling trails within a large ancient woodland in Northamptonshire. Features include a play area, café, and Gruffalo trail. It is home to a thriving red kite population and forms part of the wider Rockingham Forest.

Name: Fineshade Wood
Description: Fineshade Wood is a woodland managed by Forestry England, offering a range of recreational activities. Its visitor hub, Top Lodge, provides a café, toilets, and accessible paths for walking, cycling, and horse riding. The wood also features play areas and a Go Ape treetop adventure course.

Name: Fingle Woods
HostOrg: The Woodland Trust and National Trust
Description: Fingle Woods is an extensive ancient woodland in the Teign Valley, Dartmoor National Park, Devon. Jointly managed by the Woodland Trust and the National Trust, it is one of the UK's largest woodland restoration projects. It features diverse habitats including ancient oak, wet woodland, the River Teign, and open heathland, and is managed to restore native broadleaf trees and temperate rainforest.

Name: Fingringhoe Wick
Description: Fingringhoe Wick is a 48.6-hectare nature reserve in Fingringhoe in Essex.

Name: Fir and Pond Woods
Description: Fir and Pond Woods is a 29 hectare nature reserve in Potters Bar in Hertfordshire.  It is managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Fir Tree Copse
Description: Fir Tree Copse is a 6-hectare nature reserve south-east of Dunsfold in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust and is part of the Chiddingfold Forest Site of Special Scientific Interest This is oak and ash woodland, with hazel coppice.

Name: Firs Farm Wetlands
Description: Firs Farm Wetlands, in Winchmore Hill, Enfield, transformed an under-used playing field into an award-winning wetland. It provides a vital wildlife habitat, natural flood defence, and a community space. Regular volunteer days connect people with the river.

Name: Fivehead Arable Fields
Description: Fivehead Arable Fields is a 10.3 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near the village of Fivehead in Somerset, notified in 1990.

Name: Flamborough Head
Description: Flamborough Head is a promontory, 8 miles long on the Yorkshire coast of England, between the Filey and Bridlington bays of the North Sea.  It is a chalk headland, with sheer white cliffs.

Name: Flanders Moss NNR
Description: Flanders Moss is a raised bog, a rare habitat in Europe. It provides a home for a wide range of plants and animals. Boardwalks and a viewing tower allow visitors to explore the moss and observe wildlife. It is an internationally important site for nature conservation.

Name: Flatford
Description: Flatford, located within Suffolk's Dedham Vale, is a historic hamlet celebrated for its ties to painter John Constable. Flatford Mill and Willy Lott's House, subjects of his famous art, sit by the River Stour. The National Trust manages this site, offering scenic walks and an exhibition.

Name: Flatford
Description: Flatford, within Dedham Vale AONB, is famous for painter John Constable. Visitors explore 18th-century Flatford Mill, Willy Lott's House, and Bridge Cottage by the River Stour. Picturesque walks offer views of the iconic landscape.

Name: Flatropers Wood
Description: Flatropers Wood is a 38-hectare nature reserve in Rye in East Sussex.  It is managed by the Sussex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Flexford
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Flexford Nature Reserve is a 18-hectare nature reserve in Chandler's Ford in Hampshire.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Florence Court
Description: Florence Court in County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland, is a National Trust property featuring a large 18th-century house and demesne. The estate includes a walled garden, parkland, and ancient woodlands with walking trails. It hosts diverse flora and fauna, offering insights into historic landscape management.

Name: Fobbing Marsh
Description: Fobbing Marsh is a 75.7-hectare nature reserve east of Fobbing in Essex.

Name: Folkestone Warren
Description: Folkestone Warren is a geological SSSI within the Kent Downs AONB, managed by White Cliffs Countryside Partnership. This significant coastal landslip habitat features cliffs, boulder fields, and rare species, attracting walkers and naturalists. It is home to unique invertebrates, plants, and lichens.

Name: Folly Farm, Somerset
Description: Folly Farm is a traditionally managed working farm and nature reserve run by the Avon Wildlife Trust.  It is located between Stowey, Clutton and Stanton Wick in the civil parish of Stowey in the English county of Somerset.

Name: Fontmell Down
Description: Fontmell Down is a significant chalk downland in Dorset, offering steep slopes and views across the Blackmore Vale. It is rich in wildflowers and butterflies during summer, and home to various bird species. Managed for conservation, it represents an important grassland habitat.

Name: Foreland Point & Countisbury
Description: Foreland Point & Countisbury is a wildlife-rich headland on Exmoor National Park’s coast. Visitors can explore dramatic cliffs, enjoy coastal walks, and observe diverse flora and fauna. The area offers stunning views across the Bristol Channel.

Name: Formonthills
Description: Formonthills features a diverse woodland, integrating mature and younger trees with open grasslands. A network of paths provides public access. The site offers views over the Firth of Forth and is actively managed for wildlife conservation and recreation.

Name: Forsinard Flows
Description: Forsinard Flows is a vast blanket bog in the north of Scotland, home to rare plants, insects, and breeding birds like red-throated divers and golden plovers. It features trails, an observation tower, and a 'flows lookout' viewing point.

Name: Forsinard Flows
Description: Forsinard Flows, a major RSPB reserve in Caithness and Sutherland, forms part of the Flow Country UNESCO candidate site. This vast blanket bog is a vital European wilderness, supporting unique wildlife like waders. Its peatlands store significant carbon.

Name: Forth River Ecological Corridor
Description: The Forth River Ecological Corridor is a West Belfast regeneration project. It enhances natural habitats, promotes biodiversity, and develops a community pathway along the river. Environmental initiatives offer training and volunteering for local residents.

Name: Forty Hall Estate
Description: Forty Hall Estate in Enfield, London, is a historic estate featuring significant ancient woodland, a medieval fishing lake, and an organic farm. It serves as a crucial green space, supporting diverse habitats and biodiversity within the borough, and is managed by the London Borough of Enfield.

Name: Forvie NNR
Description: Forvie NNR features dynamic shifting sands and a significant dune system along the Scottish coast. It hosts Britain's largest eider duck breeding colony and an internationally important grey seal colony. The reserve is home to various seabirds and provides a wild coastal landscape.

Name: Fountains Abbey and Studley Royal Water Garden
Description: Fountains Abbey and Studley Royal is a World Heritage Site in North Yorkshire. It features the ruins of a Cistercian monastery, an 18th-century water garden, and a medieval deer park. Over 800 acres of diverse landscape for visitors to explore.

Name: Fowlsheugh
Description: Fowlsheugh is a clifftop nature reserve south of Stonehaven, Aberdeenshire. It supports thousands of breeding seabirds including kittiwakes, guillemots, razorbills, and puffins. Fulmars and shags also nest here, offering spectacular cliff views.

Name: Fox Covert
Description: Fox Covert is a 2.9-hectare nature reserve near Royston in North Hertfordshire.

Name: Fox Fritillary Meadow
Description: Fox Fritillary Meadow is a 2.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Framsden in Suffolk.

Name: Fox Hagg
HostOrg: Wildlife Trust for Sheffield and Rotherham
Description: Fox Hagg is a small) nature reserve in the Rivelin Valley area of Sheffield, England.  The Allen Sike flows along the north edge of the reserve and the River Rivelin flows through the reserve from Rivelin Dams to the west.

Name: Foxburrow Farm
Description: Foxburrow Farm is a 67 hectare nature reserve north of Melton in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Foxcote Reservoir
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Foxcote Reservoir and Wood is a 48.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between Akeley and Maids Moreton in Buckinghamshire, England.

Name: Foxearth Meadows
Description: Foxearth Meadows is an 11-acre (approximately 4.45-hectare) nature reserve located on the River Stour floodplain, in a quiet corner of Essex on the border with Suffolk. It is owned and managed by A Rocha UK. The site features a variety of habitats including river and riverbank, wetlands, woodland, ancient hedgerows, ponds, and marshy flower-rich grassland. It is particularly noted for its importance to dragonflies and damselflies, with 21 species recorded, and also supports other wildlife such as otter, kingfisher, harvest mouse, common lizard, and grass snake.

Name: Foxes Bridge Bog
Description: Foxes Bridge Bog is a 5.3-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: Foxholes
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Bould Wood is a 58.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Shipton-under-Wychwood in Oxfordshire.

Name: Foxley Wood
Description: Foxley Wood is a nature reserve in Foxley, Norfolk, England, the largest ancient woodland and coppice in Norfolk.  The Norfolk Wildlife Trust, which manages this reserve, bought it in 1998.

Name: Frampton Marsh
Description: Frampton Marsh is a nature reserve in Lincolnshire, England.  The reserve is situated on the coast of The Wash, 4 miles from the town of Boston, between the outfalls of the Rivers Welland and Witham, and near the village of Frampton in an area known as the “Fosdyke Wash”.

Name: Fraser Down
Description: Fraser Down is a 10-hectare nature reserve north of Betchworth in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Frays Farm Meadows
Description: Frays Farm Meadows is a 28.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Denham in the London Borough of Hillingdon.

Name: Freiston Shore
Description: Freiston Shore is an RSPB nature reserve on the Lincolnshire coast. It comprises lagoons, saltmarsh, and intertidal mudflats, providing crucial habitats for wading birds like avocets and redshanks, and supporting migratory species. Visitors can explore walking trails and use bird hides.

Name: Frensham Common
Description: Frensham Common is a large Surrey heathland covering approximately 400 hectares, featuring woodland, bogs, and two ponds (Great and Little). It is designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), Special Protection Area (SPA), and Special Area of Conservation (SAC). The site supports a wealth of rare wildlife, including sand lizards, smooth snakes, Dartford warblers, nightjars, woodlarks, and unusual plants like the insectivorous sundew. It offers opportunities for walking, cycling, birdwatching, and swimming at Frensham Great Pond.

Name: Frensham Little Pond
Description: Frensham Little Pond, a medieval fish pond and heathland in Surrey, provides a vital habitat for diverse wildlife. Accessible paths lead through woodland and open heath, offering opportunities for walking and nature observation. The site is managed for conservation.

Name: Friar's Crag
Description: Friar's Crag is a prominent rocky promontory on the eastern shore of Derwent Water, near Keswick. It provides panoramic views across the lake towards Cat Bells and the Borrowdale valley. The site is a popular walking destination within the Lake District National Park.

Name: Friar's Goose
Description: Wicken Fen, Britain's oldest nature reserve, expands into areas like Friar's Goose in the Cambridgeshire Fens. It's a crucial wetland habitat supporting diverse wildlife. The National Trust actively works to restore and enlarge this vital landscape.

Name: Friston Forest
Description: Friston Forest in the South Downs National Park, East Sussex, is Sussex's largest ancient woodland. It offers trails for walking, cycling, and horse riding. The forest includes a visitor centre, picnic area, play trail, and supports diverse wildlife.

Name: Frogmore Meadow
Description: Frogmore Meadows is a 4.6-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Hertfordshire and Buckinghamshire, north of the village of Chenies.

Name: Frome Banks
Description: Frome Banks is a 1.3-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: Fryent Country Park
Description: Fryent Country Park, located in Kingsbury, North West London, covers 103 hectares (254 acres). This extensive green space is a designated Local Nature Reserve and a Site of Importance for Nature Conservation, managed primarily for wildlife. It features a diverse mix of uncultivated hay meadows (some with Soil Association Organic Standard), ancient woodlands, hedgerows, and ponds, supporting over 800 species of wildlife. The park offers extensive views across London, particularly from Barn Hill.

Name: Fylde Sand Dunes Project
Description: The Fylde Sand Dunes Project is a partnership project to improve the dunes on the coast of the Fylde as a sea defence, conserve the coastal environment, and improve public awareness of the dunes.  The project is a partnership between the Lancashire Wildlife Trust, Fylde Council and Blackpool Council, and is funded by the Environment Agency until 2027.

Name: Gailey Reservoirs
Description: Gailey Reservoirs are two linked bodies of water by the Shropshire Union Canal near Gailey. The site is a popular destination for birdwatchers, known for its significant populations of winter wildfowl, gulls, and various wader species.

Name: Gait Barrows NNR
Description: Gait Barrows National Nature Reserve protects extensive limestone pavement, ancient woodland, and mires in Lancashire. It supports rare plants and insects, including the high brown fritillary butterfly. Management focuses on grazing and woodland restoration.

Name: Gaps Hill
Description: Duddas Wood is a broadleaved woodland in Derrington, Staffordshire, created and planted by the local community. It offers excellent views of Stafford Castle and features public access with walking paths. The wood is also located on the Sustrans national cycleway.

Name: Geilston Garden & Wood
Description: Geilston Garden is a tranquil riverside garden in Argyll, West Scotland, featuring an ancient walled garden, a herbaceous border, and a large kitchen garden.

Name: Gelt Woods
Description: Gelt Woods is an ancient woodland ravine in Cumbria, known for its diverse flora and fauna. The River Gelt carves through the sandstone, creating unique habitats. Part of the area is managed as an RSPB nature reserve, supporting ancient trees, wildflowers, and various bird species. It also features a remarkable Roman quarry, where stone was extracted for Hadrian's Wall.

Name: George Henry Wood
Description: George Henry Wood is a recently established woodland in Rutland, managed by the Woodland Trust. It was planted over four years from 2007, made possible by the legacy of George Henry Sellars, and offers a new habitat for local wildlife.

Name: George's Hayes
Description: George's Hayes is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is an ancient woodland, about a mile south-west of the village of Longdon, between Rugeley and Lichfield in Staffordshire, England.

Name: Gernon Bushes
Description: Gernon Bushes is a 32 hectare nature reserve north-east of Epping in Essex, England, which is managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust.  It is part of the Epping Forest Site of Special Scientific Interest and Nature Conservation Review site.

Name: Giant's Causeway & Causeway Coast NNR
Description: The Giant's Causeway is a UNESCO World Heritage Site on Northern Ireland's Antrim coast. It features around 40,000 interlocking basalt columns, formed by ancient volcanic activity. A national nature reserve, it offers dramatic coastal landscapes.

Name: Gibraltar Point National Nature Reserve
Description: Gibraltar Point is a headland on the coast of Lincolnshire, England, 3.5 miles south of Skegness, where the North Sea coast turns southwest towards Boston and enters The Wash.

Name: Gibside
Description: Gibside, a National Trust property near Rowlands Gill, Tyne and Wear, features an 18th-century landscape garden, a chapel, and parkland. The Nature Recovery Trail highlights ongoing conservation work, protecting diverse habitats and wildlife within this historic Georgian estate.

Name: Gibson Mill
Description: Gibson Mill, nestled within Hardcastle Crags near Hebden Bridge, is a fully off-grid 19th-century cotton mill. It generates its own electricity via hydroelectricity and solar panels, processes its own waste, and provides visitor facilities. The site demonstrates sustainable living principles.

Name: Gillham Wood
Description: Gillham Wood is a 3-hectare nature reserve west of Bexhill-on-Sea in East Sussex.  It is managed by the Sussex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Gillingham Royal Forest
Description: Stour Meadows is a Local Nature Reserve in Gillingham, Dorset, managed by Dorset Council. It comprises riverside meadows along the River Stour, providing habitats for diverse wildlife and offering opportunities for walking and enjoying nature.

Name: Gisburn Forest
Description: Gisburn Forest and Stocks reservoir, located in the Forest of Bowland AONB, is a diverse site in north east Lancashire. It offers mountain biking, walking trails, horse riding, and orienteering, and is a notable habitat for red squirrels.

Name: Glasswater Wood
Description: Glasswater Wood is a broadleaf woodland near Crossgar in County Down, Northern Ireland. Originally planted in 2000, it has been expanded and now covers almost 10 hectares (24 acres). The site features walking trails and is popular with local walkers.

Name: Glen Auldyn
Description: Glen Auldyn is a narrow valley about 6 kilometres long on the Isle of Man, with a river of the same name.  This flows in a NNE direction and flows into the River Sulby not far from its estuary, near Ramsey.

Name: Glen Finglas
Description: Glen Finglas is a Highland estate within Loch Lomond & The Trossachs National Park, part of the Great Trossachs Forest National Nature Reserve. It features ancient woodlands, heathland, and open ground, managed for conservation and public access. The site protects significant habitats and species.

Name: Glen Roy NNR
Description: Glen Roy National Nature Reserve in the Scottish Highlands is renowned for its 'Parallel Roads', a unique geological feature. These three distinct shorelines were formed by an ancient ice-dammed loch, providing a clear record of glacial lake levels and processes.

Name: Glenarm
Description: Glenarm Nature Reserve protects ancient woodland and a salmon river near Glenarm village. The site features steep slopes with oak and ash trees. Spring sees carpets of bluebells and wild garlic. Red squirrels and otters are present, reflecting its biodiversity.

Name: Glenborrodale
Description: Glenborrodale RSPB reserve lies on the Ardnamurchan peninsula, featuring ancient oak woodlands and coastal habitats. The site overlooks Loch Sunart and supports golden eagles, white-tailed eagles, red deer, and otters. Walking trails are accessible.

Name: Glenbrook Wetlands
Description: Glenbrook Wetlands is a new wetland in Glenbrook Park, Enfield, created by Thames21 as part of the "Restoring Enfield's Rivers" project. It involved de-culverting and re-naturalising the Glenbrook, enhancing local amenity and providing flood attenuation benefits.

Name: Glencoe NNR
Description: Glencoe is a stunning glacial glen and National Nature Reserve in the Scottish Highlands. Managed by the National Trust for Scotland, it is a popular destination for hikers and climbers, offering diverse trails, wildlife, and a rich history.

Name: Glencoyne Park
Description: Glencoyne Park, near Ullswater in the Lake District, showcases nature-friendly farming practices. It demonstrates how food production and nature recovery thrive, protecting fell and valley bottom habitats while supporting local wildlife.

Name: Glendun Nature Reserve
Description: Glendun (John McSparran Memorial Farm) is a traditional hill farm in the spectacular Glens of Antrim, managed by Ulster Wildlife. It aims to demonstrate the benefits of farming for nature. The 80-hectare reserve features diverse habitats including peatlands, species-rich grasslands, scrub, mixed ash woodland, rough moorland, and blanket bog, supporting a variety of wildlife such as red grouse, emperor moth, small heath butterflies, otters, red squirrels, and Irish hares.

Name: Glendurgan Wooded Valley
Description: Glendurgan Garden, a National Trust property in Cornwall, features a renowned cherry laurel maze, giant rhubarb plants, and a scenic three-valley descent to Durgan beach on the Helford River. It showcases diverse sub-tropical flora.

Name: Glenfeshie Estate
Description: Glenfeshie Estate spans over 44,000 acres in the Scottish Highlands, actively engaged in ecological restoration and rewilding. It restores native woodlands and supports diverse wildlife populations through ongoing conservation and research efforts.

Name: Glentress
Description: Glentress, near Peebles, is a 7stanes mountain biking centre within Tweed Valley Forest Park. It offers walking trails, a cafe, bike hire, and Go Ape. This site provides diverse outdoor activities for visitors.

Name: Glory Wood and Devil's Den
Description: Glory Wood and Devil's Den is a 13-hectare nature reserve south-east of Dorking in Surrey. It is an area of semi-natural woodland on sandstone hills, featuring diverse tree species like oak and sweet chestnut. The site supports various mammals including bats, roe deer, badgers, and foxes, and offers views over the North and South Downs.

Name: Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust
Description: The Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust is the Gloucestershire local partner in a conservation network of 46 Wildlife Trusts.  The Wildlife Trusts are local charities with the specific aim of protecting the United Kingdom's natural heritage.

Name: Glyme Valley
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Glyme Valley is a 28.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Chipping Norton in Oxfordshire.

Name: Gobions Wood
Description: Gobions Wood is a 36 hectare nature reserve managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust in Brookmans Park in Hertfordshire.  The site was formerly owned by the Gobions Woodland Trust, a registered charity which was closed down in 2013 because it had ceased to exist.

Name: Goblin Combe
Description: Goblin Combe is a dry valley in North Somerset which stretches for approximately 3½ km from Redhill, near Bristol International Airport on the A38, through to Cleeve on the A370.  The combe is located at, and is a 52-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest originally notified in 1999, with 9 hectares being managed as a nature reserve by the Avon Wildlife Trust.

Name: Goddards
Description: Goddards in York is a Grade I listed Arts and Crafts garden, originally designed by George Dillistone for the Terry family. It features herbaceous borders, a tennis court, a pond, and fruit trees, maintained with wildlife in mind. The garden supports local biodiversity.

Name: Godolphin Estate & Tregonning Hill
Description: Godolphin Estate features an ancient house, garden, and woodlands in Cornwall. Visitors can explore the historic estate, river walks, and Godolphin Hill. Tregonning Hill, accessible from the estate, reveals evidence of its mining heritage.

Name: Godrevy
Description: Dramatic headland with stunning views across St Ives Bay. Popular with walkers, surfers, and wildlife watchers, particularly for the grey seal colony at Mutton Cove.

Name: Gogar Wood
Description: Gogar Wood is a young, developing woodland on the western outskirts of Edinburgh. It features a range of native broadleaf species. Pathways allow for exploration and wildlife observation. The site is managed for biodiversity and public access.

Name: Golden Cap Estate
Description: Golden Cap Estate is the highest point on England's south coast, offering expansive views of Lyme Bay and the Jurassic Coast. The estate features woodlands, cliffs, and beaches, managed for nature conservation and public access through diverse footpaths.

Name: Golden Cap Estate
Description: The Golden Cap Estate includes Eype Down, cliffs, and coastal paths near West Bay, Dorset. It features the highest point on the South Coast of England, offering views across Lyme Bay towards the Isle of Portland. Managed by the National Trust.

Name: Golitha Falls
Description: Golitha Falls is a National Nature Reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest in Cornwall, England. This ancient woodland features the River Fowey cascading through a steep valley, creating a humid microclimate ideal for its renowned diverse mosses, ferns, and lichens. The reserve supports significant biodiversity, including rare bryophytes, bats, and otters.

Name: Golitha Falls
Description: Golitha Falls is a National Nature Reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest in Cornwall, South West England. This ancient woodland features a series of spectacular cascades along the River Fowey and is recognized as a temperate rainforest, supporting a rich diversity of mosses, lichens, and ferns.

Name: Gomm Valley
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Gomm Valley is a 4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Micklefield, a district of High Wycombe in Buckinghamshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust and is part of the Chilterns Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Name: Goonhilly Downs
Description: Goonhilly Downs is a Site of Special Scientific Interest that forms a raised plateau in the central western area of the Lizard peninsula in southern Cornwall, England.  It is one of 229 English national nature reserves designated by Natural England with an area of almost 1,270 hectares.

Name: Gordano Valley
Description: Gordano is an area of North Somerset, in England.  It has been designated as a National Nature Reserve.

Name: Goscote Reedbed
Description: Goscote Reedbed, a former landfill site along the Wyrley & Essington Canal in Walsall, West Midlands, has been transformed into a thriving wildlife haven. It features newly created reedbeds and wetland habitats, alongside a specific kingfisher nesting bank, enhancing biodiversity.

Name: Gowbarrow Park
Description: Gowbarrow Park, part of the Ullswater landscape, offers extensive views across the lake and features ancient woodlands. The National Trust manages this Lake District site, focusing on conservation to protect its diverse wildlife and enhance its natural beauty.

Name: Gowy Meadows Nature Reserve
Description: Gowy Meadows Nature Reserve is a 165.8-hectare nature reserve near Ellesmere Port, Cheshire, England.

Name: Gracious Pond
Description: Gracious Pond is a 14-hectare nature reserve in Chobham in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Graeme Hendrey Wood
Description: Graeme Hendrey Wood is a 10-hectare nature reserve east of Bletchingley in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Graffham Common
Description: Graffham Common is a 38-hectare nature reserve between Midhurst and Petworth in West Sussex.  It is owned and managed by the Sussex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Grafham Water
Description: Grafham Water is a large reservoir and an 806.3-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). The site includes a 114-hectare (280-acre) nature reserve, managed by Anglian Water, featuring extensive reedbeds, woodlands, and grasslands, providing habitat for diverse wildlife including overwintering birds and otters. The reserve offers hides for birdwatching.

Name: Graig Wood
Description: Graig Wood is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, noted for its biological characteristics, in Monmouthshire, south east Wales.  It forms part of the wider Hael Woods complex.

Name: Grange Barn
Description: Grange Barn is a 13th-century Cistercian monastic barn near Coggeshall, Essex, managed by the National Trust. It preserves medieval timber architecture and serves as a site for events and exploration within the wider Coggeshall Meadows.

Name: Grange Farm
Description: Grange Farm is an RSPB nature reserve near Honington, Suffolk, actively undergoing restoration from former arable land. It features a mix of newly created grasslands, wetlands, and hedgerows. The reserve provides vital habitats for a variety of bird species and local wildlife, focusing on ecological recovery.

Name: Grangelands and The Rifle Range
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 18 hectares.

Name: Granville Country Park
Description: Granville Country Park is a local nature reserve near Telford in Shropshire, England.  It is owned by Telford and Wrekin Council, who work in partnership with the Shropshire Wildlife Trust and Friends of Granville.

Name: Granville Nature Reserve
Description: Granville Country Park is a Local Nature Reserve near Telford, Shropshire, covering approximately 85.5 hectares of former industrial land. It features diverse habitats including wildflower meadows, woodlands, ponds, and marshland, supporting a variety of wildlife. The reserve is owned by Telford and Wrekin Council and managed in partnership with Shropshire Wildlife Trust and the Friends of Granville, offering accessible walking trails and showcasing its rich industrial heritage.

Name: Grays Thurrock Chalk Pit
Description: Grays Thurrock Chalk Pit is a 17.3-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest in Grays in Essex.

Name: Great Breach and Copley Woods
Description: Great Breach and Copley Woods is a 64.8 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest 1 km south of Compton Dundon and 5 km south-east of Street in Somerset, England, notified in 1972.

Name: Great Casterton Road Banks
Description: Great Casterton Road Banks is a 0.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the western outskirts of Stamford in Lincolnshire.

Name: Great Cornard Country Park
HostOrg: Great Cornard Parish Council (Owner) and Sudbury Common Lands Charity (Manager)
Description: Great Cornard Country Park is located along the River Stour Valley, forming part of the Stour Valley Path. It features meadows, woodland, and ponds, providing habitats for diverse wildlife and offering recreational space for visitors.

Name: Great Hangman & Little Hangman
Description: Great Hangman and Little Hangman are prominent coastal hills in North Devon. Great Hangman, at 318m, is England's highest sea cliff. Little Hangman is 218m. Both are part of the South West Coast Path, offering dramatic views of the Bristol Channel.

Name: Great Hockham, Thetford Forest
Description: Great Hockham is a tranquil woodland site within Thetford Forest, managed by Forestry England. It offers diverse habitats for wildlife, including distinctive features known as pingos formed during the last Ice Age. The area is part of the Breckland Forest Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a Special Protection Area (SPA) for birds like Woodlark and Nightjar. It features waymarked trails for walking and cycling, providing a peaceful environment for visitors to explore.

Name: Great Holland Pits
Description: Great Holland Pits is a 16.2-hectare nature reserve east of Great Holland in Essex.

Name: Great Langdale - Blea Tarn
Description: Great Langdale, a glacial valley in the Lake District, showcases dramatic fells and the serene Blea Tarn. This upland ecosystem supports diverse wildlife and offers tranquil landscapes. National Trust actively manages its conservation.

Name: Great Merrible Wood
Description: Great Merrible Wood is a 12 hectare nature reserve east of Hallaton in Leicestershire.  It is owned and managed by the Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust, and is part of the Eye Brook Valley Woods Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Great Wood
Description: Great Wood, an ancient woodland and conifer plantation on the Quantock Hills, features mature oak, beech, and sweet chestnut. Diverse flora and fauna thrive here. Trails for walkers and horse riders offer scenic views across the Bristol Channel.

Name: Great Wood
Description: Great Wood, managed by Forestry England, is an extensive forest in the Quantock Hills National Landscape, Somerset. It features ancient oak woodlands, majestic Douglas firs, and an extensive network of walking trails. The site is home to diverse wildlife including red deer, ravens, buzzards, and pied flycatchers, and offers picnic areas and family-friendly trails.

Name: Great Wood Borrowdale
Description: Great Wood, an ancient oak woodland in Borrowdale, is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and forms part of the internationally significant Borrowdale Rainforest National Nature Reserve in the Lake District. Situated near Derwent Water, it is a crucial area for conservation, supporting diverse flora and fauna, particularly rare lichens and bryophytes. The site offers various walking trails.

Name: Greatstone Dunes
Description: Greatstone Dunes is a Site of Special Scientific Interest in Kent, known for its unique habitat. It features mobile and fixed dunes, dune slacks, shingle, and saltmarsh. The site supports many rare plants and invertebrates, including the nationally rare sandhill rustic moth.

Name: Green Lane Wood
Description: Green Lane Wood, an ancient woodland in Cambridgeshire, is managed by the Woodland Trust. The site features mature trees, diverse flora, and a network of paths for visitors, providing a habitat for local wildlife and offering a tranquil setting.

Name: Green Park - Meadow Restoration Areas
Description: Green Park's meadow restoration areas enhance biodiversity in central London. Located near The Mall and Constitution Hill, these designated zones support pollinators and various wildlife, creating diverse habitats within the park's landscape.

Name: Greenham and Crookham Commons
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Greenham and Crookham Commons are two adjoining public park areas of 280.5-hectare common land designated as a biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in the civil parishes of Greenham and Thatcham, on the southern outskirts of Newbury in the English county of Berkshire, home to a variety of rare wildlife.

Name: Greenway Estate & River Dart Woods
Description: Greenway is a historic estate on the River Dart in Devon, once home to author Agatha Christie. The property features a house, gardens, and woodlands. Visitors can explore the house interiors, gardens with plant collections, and riverside walks.

Name: Greenwich Peninsula Ecology Park
Description: Greenwich Peninsula Ecology Park is a four-acre nature reserve in London, a designated Site of Borough Importance for Nature Conservation, Grade I. It features diverse freshwater habitats including two lakes, marshland, reedbeds, and meadows, supporting a rich variety of wildlife such as amphibians, fish, insects, and birds. The Conservation Volunteers (TCV) manages the site, offering environmental education and community events.

Name: Greno Woods
HostOrg: Wildlife Trust for Sheffield and Rotherham
Description: Greno Woods is a 178 hectares area of ancient woodland and nature reserve located north of Grenoside village, a suburb of Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England.  Previously used as a quarry, hunting ground, and for commercial forestry; it is now used for recreational walking, jogging and mountain biking.

Name: Grey Hope Bay
Description: Greyhope Bay is an award-winning community-led marine experience at the mouth of Aberdeen Harbour. It offers views of bottlenose dolphins, harbour porpoise, grey seals, and various seabirds. The site features a repurposed shipping container visitor centre and cafe.

Name: Grey Mare's Tail
Description: Grey Mare's Tail is a dramatic 60m waterfall in the Moffat Water Valley, offering a challenging upland walk to a tranquil loch above. The nature reserve is home to peregrine falcons, ospreys during summer, and a population of wild mountain goats.

Name: Greyfield Wood
Description: Greyfield Wood is a 36.23-hectare (89.5-acre) ancient woodland situated on the outskirts of High Littleton in north-east Somerset, approximately 16 km from Bath and 19 km from Bristol. Managed by the Woodland Trust, it features a diverse mix of ancient broadleaf trees, naturally regenerated areas, and conifer plantations, supporting a rich array of flora and fauna. It offers extensive permissive paths for public access, including circular walks.

Name: Greylake
Description: Greylake is an RSPB nature reserve situated on the Somerset Levels. The site features an accessible hide and boardwalk, offering views of wetland birds such as lapwings, snipe, and various duck species. It provides habitat for diverse wildlife, with seasonal highlights including breeding waders and wintering wildfowl.

Name: Greywell Moors
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Greywell Fen is a 38-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Greywell in Hampshire.  It is a Nature Conservation Review site, Grade 2, and an area of 13 hectares is a nature reserve called Greywell Moors, which is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Griffin Wood
Description: Griffin Wood is a 12-hectare community woodland in Bold, south St. Helens, Merseyside, managed by The Mersey Forest in partnership with the Friends of Griffin Wood. It comprises both mature and newly planted broadleaved trees and pines, along with wildflower meadows. The site features meandering paths, a community orchard, and a sculpture trail, offering green space for recreation and nature observation. It is part of the larger Bold Forest Park.

Name: Grime’s Graves
Description: Grime’s Graves is a unique Neolithic flint mine site and Scheduled Monument, managed by English Heritage. It features diverse chalk grassland and woodland, supporting rare plants like the military orchid and various invertebrate species, important for its archaeology and biodiversity, with ecological input from Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Grimwith Reservoir
Description: Grimwith Reservoir, a large upland reservoir in the Yorkshire Dales National Park near Pateley Bridge, supplies drinking water. It features extensive peat bogs, heather moorland, and grasslands, supporting diverse wildlife and critical habitats for wading birds.

Name: Grizedale Forest
Description: Grizedale Forest, located in the Lake District, features an extensive network of walking and cycling trails through woodlands. It is home to a unique collection of outdoor sculptures and provides habitats for diverse wildlife, including red deer. A visitor centre offers amenities.

Name: Grogley Wood
Description: Grogley Wood, part of the larger Bishop's, Hustyn, and Grogley Woods complex, is a semi-ancient woodland site near Bodmin, Cornwall. Managed by Forestry England, it features broadleaf and conifer areas, rich ground flora, and diverse birdlife. The woods are popular for public footpaths and offer extensive mountain biking trails, with connections to the Camel Trail.

Name: Groton Wood
Description: Groton Wood is a 20.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-east of Groton in Suffolk.

Name: Grovelands Park
Description: Grovelands Park is a Grade II* listed Green Flag park in Enfield, London. It features extensive woodlands, a formal garden, and a large lake. The lake has undergone enhancements to boost its biodiversity, supporting local wildlife.

Name: Gugh
Description: Gugh could be described as the sixth inhabited island of the Isles of Scilly, but is usually included with St Agnes with which it is joined by a sandy tombolo known as "The Bar" when exposed at low tide.  The island is only about 1 km long and about 0.

Name: Guisborough Forest
Description: Guisborough Forest is a popular woodland site managed by Forestry England, located on the edge of the North York Moors National Park. It provides trails for walking, cycling, and horse riding, along with a visitor centre and children's play areas for recreational activities.

Name: Gullivers Farm
Description: Gullivers Farm is a 90-acre organic and biodynamic working farm and social enterprise in West Moors, Dorset, managed by Sturts Community Trust. It provides support and opportunities to adults with varying support needs, alongside sustainable farming practices and a farm shop and cafe.

Name: Gunby Hall Estate
Description: Gunby Hall Estate near Spilsby, Lincolnshire, is a Victorian country house with gardens and parkland managed by the National Trust. It focuses on 'Wolds Edge Farming for Nature' to encourage wildlife and biodiversity across the landscape. Visitors can explore the house, formal gardens, and wider estate.

Name: Gunners Park and Shoebury Ranges
Description: Gunners Park and Shoebury Ranges is a 25 hectare nature reserve in Shoeburyness in Essex.  It is managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Gunnersbury Triangle
Description: Gunnersbury Triangle is a 2.57-hectare local nature reserve in Chiswick, in the London boroughs of Ealing and Hounslow, immediately to the east of Gunnersbury.

Name: Gunpowder Park
Description: Gunpowder Park, a Green Flag site in Lee Valley Regional Park, was transformed from a former testing ground. It offers 100 acres of meadows and woods, providing habitats for diverse wildlife. The park features trails for walking and cycling.

Name: Gunton Meadow
Description: Gunton Meadow is a 2-hectare nature reserve in Lowestoft in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Gunton Warren
Description: Gunton Warren and Corton Woods is a 31.9 hectare Local Nature Reserve in Lowestoft in Suffolk.

Name: Gunwalloe & Church Cove
Description: Gunwalloe and Church Cove in Cornwall is a coastal site managed by the National Trust. It features sandy beaches, a historic church, and access to the South West Coast Path. The area is known for shipwrecks and natural beauty.

Name: Gwaith Powdwr
Description: Gwaith Powdwr,, situated in Penrhyndeudraeth, Wales, is a decommissioned explosives works now managed as a Nature Reserve by the North Wales Wildlife Trust.  The explosives factory was initially opened in 1865 and changed hands several times before being bought by Ralph Cooke in 1922.

Name: Gwen and Vera's Fields
Description: Gwen and Vera's Fields is a 0.28-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: Gwenffrwd-Dinas
Description: Ancient oak woodlands in the Tywi valley, Carmarthenshire, Wales. A Special Area of Conservation, home to pied flycatchers, redstarts, and wood warblers. Bluebells carpet the valley floor. Features rocky river stretches and waterfalls, managed by RSPB.

Name: Hackhurst Downs
Description: Hackhurst and White Downs is a 185.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Dorking in Surrey.

Name: Hadrian's Wall & Housesteads Fort
Description: Housesteads Roman Fort, a UNESCO World Heritage Site on Hadrian's Wall, offers visitors a unique blend of history and nature. Explore Britain's most complete Roman fort, including barracks, a hospital, granaries, and latrines, while discovering Roman soldier life. The fort is set within a dramatic natural landscape cared for by the National Trust, offering stunning views across the wall and opportunities to experience the surrounding natural wilderness and spot diverse wildlife, contributing to wider nature conservation efforts along Hadrian's Wall.

Name: Hadrian's Wall Wetlands Landscape Recovery Project
Description: Hadrian's Wall Wetlands is an 11,000-acre Landscape Recovery Project. It restores and enhances peatlands and wetlands across the Hadrian's Wall area in Northumberland, aiming to improve biodiversity, water quality, and carbon storage within the national park.

Name: Hainault Forest
Description: Hainault Forest spans 335 acres in northeast London, featuring ancient woodland, grasslands, a lake, and a zoo. Visitors can explore various walking trails, engage with wildlife, and enjoy open spaces for recreation. The site is a significant green lung.

Name: Haldon Forest Park
Description: Haldon Forest Park, near Exeter, provides varied outdoor activities including walking, running, and cycling trails for all abilities. It features scenic views and diverse woodlands managed for recreation and conservation. The site offers a Discovery Trail and challenging mountain bike routes.

Name: Halesworth Millennium Green
Description: Halesworth Millennium Green is a 55-acre nature reserve on the River Blyth flood plain in Suffolk, offering diverse habitats from meadows to woodlands. The site provides walking trails and focuses on conservation, with ongoing river restoration work, and is managed by the Halesworth Millennium Green CIO.

Name: Ham Hill, Wiltshire
Description: Ham Hill is a hill and area of chalk downland in Wiltshire, England, on the steep banks running alongside the road from the village of Ham to Buttermere, close to the Berkshire border.  A biological Site of Special Scientific Interest, notified in 1971, covers 1.

Name: Ham House and Garden
Description: Ham House is a 17th-century house by the River Thames in Richmond, London. Its formal gardens feature an orangery, kitchen garden, and ancient trees. Re-created 17th-century wilderness areas and wildflower meadows also exist within the estate.

Name: Ham Street Woods
Description: Ham Street Woods is a 97-hectare ancient woodland National Nature Reserve (NNR) and Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) near Hamstreet, Ashford, Kent. It is a remnant of the extensive oak forests that once covered the Weald, featuring diverse habitats including oak and hornbeam stands, supporting varied flora and fauna. The reserve is actively managed by Natural England for conservation, scientific research, education, and public access, offering waymarked trails.

Name: Ham Wall
Description: Ham Wall is a Somerset wetland nature reserve managed by the RSPB. It features extensive reedbeds, open water, and wet woodland, providing habitat for diverse wildlife including bitterns, marsh harriers, and otters. Visitors can explore a network of trails and viewing hides.

Name: Hamford Water National Nature Reserve
Description: Hamford Water is an internationally important wetland, encompassing creeks, saltmarsh, and mudflats. It supports significant populations of overwintering and breeding birds, including avocets and dark-bellied brent geese. This estuarine site is also home to seals and diverse marine life.

Name: Hampstead Heath
Description: Hampstead Heath is a large, ancient parkland in north London, offering diverse habitats, natural swimming ponds, and panoramic city views. It features extensive woodlands, meadows, and sports facilities, managed for public access and conservation.

Name: Hamsterley Forest
Description: Hamsterley Forest covers 2,000 hectares, making it County Durham's largest woodland. It features diverse walking, cycling, and horse riding trails, alongside play areas and a cafe. The forest offers year-round opportunities for wildlife observation and outdoor activities.

Name: Hanbury Hall
Description: Hanbury Hall is a William and Mary style country house in Worcestershire, cared for by the National Trust. It features a formal Baroque garden, extensive parkland, and an orchard, reflecting 18th-century design and rural life.

Name: Handa, Scotland
Description: Handa Island or usually Handa, is an island in Eddrachillis Bay off the west coast of Sutherland, Scotland.  It is 309 hectares and 123 metres at its highest point.

Name: Hannah's Meadows
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 9 hectares.

Name: Hanningfield Reservoir
Description: Hanningfield Reservoir is a large 25,500-million-litre pumped storage reservoir located between Billericay and Chelmsford in Essex.  It has a surface area of 352 hectares and is owned and operated by Essex and Suffolk Water.

Name: Hardcastle Crags
Description: Hardcastle Crags features ancient woodlands and a rare temperate rainforest. The 19th-century Gibson Mill is water-powered. Miles of footpaths wind through steep valleys, home to diverse wildlife and over 100 species of mosses and liverworts.

Name: Harden Quarry
Description: Harden Quarry is an active hard rock quarry within Northumberland National Park, known for significant Bronze Age archaeological discoveries including a settlement and burial sites. Located in the Cheviot Hills, it is also a site where nature recovery efforts are underway, involving local partners and volunteers for conservation tasks.

Name: Hardwick Hall
Description: Hardwick Hall, a National Trust property, is undergoing significant restoration within the Doe Lea River Valley. Work focuses on improving river health, water quality, and biodiversity. Efforts aim to restore natural river flow and create new habitats for a diverse range of wildlife.

Name: Hare Hill
Description: Hare Hill is a tranquil wooded garden and parkland managed by the National Trust, located near Macclesfield in Cheshire. It features a delightful walled garden, renowned rhododendrons, azaleas, and diverse plant collections. Visitors can explore various paths, serene ponds, and a natural play area for families.

Name: Haresfield Beacon & Standish Wood
Description: Haresfield Beacon and Standish Wood offers expansive views across the Severn Vale towards the Brecon Beacons. This Cotswold escarpment features ancient woodland, limestone grassland, and Iron Age hillfort remnants. It provides habitats for diverse wildlife, including wildflowers and butterflies.

Name: Harridge Wood
Description: Harridge Wood is an area of woodland in Somerset, England.  From about 1300 AD part of the wood was the scene of coal mining, which continued until around 1800.

Name: Harston Wood
Description: Harston Wood is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is an ancient woodland, adjacent to the village of Froghall, near Cheadle, Staffordshire, England.

Name: Hartslock
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Hartslock, also known as Hartslock Woods, is a 41.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in a wooded area on the north bank of the River Thames to the south-east of Goring-on-Thames in the English county of Oxfordshire.

Name: Harwood Forest
Description: Harwood Forest, north of Rothbury, is a vast expanse of commercial conifers and ancient woodland. It offers numerous walking and cycling trails, providing scenic views across the Northumberland countryside.

Name: Hatchmere
Description: Hatchmere is a small mere and nature reserve in Delamere Forest, southeast of Frodsham, Cheshire, England.  It is also the name of a hamlet near the village of Norley.

Name: Hatfield Forest
Description: Hatfield Forest is a unique example of a nearly complete medieval hunting forest.
