Managed in partnership by Essex Wildlife Trust and the National Trust, it features ancient trees, open glades, and a large lake, providing diverse habitats for wildlife. Visitors can explore woodlands and grasslands.

Name: Hatfield Forest
Description: Hatfield Forest, a National Nature Reserve in Essex, is England's only remaining intact Royal hunting forest. It features ancient trees, woodlands, grasslands, and a lake, demonstrating a landscape shaped by centuries of traditional forest management.

Name: Hatfield Moors
Description: Hatfield Moors is a large nature reserve in South Yorkshire, part of the Humberhead Peatlands National Nature Reserve, featuring extensive blanket bog and wet heath. It supports species like red grouse, golden plover, and curlew. The site is crucial for carbon storage and water quality.

Name: Haughmond Hill
Description: Haughmond Hill offers views over Shrewsbury, the Shropshire Hills, and the Cheshire Plain. It features waymarked trails for walking and cycling through mixed woodland. Visitors can find picnic areas, a cafe, and a play area. The site is managed by Forestry England.

Name: Hawkins Wood
Description: Hawkins Wood is a 10 hectare nature reserve south of Therfield in Hertfordshire.  It is managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Hawthorn Dene
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 67 hectares.

Name: Hayle
Description: Hayle is a port town and civil parish in west Cornwall, England, United Kingdom.  It is situated at the mouth of the Hayle River and is approximately seven miles northeast of Penzance.

Name: Haymill Valley
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Haymill Valley is a 7.8-hectare Local Nature Reserve in Slough in Berkshire.

Name: Haysden Country Park
Description: Haysden Country Park, near Tonbridge, is a Local Nature Reserve. It features varied habitats, including lakes, a river, and woodlands. The park supports diverse wildlife and offers recreational activities such as walking and watersports. It is popular for its natural beauty and accessible paths.

Name: Hazlewood Marshes
Description: Hazlewood Marshes is a 64 hectare nature reserve west of Aldeburgh in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Headley Heath
Description: Headley Heath is a rare heathland and woodland site in the Surrey Hills National Landscape, South East England. This Site of Special Scientific Interest supports diverse habitats, including rare birds and reptiles. It is popular with walkers, cyclists, and horse riders.

Name: Headstone Manor Park
Description: Headstone Manor Park in Harrow, London, features a river restoration project that daylighted 150m of the Yeading Brook. A new meandering channel replaces a culvert, improving water quality, habitats, and reducing flood risk, enhancing the park's environment.

Name: Heartwood Forest
Description: Heartwood Forest near St Albans, Hertfordshire, is England's largest new native forest, spanning 858 acres. Managed by the Woodland Trust, it features extensive woodlands, meadows, and orchards, offering walking trails and diverse wildlife habitats.

Name: Heath's Meadows
Description: Heath's Meadows is a local nature reserve with an area of over 5.5 ha located in Burgh le Marsh, Lincolnshire, England.

Name: Heather Underhill
Description: Heather Underhill is a 13-hectare woodland, part of the National Forest in Leicestershire. It features diverse native broadleaf and conifer trees, offering wildlife habitat. The site provides public access for walking and connects to a wider path network. It is actively managed.

Name: Heaton Park
Description: Heaton Park is a municipal park in north Manchester, England, covering over 600 acres. The largest park in Greater Manchester, it features woodlands, grasslands, and wetlands. Biodiversity recovery areas are actively managed to enhance ecological value for diverse wildlife.

Name: Heber's Ghyll
Description: Heber's Ghyll is a beautiful woodland area and stream with waterfalls located near Ilkley, West Yorkshire. It offers scenic walks through ancient woodland and is managed by Bradford District Parks, providing a tranquil spot for nature observation.

Name: Hedgecourt
Description: Hedgecourt is a 33.6-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Felbridge in Surrey.

Name: Hedley Stringer Wood
Description: Hedley Stringer Wood is a young woodland near the village of Wilsden, Bradford, planted in 2000. It offers open vistas, a small stream, and a network of paths suitable for dog walking and family visits. The site enhances local biodiversity and provides green space.

Name: Hedleyhope Fell
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 202 hectares.

Name: Heigham Holmes
Description: Heigham Holmes is a secluded island in the Norfolk Broads, only accessible by boat on the River Thurne. It serves as a vital wildlife haven, home to otters and the rare fen raft spider. Visits are by pre-booked boat trip only.

Name: Hem Heath Woods
Description: Hem Heath Woods is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is on the southern fringe of Stoke-on-Trent, England.

Name: Hemsted Forest
Description: Hemsted Forest is a working woodland near Benenden, Kent, offering walking, cycling, and horse riding trails. It features mature conifer and broadleaf trees, and is managed by Forestry England. The site provides a natural habitat for various wildlife.

Name: Hen Reedbeds
Description: Hen Reedbeds is a 55 hectare nature reserve near the North Sea coast of the English county of Suffolk.  The reserve is located in the Blyth valley between Reydon and Blythburgh, approximately 2.

Name: Hertford Heath
Description: Hertford Heath nature reserve is a 28 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Hertford Heath in Hertfordshire.  It is managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust and the local planning authority is East Hertfordshire District Council.

Name: Hesleden Dene
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 9 hectares.

Name: Hethel Old Thorn
Description: Hethel Old Thorn is a 0. 025-hectare nature reserve south-west of Norwich in Norfolk.

Name: Hewitt's Chalk Bank
Description: Hewitt's Chalk Bank is a 4-hectare nature reserve north-east of Pratt's Bottom in the London Borough of Bromley.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Hexhamshire Common
Description: Hexhamshire Common, part of the Northumberland uplands, is a significant peatland area within the Great North Bog initiative. This landscape-scale restoration project aims for environmental recovery across Northern England.

Name: Hexton Chalk Pit
Description: Hexton Chalk Pit is a 1.9-hectare nature reserve in Hexton in North Hertfordshire, managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Heyford Meadow
Description: Heyford Meadow is a species-rich floodplain meadow by the River Thames, Oxfordshire. It features colourful wildflowers such as the nationally scarce snake's head fritillary, supporting diverse insects, birds, and other wildlife.

Name: Heysham Coast
Description: Heysham Coast offers varied coastal habitats including saltmarsh, sand dunes, and grassland, important for diverse birdlife. Visitors can explore historic St Patrick's Chapel ruins and enjoy scenic views across Morecambe Bay, a significant natural environment.

Name: Hickling Broad
Description: Hickling Broad is a 600-hectare nature reserve 4 km south-east of Stalham, north-east of Norwich in Norfolk.  It is managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: High Close Estate and Arboretum
Description: High Close Estate and Arboretum, near Loughrigg Fell, Lake District, features historic gardens with mature trees, rhododendrons, and azaleas. It offers views across Langdale Valley and includes diverse plant collections and walking paths for visitors.

Name: High Elms Country Park
Description: High Elms Country Park, near Orpington, features ancient woodlands, wildflower meadows, and chalk grassland. It supports diverse wildlife. Managed by London Borough of Bromley, Kent Wildlife Trust also manages a part.

Name: High Wood NR
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 3 hectares.

Name: High Woods Country Park
Description: High Woods Country Park, a Green Flag award winner in Colchester, features woodland, grassland, lake, and marsh habitats. Owned by Colchester City Council, it provides crucial space for local wildlife and community recreation. Essex Wildlife Trust manages adjacent areas.

Name: Highfield Moss
Description: Highfield Moss is a nature reserve of the Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside, near Lowton in the Metropolitan Borough of Wigan, Greater Manchester.  It is designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Highgate Common
Description: Highgate Common is a Staffordshire Wildlife Trust reserve containing a mix of heathland and woodland.  It is about 116 hectares or 286 acres in size.

Name: Highgate Wood
Description: Highgate Wood is a 28-hectare ancient woodland in north London, managed as a public open space. It features mature trees, diverse wildlife, and facilities including a playground, cafe, and sports pitches. The site is popular for recreation and nature observation.

Name: Hilfield Park Reservoir
Description: Hilfield Park Reservoir is a 76.3 ha construction built in 1953 between Bushey and Elstree in Hertfordshire, and owned by Affinity Water.

Name: Hill End Pit
Description: Hill End Pit is a 0.7-hectare nature reserve on the site of a former chalk pit, in St Paul's Walden in North Hertfordshire.

Name: Hill Hook Local Nature Reserve
HostOrg: Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust
Description: Hill Hook is an area of Sutton Coldfield, Birmingham, England.  The area includes Hill Hook Local Nature Reserve, declared in 2003 with an area of 5.

Name: Hill Park
Description: Hill Park, Tatsfield is a 24.5-hectare Local Nature Reserve south of Tatsfield in Surrey.

Name: Hindhead Commons and the Devil's Punch Bowl
Description: Hindhead Commons and the Devil's Punch Bowl is a large area of heathland and woodland in Surrey, managed by the National Trust. It offers dramatic views, walking trails, and significant natural heritage. This site is known for its diverse wildlife and ongoing conservation.

Name: Hinksey Heights
Description: Hinksey Heights is a diverse nature reserve in Oxford, featuring a nationally rare alkaline fen, reedbeds, wet woodlands, and grasslands. It provides vital habitats for rare plants, butterflies, and birds, including species like Marsh Helleborine and the Dark-winged Soldier fly. Ongoing restoration efforts are focused on enhancing its significant biodiversity. Visitors enjoy extensive views across the city.

Name: Hitchcopse Pit
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Hitchcopse Pit is a 3-hectare nature reserve north-west of Abingdon-on-Thames in Oxfordshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Hobbs Quarry SSSI, Longhope
Description: Hobbs Quarry, Longhope is a 1-hectare geological and biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, England, notified in 1966.  It is situated midway between Longhope and Dursley Cross in the Forest of Dean.

Name: Hockley Meadows
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Hockley Meadows is a 9-hectare nature reserve south of Winchester in Hampshire.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Hoe Road Meadow
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 3 hectares.

Name: Hoe Rough
Description: Hoe Rough is a 12-hectare nature reserve north of Dereham in Norfolk.  It is managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust, and is part of the Beetley and Hoe Meadows Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Hog and Hollowhill Woods
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Hollowhill and Pullingshill Woods is a 23-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Marlow in Buckinghamshire.  It is in the Chilterns Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, and the Chilterns Beechwoods Special Area of Conservation.

Name: Holborough Marshes
Description: Holborough Marshes is a 35-hectare nature reserve on the outskirts of Snodland, south-west of Chatham in Kent.  It is managed by Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Holcroft Moss
Description: Holcroft Moss is a nature reserve of the Cheshire Wildlife Trust, a lowland bog about 6 miles north-east of Warrington.

Name: Holes Bay Nature Park
Description: Holes Bay Nature Park is a protected area, 286 hectares in size, on and around Holes Bay, an embayment of Poole Harbour within the Borough of Poole that is important for wildlife, especially wetland birds.  It was designated a nature park in March 2015.

Name: Holland Haven
Description: Holland Haven is a coastal nature reserve in Essex, featuring saltmarsh, reedbeds, and grasslands. It provides essential habitats for a variety of birds, including bearded tits and marsh harriers, alongside diverse insect populations. The site offers accessible walking routes and birdwatching opportunities.

Name: Holly Hill
Description: Holly Hill is a public open space managed by Tonbridge and Malling Borough Council, located on the North Downs between Vigo and Snodland, near Meopham. It features ancient woodland with coppiced hazel, mature oak, and sweet chestnut trees. The site supports diverse wildlife, including various bird species and invertebrates, providing a habitat for woodland flora.

Name: Hollybed Farm Meadows
Description: Hollybed Farm Meadows is nature reserve of the Worcestershire Wildlife Trust, about 1 mile west of the village of Castlemorton, in Worcestershire, England.  The habitat is grassland.

Name: Holme Dunes
Description: Holme Dunes is a 192-hectare nature reserve near Holme-next-the-Sea in Norfolk.  It is managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust, and is a National Nature Reserve.

Name: Holme Fen National Nature Reserve
Description: Holme Fen is a National Nature Reserve in Cambridgeshire and a key part of the Great Fen project. It holds the lowest point in Britain and features diverse habitats including silver birch woodland and fenland. Distinctive 'bog oaks' are present.

Name: Holt Fish Pass
Description: Holt Lock & Weir is the highest point fish can reach on the River Severn. The fish pass, part of the Unlocking the Severn project, helps species like the Twaite Shad bypass the weir. The site includes an observation window for visitors to view migrating fish. Parking is available nearby.

Name: Holwell Reserves
Description: Holwell Reserves is a 16.4 hectares nature reserve north of Melton Mowbray in Leicestershire.

Name: Holyfield Marsh
Description: Holyfield Marsh, part of Lee Valley Regional Park in Essex, is an internationally important wetland. It provides a vital habitat for diverse bird populations, including waterfowl and waders, offering year-round birdwatching.

Name: Holywell Bay & Kelsey Head
Description: Holywell Bay offers golden sands, grassy dunes, and the iconic Gull Rocks on the North Cornwall coast. Part of a larger landscape including Kelsey Head, it provides coastal walks, wildlife spotting, and rock pool exploration for visitors.

Name: Homefield Wood
Description: Homefield Wood is a mixed woodland nature reserve near Marlow. It features ancient woodland characteristics and supports diverse flora and fauna, including dormice and various orchids. Traditional coppicing is used to maintain biodiversity and create habitats for rare butterflies.

Name: Homefield Wood
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Homefield Wood is a 6.1-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest in Hambleden in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Homington and Coombe Bissett Downs
Description: Homington and Coombe Bissett Downs is a 25. 0 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Wiltshire, notified in 1971.

Name: Honeygar Farm
Description: Honeygar Farm, or Honeygar, is a rewilding project of Somerset Wildlife Trust, near Westhay on the Somerset Levels of Somerset, England.

Name: Honeypot Wood
Description: Honeypot Wood is a 9.5-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Dereham in Norfolk, England.

Name: Hook Common and Bartley Heath
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Hook Common and Bartley Heath is a 129.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the southern outskirts of Hook in Hampshire, England.

Name: Hook Norton Cutting
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Hook Norton Cutting and Banks is a 6.7-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Hook Norton in Oxfordshire.

Name: Hopton Fen
Description: Hopton Fen is a 15.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Hopton in Suffolk.

Name: Hornchurch Country Park
Description: Hornchurch Country Park is a Green Flag park in Havering, London, on a former WWII airfield. It offers diverse habitats like grasslands, woodlands, and ponds, traversed by the River Ingrebourne, providing wildlife haven and recreation.

Name: Horndon Meadow
Description: Horndon Meadow is a 0.8-hectare nature reserve north of Stanford-le-Hope in Essex.

Name: Horsey Island, Devon
Description: Horsey Island is a nature reserve adjoining the Taw estuary in northwest Devon, England.  It is owned and managed by the Devon Wildlife Trust, the trust having purchased the 80 hectare site in November 2019.

Name: Horsey Mere & Marshes
Description: Horsey Mere and its marshes are a key part of the Norfolk Broads. The site offers panoramic views and provides habitat for diverse wildlife, including many bird species. Visitors explore the historic Horsey Windpump and its scenic walking trails.

Name: Horsey Windpump
Description: Horsey Windpump stands on the Horsey Estate in the Broads National Park, Norfolk. This iconic National Trust windpump offers panoramic views across the mere and surrounding marshes, a haven for wildlife. Visitors can climb to the top for expansive views.

Name: Hosehill Lake
Description: Hosehill Lake is a former gravel pit near Theale, West Berkshire, now a diverse nature reserve. It features a large lake, reedbeds, and woodlands, providing a vital habitat for numerous bird species throughout the year. Visitors can enjoy walking trails and bird hides.

Name: Hosehill Lake
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Hosehill Lake is a 23.6-hectare Local Nature Reserve west of Reading in Berkshire.

Name: Hothfield Heathlands
Description: Hothfield Common is a 56.5-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-east of Ashford in Kent.

Name: Houghton Forest
Description: Houghton Forest lies on the edge of the South Downs National Park in West Sussex. It features varied woodlands, open chalk grassland, and panoramic views across the Arun Valley. This site provides diverse habitats and is popular for walking.

Name: Hounslow Heath Green Gym
Description: Hounslow Heath Green Gym is a TCV project in West London. It meets weekly, offering conservation activities like scrub removal, path clearing, and pond maintenance. Tasks vary seasonally, contributing to the management of Hounslow Heath. No experience is required.

Name: How Hill National Nature Reserve
Description: How Hill National Nature Reserve offers diverse habitats within the Norfolk Broads, including wetlands and woodlands. Visitors can explore nature trails, the gardens of How Hill House, and a boardwalk through sedge and rush beds. Electric Eel boat trips provide unique water-based tours.

Name: Howell Hill
Description: Howell Hill is a 5-hectare nature reserve east of Ewell in Surrey.  It is owned by Surrey County Council and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Howlands Marsh
Description: Howlands Marsh is a 29.9-hectare nature reserve north-east of St Osyth in Essex.

Name: Howsham Mill Island
Description: Howsham Mill Island is a wooded island in the River Derwent near Malton, North Yorkshire. It provides habitat for otters, kingfishers, and various invertebrates. The island is part of the River Derwent Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and is managed for biodiversity by the Renewable Heritage Trust. The island is publicly accessible, though the mill building has specific opening hours.

Name: Huckerby's Meadows
Description: Huckerby's Meadows is a 13 hectare nature reserve adjacent to Heathrow Airport in the London Borough of Hillingdon.  It is managed by the London Wildlife Trust, and is part of the Crane Corridor Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation.

Name: Hucking Estate
Description: Hucking Estate offers a mosaic of ancient woodland, grassland, orchards, and arable land in the Kent Downs Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. This wildlife haven supports varied flora and fauna, including dormice and many bird species. Walking trails are present.

Name: Hucking Estate
Description: Hucking Estate is a large woodland and open space mosaic in Kent, South East England. It features ancient woodland, recently planted areas, and meadows, providing diverse habitats for wildlife. The site offers numerous walking trails and is part of a landscape restoration project.

Name: Humberhead Peatlands National Nature Reserve
Description: Humberhead Peatlands National Nature Reserve is England's largest lowland raised bog, encompassing Thorne, Hatfield, and Crowle Moors across 2,800 hectares. It is a Special Area of Conservation, vital for its unique peatland habitats and rare wildlife. Restoration efforts are ongoing.

Name: Hunsdon and Eastwick Meads
Description: Hunsdon Mead is a 34 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Harlow and east of Roydon in Essex.  The site is partly in Essex and partly in Hertfordshire, and it is jointly owned and managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust and the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Hunsdon Mead
Description: Hunsdon Mead is a 34 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Harlow and east of Roydon in Essex.  The site is partly in Essex and partly in Hertfordshire, and it is jointly owned and managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust and the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Hunter's Hill
Description: Hunter's Hill is a woodland reserve overlooking the Douglas Valley near Parbold. Mixed oak and birch woodlands support diverse wildlife along a network of paths. The site also features the remains of a Victorian folly, offering historical interest to visitors.

Name: Hunter's Wood Nature Reserve
Description: Hunter's Wood Nature Reserve is a nature reserve near Kingsley, Cheshire, England, managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.  Hunter's Wood is a relatively new piece of woodland, originally planted on what was rough pasture on the southern bank of the River Weaver in 1999.

Name: Hunthouse Wood
Description: Hunthouse Wood is a nature reserve of the Worcestershire Wildlife Trust, situated near the villages of Clows Top and Mamble, in Worcestershire, England.

Name: Hurley Chalk Pit
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Hurley Chalk Pit is a 1-hectare nature reserve west of Maidenhead in Berkshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Hustyn Wood
Description: Hustyn Wood is a mixed woodland in Cornwall, managed by Forestry England, adjoining Bishop's Woods. It features ancient trees, including tall Douglas firs, and offers a diverse habitat for wildlife. The site provides popular walking and cycling trails, accessible from the Camel Trail, and contributes to local biodiversity.

Name: Hutchinson's Bank
Description: Hutchinson's Bank is 21.8 hectare Local Nature Reserve and Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation in New Addington in the London Borough of Croydon.

Name: Hutchison's Meadow
Description: Hutchison's Meadow is a one hectare nature reserve in Melton in Suffolk.  It is owned and managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Hutton Roof Crags
Description: Hutton Roof Crags is a hill in southeastern Cumbria in northwest England, located near to the village of Hutton Roof.  It has extensive areas of limestone pavement as well as grassland and woodland.

Name: Hyde Park
Description: Hyde Park in central London features The Dell, a picturesque rock garden, and the Serpentine lake, which supports diverse wildlife. It is one of the capital's eight Royal Parks, offering both natural habitats and recreational spaces for visitors.

Name: Hythe Spartina Marsh
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 10 hectares.

Name: Ickworth Estate
Description: Ickworth Estate is an 1,800-acre Suffolk property featuring a neoclassical mansion, Italianate garden, and ancient deer park. The estate actively manages nature recovery projects across its parkland and Lownde Wood, enhancing diverse habitats for wildlife. Visitors can explore extensive walks.

Name: Ide Hill
Description: Ide Hill offers panoramic views over the Weald of Kent, featuring ancient woodlands and open commons along the Greensand Ridge. Visitors can follow waymarked trails through diverse habitats. The site is managed for conservation, providing opportunities for walking and enjoying nature.

Name: Idle Valley Nature Reserve
Description: The Idle Valley Nature Reserve, also known as Lound Gravel Pits or Sutton and Lound Gravel Pits, is a wetland Site of Special Scientific Interest situated north-west of the town of Retford in the Bassetlaw district of north Nottinghamshire.  The nature reserve is situated along the western bank of the River Idle and east of the villages of Sutton cum Lound and Lound.

Name: Iffley Meadows
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Iffley Meadows is a 36.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Oxford in Oxfordshire.

Name: Ilam Park & Dovedale
Description: Ilam Park, a 160-acre riverside park, features a 17th-century hall and designed landscape near Dovedale. It offers walking routes along the River Manifold and serves as a gateway to the White Peak, known for its distinctive limestone geology.

Name: Ilfracombe & Torrs Park
Description: A dramatic coastal landscape near Ilfracombe, North Devon, offering rugged cliffs, panoramic views across the Bristol Channel, and ancient woodlands. Popular for walking, the site features maintained paths, including parts of the South West Coast Path. Managed for nature and public access.

Name: Ilkley Integrated Constructed Wetland
Description: The Ilkley Integrated Constructed Wetland is a nature-based solution designed to provide a final stage of wastewater treatment for the upgraded Ilkley Wastewater Treatment Works. It features six interconnected lagoons with specially chosen wetland plants that naturally treat water before its safe return to the River Wharfe. This project also creates new habitats, enhances biodiversity, and provides public access, contributing to the ecological health and natural flood management of the Lower Wharfe Valley.

Name: Inchnadamph NNR Bone Caves
Description: Inchnadamph NNR in the Scottish Highlands is a landscape of limestone hills, caves, and gorges. Its famous Bone Caves contain unique remains of arctic animals from the last Ice Age, including lynx and polar bear. The reserve supports ancient woodlands and diverse plant life.

Name: Inchree Waterfall & Wood
Description: Inchree, near Fort William, features a spectacular multi-tiered waterfall and accessible woodland trails for walking and cycling. Visitors enjoy nature and wildlife watching opportunities within the Scottish Highlands.

Name: Ingleborough
Description: Ingleborough is the second-highest mountain in the Yorkshire Dales, England.  It is one of the Yorkshire Three Peaks, and is frequently climbed as part of the Three Peaks walk.

Name: Ingrebourne Valley
Description: Ingrebourne Valley, a nature reserve in Havering, offers diverse habitats including woodlands, grasslands, and wetlands. Part of Ingrebourne Marshes SSSI, it runs south from Upminster to Hornchurch, supporting various wildlife species and providing public recreation.

Name: Ingrebourne Valley
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 261 hectares.

Name: Inkpen Common
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Inkpen Common or Inkpen Great Common is a 12.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Inkpen in Berkshire.

Name: Inkpen Crocus Field
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Inkpen Crocus Fields is a 3.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Inkpen in Berkshire.

Name: Inner Forth
Description: The Inner Forth Wetlands are a significant landscape project in Central Scotland, focused on restoring and connecting vital habitats for migratory birds and local wildlife. It encompasses a network of nature reserves and coastal areas.

Name: Insh Marshes
HostOrg: Royal Society for the Protection of Birds
Description: Insh Marshes is one of Europe's most important wetlands, a vast flood plain alongside the River Spey. Thousands of migratory birds stop here seasonally, and many species of waders, ducks, and geese breed in summer. The reserve supports diverse wildlife, including otters and ospreys. Accessible trails and hides offer viewing opportunities.

Name: Invereshie and Inshriach NNR
Description: Invereshie and Inshriach NNR spans a vast Highland landscape between Strathspey and Speyside. It features extensive Caledonian pinewoods, open moorland, montane habitats, and the River Feshie. This reserve supports rare species including capercaillie, Scottish crossbill, red squirrel, and wildcat.

Name: Inverewe Garden & Estate
Description: Inverewe Garden & Estate is a historic botanical garden in Wester Ross, Scotland, established in the 19th century. It showcases diverse plant collections from around the world, benefiting from the Gulf Stream. The estate includes woodlands, a walled garden, and offers various walking routes.

Name: Iona
Description: Iona, an island off Mull, offers sandy beaches, rocky coves, and significant natural heritage. Its traditional crofting lands support diverse wildlife, including corncrakes. It is a historic place of pilgrimage and peace.

Name: Iping and Stedham Commons
Description: Iping and Stedham Commons is a nature reserve owned and managed by the Sussex Wildlife Trust.  It is a 125.

Name: Iron Latch
Description: Iron Latch is a 4.3-hectare nature reserve in Eight Ash Green, west of Colchester in Essex.

Name: Isabella Plantation
Description: Isabella Plantation is a 40-acre ornamental woodland garden located within Richmond Park in London. It is renowned for its evergreen azaleas, rhododendrons, and other acid-loving plants. The garden features diverse seasonal displays, streams, and ponds, providing a habitat for native wildlife.

Name: Isleworth Ait
Description: Isleworth Ait is a wooded island in the River Thames near Isleworth, West London, close to where the River Crane meets the Thames. The Conservation Volunteers (TCV) supports habitat management work in the wider River Crane Project area to enhance local biodiversity and natural habitats.

Name: Isleworth Ait
Description: Isleworth Ait is a London Wildlife Trust nature reserve, and is a teardrop-shaped island in the River Thames in England, between 3.5-hectare and 9.

Name: Iver Environment Centre
Description: Iver Environment Centre, located in the Colne Valley between Uxbridge and Slough, is a 2.4-acre site featuring diverse habitats including ponds, meadows, a community orchard, woodland, and a poly tunnel rainforest. Managed by Groundwork South, it serves as a local hub for environmental education, outdoor learning, and community activities, supporting wildlife and engaging people of all ages and abilities.

Name: Ivy Hatch
Description: Ivy Hatch Nature Reserve in Ivy Hatch, north of Tonbridge in Kent, is a 0.5-hectare reserve managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Jackson’s Bank
Description: Jackson’s Bank is a community woodland near Swadlincote within the National Forest, featuring mixed broadleaf trees and a network of footpaths. The site offers opportunities for local residents and visitors to explore nature and enjoy woodland walks, supporting local biodiversity.

Name: Jackson's Coppice and Marsh
Description: Jackson's Coppice and Marsh is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust.  It is along the River Sow, near the village of Bishop's Offley and about 2.

Name: Jeskyns Community Woodland
Description: Jeskyns Community Woodland spans 360 acres near Cobham, Kent, featuring new and established woodlands, meadows, and ponds. Owned and operated by Forestry England, it offers trails, play areas, and a cafe. This diverse site provides habitats for varied wildlife.

Name: Joe's Pond
Description: Joe's Pond is a 4-hectare Site of Special Scientific Interest that lies to the east of, and adjacent to, the Rainton Meadows nature reserve in Tyne and Wear, England.

Name: John Weston Nature Reserve
Description: John Weston Nature Reserve is a 3.6-hectare nature reserve north of Walton-on-the-Naze in Essex.

Name: Johnny Wood, Borrowdale
Description: Johnny Wood in Borrowdale, Lake District, features ancient Atlantic oak woodland. A designated Site of Special Scientific Interest, it supports diverse plant and animal life. The wood lies on the banks of the River Derwent.

Name: Jones's Mill
Description: Jones's Mill is an 11.6 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Pewsey in Wiltshire, notified in 1975.

Name: Kearney Village & Coast
Description: Kearney Village, Ards Peninsula, Northern Ireland, is a National Trust site. It preserves a traditional Ulster fishing community. Whitewashed cottages, a harbour, coastal paths, wildlife, and sea views.

Name: Kedington Meadow
Description: Kedington Meadow is a species-rich grassland near Kedington in Suffolk, managed for its wildflowers and insects. Traditional hay cutting and grazing maintain this vital habitat. The reserve offers an important green space for local wildlife.

Name: Kedleston Hall
Description: Kedleston Hall, an 18th-century mansion near Derby, sits amidst historic parkland. Designed by Robert Adam and Matthew Brettingham, the estate features a large serpentine lake and ancient trees, supporting diverse wildlife.

Name: Kelham Bridge
Description: Kelham Bridge is a 8.1 hectares nature reserve north of Ibstock in Leicestershire.

Name: Kemsing Down
Description: Kemsing Down is a 16-hectare nature reserve north of Sevenoaks in Kent.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Ken-Dee Marshes
Description: Ken-Dee Marshes is an RSPB nature reserve in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland. It features a mosaic of wetlands, woodlands, and grasslands, supporting ospreys, red kites, and other diverse wildlife. The site offers trails and hides for visitors.

Name: Kenley Common
Description: Kenley Common is a 55-hectare site in Croydon, South London. It features chalk grassland, ancient woodland, and neutral grassland, offering extensive views and supporting diverse wildlife. The common includes elements of the historic Kenley Airfield.

Name: Kennet and Avon Canal
Description: The Kennet and Avon Canal is a waterway in southern England with an overall length of 87 miles, made up of two lengths of navigable river linked by a canal.  The name is used to refer to the entire length of the navigation rather than solely to the central canal section.

Name: Kensington Gardens - The Long Water
Description: The Long Water in Kensington Gardens, shared with Hyde Park, serves as a significant bird sanctuary. It provides a haven for diverse waterfowl species including mute swans, greylag geese, and tufted ducks, supporting local wildlife populations.

Name: Kersal Dale
Description: Kersal Dale is a local nature reserve in Salford, part of the Irwell Valley. It features diverse habitats including woodlands, grasslands, and wetlands, supporting a variety of wildlife. The site is popular for walks and nature observation.

Name: Ketford Bank
Description: Ketford Bank is a 0.69-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: Ketton Quarry
Description: Ketton Quarries is a 115.6-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Ketton in Rutland.

Name: Kielder Water & Forest Park
Description: Kielder Water & Forest Park, Northumberland, hosts northern Europe's largest man-made lake and England's biggest forest. This 250 sq mile park offers walking, cycling, water sports, and vital habitats for red squirrels and ospreys. It is famed for its dark skies.

Name: Killaloo Wood
Description: Killaloo Wood is a mature broadleaved woodland near Derry. It features a circular path, offering views of the Sperrin Mountains and the River Faughan. Species include oak, ash, and hazel, with a diverse ground flora.

Name: Killerton Estate
Description: Killerton Estate in Devon features an 18th-century house, extensive garden, and parkland. It encompasses woodlands and is an active site for large-scale tree planting and conservation efforts, supporting local biodiversity.

Name: Killiecrankie
Description: Killiecrankie is a dramatic wooded gorge in Perthshire, Scotland, famed for spectacular autumnal colours. It features the 'Soldier's Leap' viewpoint over the River Garry, offering diverse walking trails and habitats for wildlife.

Name: Kilminorth Woods
Description: Kilminorth Woods, an ancient woodland owned by Cornwall Council, is a designated Local Nature Reserve and County Wildlife Site by the West Looe River in Cornwall. It hosts diverse flora like wild garlic and bluebells, alongside fauna such as bats, otters, roe deer, foxes, and badgers. Well-maintained walking trails provide access to the Looe Valley Line.

Name: Kiln Wood
Description: Kiln Wood is a 6-hectare nature reserve south of Lenham in Kent.  It is managed by Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Kinclaven Bluebell Wood
Description: Kinclaven Bluebell Wood, Perthshire, Scotland, is an ancient woodland known for its stunning bluebell displays each spring. It features native trees like oak and birch, supporting diverse wildlife. Managed by the Woodland Trust, the site offers walking routes.

Name: Kinder Scout
Description: Kinder Scout is a moorland plateau and the highest point in the Peak District, managed by the National Trust. Famous for the 1932 Mass Trespass, it offers challenging walking trails across peat bogs and gritstone edges. The estate focuses on landscape conservation and rewilding efforts.

Name: Kinder Scout
Description: Kinder Scout, an iconic plateau in the Peak District, is subject to extensive peatland restoration and rewilding. This work improves biodiversity, water quality, and carbon sequestration. The National Trust manages public access and conservation efforts.

Name: King's Meads
Description: King's Meads is a nature reserve between the towns of Hertford and Ware in Hertfordshire.  It is managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust, and with an area of 96 hectares it is the largest of the Trust's reserves.

Name: King's Wood, Challock
Description: King's Wood, near Challock in Kent, features diverse woodlands, open spaces, and ancient trees. It provides walking, cycling, and horse riding trails through a varied landscape, including a Sculpture Trail. The site is managed for both recreation and biodiversity.

Name: Kings Wood, Mendips
Description: Kings Wood, near Winscombe, is an ancient woodland and part of the Mendip Hills, once a medieval 'royal hunting forest'. It is owned by the National Trust and forms part of the Crook Peak to Shute Shelve Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). The wood features a diverse range of tree species, including oak, ash, and hazel, supporting varied wildlife and rich ground flora. Footpaths allow public access for walking and nature observation.

Name: Kingston Lacy Estate
Description: Kingston Lacy is an elegant country mansion set in 8,500 acres of estate. The property features formal gardens, parkland, and a diverse heathland habitat. The estate is home to significant biodiversity, including rare plants and wildlife.

Name: Kintail & Morvich
Description: Kintail, on Scotland's west coast, encompasses dramatic mountains, lochs, and glens, including the Five Sisters of Kintail. This wild land offers challenging walking routes and diverse wildlife. Morvich provides a ranger centre and accessible trails, supporting conservation efforts.

Name: Kintbury Newt Ponds
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Kintbury Newt Ponds is a 3-hectare nature reserve in Kintbury in Berkshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Kinver Edge & the Rock Houses
Description: Kinver Edge is an escarpment of Triassic sandstone. The Rock Houses are dwellings carved into the sandstone cliff, inhabited until the 1960s. The site offers views across Worcestershire and the Black Country. Woodland and heathland are present.

Name: Kirkby Moor
Description: Kirkby Moor is an elevated area of lowland heath, woodland and farmland in central Lincolnshire between the villages of Woodhall Spa to the west and Kirkby on Bain to the east.  Roughton Moor lies to the north and the former RAF Woodhall Spa and the Lincolnshire Fens beyond to the south.

Name: Kitchen Copse
Description: Kitchen Copse is a 7-hectare nature reserve north of Bletchingley in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Kiveton Community Woodland
Description: Kiveton Community Woodland, a former colliery, now provides varied woodland, ponds, meadows, and paths near Kiveton Park, Sheffield. TCV South Yorkshire manages the site, offering regular volunteering opportunities for habitat creation and woodland management.

Name: Knapdale
Description: Knapdale Forest, in Argyll, Scotland, hosts a pioneering beaver reintroduction project. Visitors can explore ancient woodlands, temperate rainforest remnants, and lochside trails. The area is rich in biodiversity, offering numerous walking opportunities through diverse habitats.

Name: Knapdale Beaver Trail
Description: Knapdale Forest is a key site for the Scottish Beaver Trial, featuring walking trails around lochs such as Loch Coille Bharr and Dubh Loch, offering views of beaver activity and their impact on the landscape. The main visitor infrastructure is located at Barnluasgan, which includes an accessible hide, car park, and information panels detailing the species' reintroduction. The area is managed by Forestry and Land Scotland.

Name: Knapdale Forest
Description: Knapdale Forest, a National Nature Reserve in Argyll, Scotland, hosts the Scottish Beaver Reintroduction Project. The site's diverse woodlands and lochs allow visitors to explore trails and observe beaver activity and environmental impact.

Name: Knettishall Heath
Description: Knettishall Heath is a 91.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Knettishall in Suffolk, England.

Name: Knighton Down
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 15 hectares.

Name: Knightshayes
Description: Knightshayes features a Victorian country house and extensive gardens with rare plants. Visitors can explore parkland, ancient woodland, and scenic walks. The estate offers views over the Exe Valley, conserving diverse habitats and historic landscapes in Devon.

Name: Kynance Cove
Description: Kynance Cove is a stunning cove on the Lizard Peninsula, famous for its turquoise waters, white sand, and unique serpentine rock formations. Managed by the National Trust, it features an iconic tidal island, Asparagus Island, and offers dramatic coastal walks.

Name: Lackford Lakes
Description: Lackford Lakes is a 105.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north and east of Lackford in Suffolk.

Name: Lacock Abbey & Riverside Woods
Description: Lacock Abbey, a former nunnery, features medieval architecture and a Georgian country house. It is the home of photography pioneer William Henry Fox Talbot, with a museum and medieval cloister. Riverside woods and grounds surround the historic Abbey.

Name: Lady's Wood
Description: Lady's Wood is a 7.1-hectare nature reserve west of Upwood in Cambridgeshire.

Name: Ladybelt Country Park
HostOrg: East Carleton and Ketteringham Parish Council
Description: Ladybelt Country Park is an extensive area of parkland and woodland in south-west Norfolk, managed by East Carleton and Ketteringham Parish Council. It is important for its mature trees, including sweet chestnut coppice, and supports a variety of birds and invertebrates. The park offers waymarked routes for enjoyable walks and has a car park.

Name: Ladywalk Nature Reserve
Description: Ladywalk Nature Reserve is a wildlife haven situated in the Tame Valley, near Birmingham, and managed by the West Midland Bird Club. It encompasses diverse habitats including wetlands, pools, and reedbeds, supporting a wide array of bird species, notably wintering Eurasian Bittern. Access to the reserve is restricted to members of the West Midland Bird Club or by permit.

Name: Ladywalk Reserve
Description: Ladywalk Reserve, a 51-hectare nature reserve in Warwickshire's Tame Valley, is managed by the West Midland Bird Club. It features diverse habitats like pools, marshland, and reedbeds, supporting a variety of bird species. Hides offer viewing access.

Name: Ladywell Fields
Description: Ladywell Fields features over 1000m of river restoration work on the Ravensbourne, including naturalisation and new backwater channels. This increases biodiversity by creating habitats for fish, invertebrates, and plants. Volunteers maintain the river and its banks.

Name: Lambert's Castle & Coney's Castle
Description: Lambert's Castle and Coney's Castle are Iron Age hill forts near Marshwood Vale in Dorset. Lambert's offers panoramic views of Lyme Bay. Coney's is a Scheduled Monument. Managed by the National Trust, the site provides walking and nature enjoyment.

Name: Landford Bog
Description: Landford Bog is an 11.6 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest at Landford in southeast Wiltshire, England.

Name: Lang Craigs
Description: Lang Craigs is a Woodland Trust site within the Kilpatrick Hills, featuring ancient oakwoods, grassland, and newly planted areas. It offers a network of paths with views over the Clyde and Dumbarton Rock, providing accessible walks for wildlife enthusiasts.

Name: Langdale Forest
Description: Langdale Forest, near Pickering, is a working forest on the edge of the North York Moors National Park. It offers marked walking and cycling routes suitable for various abilities. The forest actively produces timber, contributing to local industry and woodland management.

Name: Langdon Nature Reserve
Description: Langdon Nature Reserve is a 210 hectare nature reserve west of Basildon in Essex.  It is managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust, and forms part of the Langdon Ridge Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Langford Heathfield
Description: Langford Heathfield is a 95.4 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest at Langford Budville, 3 km north west of Wellington in Somerset, notified in 1966.

Name: Langstone Harbour
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Langstone Harbour is a 2,085.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Hampshire.

Name: Lanhydrock Parkland & Woods
Description: Lanhydrock is a grand Victorian country house, gardens, and wooded estate in Cornwall. The gardens feature colourful parterres and borders. Extensive parkland offers walking and cycling trails through ancient woodlands and the River Fowey valley.

Name: Lanhydrock Woods
Description: Lanhydrock Woods, part of the National Trust's Lanhydrock Estate, is situated in the Glynn Valley near Bodmin, Cornwall. The extensive woodlands feature diverse native trees like oak, ash, and hazel, offering varied habitats for wildlife. Visitors can explore numerous walking and cycling trails, including paths along the River Fowey.

Name: Lardon Chase
Description: Lardon Chase is a chalk grassland nature reserve near Streatley, Berkshire, offering expansive views over the Thames Valley. The site supports a rich diversity of wildflowers, including orchids, and numerous insect species like butterflies and moths.

Name: Lashford Lane Fen
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Lashford Lane Fen is a 7-hectare nature reserve north of Dry Sandford in Oxfordshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lassington Wood
HostOrg: Tewkesbury Borough Council and Highnam Parish Council
Description: Lassington Wood is a mature, mixed woodland nature reserve near Highnam, Gloucestershire. Historically part of the Guise family estate since the 13th century, it was acquired by Gloucester County Borough Council in 1921. It is now managed jointly by Tewkesbury Borough Council and Highnam Parish Council. The wood is renowned for its spectacular display of bluebells in spring and features a network of public footpaths. It was also formerly home to the notable Lassington Oak.

Name: Launde Woods
Description: Launde Woods is a 99 hectares nature reserve north of Launde in Leicestershire.  It is owned by the Leicester Diocesan Board of Finance and leased to the Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lavender Pond Nature Park
Description: Lavender Pond Nature Park, part of Russia Dock Woodlands in Rotherhithe, Southwark, is a peaceful oasis, formerly a working dock. It features woodland, meadows, and ponds, providing vital habitats for diverse wildlife. Conservation tasks and wildlife surveys occur regularly.

Name: Lavenham Guildhall
Description: Lavenham Guildhall, a 1530 timber-framed building, showcases the village's rich history, including its wool trade prominence, its uses as a prison and workhouse, and local heritage exhibitions. The site also provides access to various countryside walks in and around Lavenham.

Name: Lavenham Woodland
Description: Lavenham Woodland refers to the collection of woodlands managed by Forestry England in the Lavenham area of Suffolk. These woodlands offer varied routes for walking, cycling, and horse riding, providing diverse wildlife habitats for visitors to explore.

Name: Lawrence Weston Moor
Description: Lawrence Weston is a post-war housing estate in northwest Bristol, England, between Henbury and Shirehampton.  The estate is bounded in the east by the Blaise Castle estate and woods.

Name: Laymoor Quag
Description: Laymoor Quag is a 3.5-hectare nature reserve within the Forest of Dean in Gloucestershire.

Name: Lea Meadows
Description: Lea Meadows is a 12-hectare nature reserve east of Markfield in Leicestershire.  It is owned and managed by the Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lee Navigation Reedbeds
Description: Lee Navigation Reedbeds, near Tottenham Hale, are artificial floating reedbeds created to improve water quality and increase biodiversity. They provide crucial habitats for wildlife in an urban waterway setting. This project enhances ecological resilience.

Name: Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust
Description: The Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust is one of 46 wildlife trusts across the United Kingdom.  It manages nature reserves in Leicestershire and Rutland, and was founded in 1956 as the Leicestershire and Rutland Trust for Nature Conservation.

Name: Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust
Description: The Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust is one of 46 wildlife trusts across the United Kingdom.  It manages nature reserves in Leicestershire and Rutland, and was founded in 1956 as the Leicestershire and Rutland Trust for Nature Conservation.

Name: Leigh Woods
Description: Leigh Woods is a National Nature Reserve near Bristol, managed by Forestry England. It features ancient woodland, walking and cycling trails, and views of the Avon Gorge. The site is home to diverse wildlife and rare species, designated for its ecological significance.

Name: Leith Hill
Description: Leith Hill is Surrey's highest point, home to Leith Hill Tower, offering panoramic views across the South East. Managed by the National Trust, visitors explore ancient woodlands and footpaths surrounding this popular beauty spot, located within the Surrey Hills AONB.

Name: Lemsford Springs
Description: Lemsford Springs is a 4 hectare nature reserve in Lemsford, Hertfordshire, England.  It is managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust, which purchased the site in 1970.

Name: Letcombe Valley
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Letcombe Valley is a 7.5-hectare nature reserve south of Letcombe Regis in Oxfordshire.

Name: Levant Mine & the Tin Coast
Description: Levant Mine, a Cornish beam engine and a site of a Victorian mining disaster, is part of the Cornish Mining World Heritage Site. Located on the Tin Coast, it offers underground tours and insights into Cornwall's rich mining heritage.

Name: Levin Down
Description: Levin Down is a 25.6-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Midhurst in West Sussex.

Name: Levington Lagoon
Description: Levington Lagoon is a 5 hectare nature reserve south-east of Levington in Suffolk.  It is owned by Suffolk Yacht Harbour Ltd and managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lexden Gathering Grounds
Description: Lexden Gathering Grounds is an 8.9-hectare nature reserve in Lexden, a suburb of Colchester in Essex.

Name: Leyburn Old Glebe
Description: Leyburn Old Glebe Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest managed by the Yorkshire Wildlife Trust.  It is about 440 yards east of the village of Wensley and 0.

Name: Leyton Jubilee Park
Description: Leyton Jubilee Park hosts the Waltham Forest Green Gym, offering weekly conservation tasks. Activities include tree and shrub maintenance, gardening, habitat management, and litter picking, suitable for all abilities.

Name: Lightwater Country Park
Description: Lightwater Country Park, owned by Surrey Heath Borough Council, encompasses heathland, woodland, and grassland. Its heathland sections, part of the Thames Basin Heaths Special Protection Area, protect ground-nesting birds. The site is open to the public.

Name: Ligoniel Dams & Park
Description: Ligoniel Dams and Park is an urban oasis in north Belfast, managed by the Belfast Hills Partnership. Two man-made dams, fed by the Ligoneil River, support waterbirds and amphibians. Walking paths explore former printworks and mill race remains.

Name: Limekiln Wood Nature Reserve
Description: Limekiln Wood Nature Reserve is a 13.1-hectare nature reserve in Cheshire, England, north of the village of Mow Cop.

Name: Lincomb Fish Pass
Description: Lincomb Fish Pass, near Stourport-on-Severn on the River Severn, aids migrating fish like salmon and eels in bypassing Lincomb Weir. Part of the Unlocking the Severn project, it uses a Larinier super active baffle design for easier upstream passage.

Name: Lindean Loch
Description: Lindean Loch is a shallow loch in a natural hollow, surrounded by sedge and reed swamp, with open water. It supports diverse bird life, including wildfowl and waders, acting as an important breeding ground. The site is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, with limited visitor access.

Name: Lindisfarne National Nature Reserve
Description: Lindisfarne National Nature Reserve is a 3,541-hectare UK national nature reserve located on Holy Island, a tidal island off the Northumberland coast. Managed by Natural England, it safeguards internationally important wintering bird populations, including pale-bellied brent geese, pink-footed geese, and wigeons. The reserve encompasses diverse habitats such as sand dunes, intertidal mudflats, rocky shores, and salt marshes, making it a Ramsar site of international significance.

Name: Lineover Wood
Description: Lineover Wood is an ancient woodland on the Cotswold scarp, featuring mature beech and ash trees. It is home to diverse wildlife, including various bird species and dormice. The site offers walking trails and scenic views over the surrounding countryside.

Name: Linhope Spout
Description: Linhope Spout is a waterfall located within Northumberland National Park, North East England. It currently hosts a temperate rainforest pilot project. This initiative focuses on restoring and expanding vital rainforest habitats around the spout and the adjacent Bizzle Burn.

Name: Linn of Tummel
Description: The Linn of Tummel is a stunning natural waterfall and gorge located where the rivers Tummel and Garry meet in Perthshire. Ancient woodlands and rich wildlife surround tranquil pools and cascades. Historic bridges cross the river, offering scenic viewpoints.

Name: Lion Creek and Lower Raypits
Description: Lion Creek and Lower Raypits is a 65.2-hectare nature reserve east of Canewdon in Essex.

Name: Lion Pit
Description: Lion Pit is a 2.5-hectare geological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Grays in Essex.

Name: Lippets Grove
Description: Lippets Grove is a 5-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.  The site was leased from the Forestry Commission in 1987 and is managed by the Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Little Dartmouth & Coast
Description: Little Dartmouth offers dramatic clifftop walks with views of Dartmouth Castle, Start Bay, and the coastline. It features diverse habitats, including woodland and coastal paths, supporting varied wildlife. This section of the South West Coast Path is popular for walkers.

Name: Little Haven
Description: Little Haven is a 37.2-hectare nature reserve in Thundersley in Essex, England.

Name: Little Linford Wood
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Little Linford Wood is a 42.5-hectare nature reserve in Little Linford in the City of Milton Keynes, Buckinghamshire, England.

Name: Little Waltham Meadows
Description: Little Waltham Meadows is an 8.9-hectare nature reserve south of Little Waltham in Essex.

Name: Littlefield Common
Description: Littlefield Common is a 17-hectare nature reserve south-west of Worplesdon in Surrey.  It is owned by Surrey County Council and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lizard Point & Bass Point
Description: Lizard Point, the UK's most southerly mainland point, and Bass Point are dramatic headlands on Cornwall's coast. The area features rugged cliffs, rare flora, and diverse marine wildlife, including choughs. Visitors explore coves and walk scenic coastal paths.

Name: Llanerchaeron
Description: Llanerchaeron is a Georgian villa, farm, and walled garden near Aberaeron, Ceredigion, West Wales. This largely unaltered 18th-century estate features traditional Welsh livestock and showcases historic self-sufficiency. It offers a glimpse into rural life.

Name: Lloyd Park
Description: Lloyd Park in Walthamstow, London, is a Green Flag Award-winning park and a designated Local Wildlife Site, featuring woodland, a medieval ornamental moat, and diverse habitats supporting birds and bats. The TCV (The Conservation Volunteers) Green Gym meets weekly here, engaging volunteers in practical conservation tasks such as tree planting, wildflower meadow maintenance, wetland management, and habitat creation, offering free outdoor exercise and contributing to the park's biodiversity.

Name: Llyn Tegid (Bala Lake)
Description: Llyn Tegid (Bala Lake) is Wales' largest natural lake, found within Snowdonia National Park, Gwynedd. This glacial lake is a Special Area of Conservation, known for its clear waters and rare gwyniad fish, supporting diverse habitats.

Name: Llyn Tegid NNR
Description: Llyn Tegid (Bala Lake) is Wales’ largest natural lake. A National Nature Reserve (NNR) protecting rare wildlife like the gwyniad fish, it is popular for water sports, walking, and its scenic railway.

Name: Llyn y Fan Fach
Description: Llyn y Fan Fach is a stunning glacial lake on Mynydd Du, within Bannau Brycheiniog National Park. It is considered the southernmost montane lake in the UK, surrounded by moorland and home to unique aquatic flora and fauna. The site supports important bird species.

Name: Loch Arkaig Pine Forest
Description: Loch Arkaig Pine Forest is a surviving fragment of ancient Caledonian Forest in the Scottish Highlands. The site features ancient Scots pine, hosting diverse wildlife including red squirrels, pine martens, and ospreys. Woodland Trust and Arkaig Community Forest manage the area for conservation.

Name: Loch Fleet
Description: Loch Fleet is a large, shallow, tidal basin and National Nature Reserve in Sutherland, Scotland. The site features saltmarsh, dunes, coastal heath, and pine woods. It provides habitat for wading birds, wildfowl, otters, seals, and ospreys.

Name: Loch Garten Nature Centre
Description: Loch Garten Nature Centre is within RSPB Abernethy, a significant Caledonian pinewood in the Cairngorms National Park. It is renowned for returning ospreys, red squirrels, capercaillie, and crested tits, offering visitor viewing facilities.

Name: Loch Gruinart
Description: Loch Gruinart is an RSPB nature reserve on Islay, known for its diverse birdlife including wintering barnacle geese. The reserve features wetlands, woodlands, and farmland habitats, offering hides for wildlife viewing and marked walking trails.

Name: Loch Leven National Nature Reserve
Description: Loch Leven NNR, a freshwater loch in Perth and Kinross, Scotland, is a vital wintering ground and breeding site for wildfowl and birds. It serves as a crucial migratory stopover for many bird populations. NatureScot manages this important wetland.

Name: Loch Lomond
Description: RSPB Loch Lomond reserve protects vital habitats on Scotland's largest freshwater loch. It supports diverse wildlife, including geese, ducks, and waders. Visitors can explore trails, hides, and learn about conservation at the Nature Hub.

Name: Loch of Kinnordy
HostOrg: Royal Society for the Protection of Birds
Description: Loch of Kinnordy is a shallow freshwater loch and fen wetland in Strathmore, Scotland. It supports breeding and wintering wildfowl and waders like osprey, pintail, and whooper swans. The fen and reedbeds provide habitat for rare plants and insects.

Name: Loch of Spiggie
Description: Loch of Spiggie is a large freshwater loch in south-west Mainland Shetland. It is important for wintering wildfowl, including wigeon, teal, mallard, pintail, tufted duck, pochard, and whooper swans. Surrounding habitats feature reedbeds and fen areas. The site is notable for great northern divers and Slavonian grebes, managed by RSPB.

Name: Loch of Strathbeg
Description: Loch of Strathbeg is Scotland's largest coastal wetland, situated in Aberdeenshire. It serves as a crucial wintering ground for thousands of migrating wildfowl, including geese, swans, and ducks. The reserve features diverse habitats like reeds, dunes, and farmland.

Name: Loch of the Lowes
Description: Loch of the Lowes is a loch near Dunkeld in Perth and Kinross, Scotland.  The loch and the surrounding area are designated as a wildlife reserve, run by the Scottish Wildlife Trust.

Name: Loch Ruthven
Description: Loch Ruthven is a remote, tranquil upland freshwater loch in the Scottish Highlands. It hosts over a quarter of the UK's Slavonian grebe population, which breed here each spring before moving to sea for winter. The site is an important habitat for these birds.

Name: Lochwinnoch
Description: RSPB Lochwinnoch is a nature reserve in West Scotland, situated on the shores of Castle Semple Loch. It features open water, reedbed, and wet woodland habitats, supporting diverse wildlife. Visitors can use nature trails, bird hides, and a visitor centre.

Name: Lockerbrook Woodland
Description: Lockerbrook Woodland is a 191-hectare area within the Peak District National Park, managed by Forestry England as part of the Dark Peak Forest Plan. This woodland is actively managed for sustainable timber production, habitat diversification, and the restoration of native clough woodland, contributing to the ecological interest of the Dark Peak area.

Name: Loddon Nature Reserve
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 14 hectares.

Name: Lodge Park & Sherborne Park Estate
Description: Lodge Park, a 17th-century deer course grandstand, stands within Sherborne Park Estate, a significant conservation landscape. This estate features historic parkland and diverse wildlife habitats. Visitors explore the grandstand and enjoy walks through the wider estate, observing nature and architectural heritage.

Name: Loggans Moor
Description: Loggans Moor is a nature reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest, noted for its biological characteristics, in west Cornwall, England, UK.  It is located 1 mile north-east of the town of Hayle, off the A30 road.

Name: Lolly Moor
Description: Lolly Moor is a 3-hectare nature reserve south of Dereham in Norfolk.  It is managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Long Deans
Description: Long Deans is a 15 hectare nature reserve managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust in Nash Mills, between Kings Langley and Hemel Hempstead in Hertfordshire.  It is neutral and chalk grassland and woodland with beech, ash, oak and wild cherry.

Name: Long Dole Wood and Meadows SSSI
Description: Long Dole Wood and Meadows SSSI is a 9.8 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between the villages of Farrington Gurney and Hinton Blewitt in Bath and North East Somerset, notified in 1987.

Name: Long Grove Wood
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Long Grove Wood is a 1.5-hectare nature reserve managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust in Seer Green in Buckinghamshire.

Name: Longburnford Quarry
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 1 hectares.

Name: Longford River, Bushy Park
Description: The Longford River is a man-made watercourse, constructed in the 1630s to supply water to Hampton Court Palace. It flows through Bushy Park, feeding ponds and water gardens before reaching the palace grounds. It supports diverse wildlife and habitats.

Name: Longshaw Estate
Description: Longshaw Estate, located within the Peak District, encompasses diverse moorland, woodland, and parkland environments. It features historic Longshaw Lodge and is a popular destination for walking, nature observation, and family activities. Padley Gorge is a notable feature.

Name: Longspring Wood
Description: Longspring Wood is a 1.2-hectare nature reserve managed by the Herts and Middlesex Wildlife Trust in Kings Langley in Hertfordshire.

Name: Lough Foyle
Description: Lough Foyle is a large, shallow estuary on the border of Northern Ireland, internationally important for wintering wildfowl and wading birds. It provides vital feeding and roosting grounds for species like whooper swans and light-bellied brent geese.

Name: Lough Foyle Native Oyster Recovery
Description: Lough Foyle, Northern Ireland, hosts a native oyster recovery project. It reintroduces oysters to restore populations, enhance marine biodiversity, and improve water quality within the lough's ecosystem, working with local communities.

Name: Loughborough Big Meadow
Description: Loughborough Meadows is a 60.5 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the northern outskirts of Loughborough in Leicestershire, England.

Name: Lound Lakes
Description: Lound Lakes is a 113 hectares nature reserve and series of reservoirs on the border between the English counties of Norfolk and Suffolk.  It is 2 miles south-west of Gorleston-on-Sea, 5 miles north-west of Lowestoft and around 1.

Name: Love Your River Cole
Description: The Love Your River Cole project improves a 2.5km stretch of the River Cole within Birmingham's Kingfisher Country Park, specifically in the Shard End and Stechford areas. It focuses on enhancing river access, boosting biodiversity, and offering community engagement opportunities. The project is managed by the Tame Valley Wetlands Landscape Partnership.

Name: Low Barns
Description: Witton-le-Wear is a Site of Special Scientific Interest located in the valley of the River Wear, immediately east of the village of Witton-le-Wear in County Durham, England.  It is important as the only extensive body of biologically significant open water in West Durham.

Name: Lower Common
Description: Lower Common near Verwood, Dorset, is a 30-hectare nature reserve. It features mixed woodland, coniferous plantations, and wet and dry heathland. The site supports nightjar, woodcock, sand lizard, and smooth snake. Grazing ponies maintain habitats.

Name: Lower East Prawle
Description: Lower East Prawle is a coastal nature reserve near Start Point in South Devon. It features species-rich grassland, ancient hedgerows, and coastal scrub. The site supports various rare invertebrates and is managed for biodiversity.

Name: Lower Lough Erne Islands
Description: Lower Lough Erne Islands, located in County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland, comprise numerous small islands and the mainland site of Hare Island. This site is a stronghold for breeding waders, particularly curlews. Conservation efforts focus on managing grazing and scrub to maintain suitable habitats.

Name: Lower Test
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Lower Test Valley is a 142-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Totton in Hampshire.  It is part of Solent and Southampton Water Ramsar site and Special Protection Area, and of Solent Maritime Special Area of Conservation.

Name: Lower Wood, Ashwellthorpe
Description: Lower Wood, Ashwellthorpe is a 37.9-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of Wymondham in Norfolk, England.

Name: Lower Woods
Description: Lower Woods is a 280.1-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest near the village of Wickwar, South Gloucestershire, notified in 1966 and renotified in 1985.

Name: Lower Wye Gorge SSSI
Description: Lower Wye Gorge is a 65-hectare biological and geological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Gloucestershire, notified in 1954 and renotified 1987.  The site includes two Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust nature reserves being Ban-y-gor Wood and Lancaut.

Name: Loynton Moss
Description: Loynton Moss is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust, near the village of Woodseaves, in Staffordshire, England.  It is adjacent to the Shropshire Union Canal, as it runs from nearby Norbury to High Offley.

Name: Lucas Marsh
Description: Lucas Marsh is a 1.5 hectare Local Nature Reserve in Oadby in Leicestershire.

Name: Ludshott Commons
Description: Ludshott Commons is one of the largest remaining areas of heathland in East Hampshire, known for its diverse habitats supporting rare birds, reptiles, and insects. The site features woodlands, open heath, and ponds, offering extensive walking trails. It is a vital area for biodiversity conservation.

Name: Ludwell Valley Park
Description: Ludwell Valley Park is wildlife-focused public park in Exeter, Devon, United Kingdom.  The park is owned by Exeter City Council and managed by Devon Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lullingstone Country Park
Description: Lullingstone Country Park is a Green Flag award-winning park near Eynsford, Kent. It is internationally important for its collection of ancient trees, including over 300 veteran oak, beech, ash, hornbeam, and sweet chestnut, some estimated to be 800 years old. The park features chalk grasslands with spectacular displays of orchids and other wildflowers, supporting diverse wildlife. The River Darent flows through the park, and the Darent Valley Path offers walking routes and scenic views. It is owned and managed by Kent County Council.

Name: Lullingstone Country Park
Description: Lullingstone Country Park is an internationally important site for its collection of ancient trees, chalk grassland, and diverse wildlife, situated in the Darent Valley. Managed by Kent County Council, the park features varied habitats including woodlands and grasslands, supporting a wide array of flora and fauna.

Name: Lundy Bay
Description: Lundy Bay is a secluded sandy cove on the North Cornwall coast, notable for its dramatic cliffs and unique geological formations. The site, managed by the National Trust, provides access to coastal walks along the South West Coast Path.

Name: Lydden Meadows
Description: Lydden Meadows, also known as RSPB Lydden Valley Reserve or Worth Marshes, is a Kent nature reserve managed by the RSPB. It features damp meadows, ditches, and woodland, with ongoing work to create new scrapes and wetlands. It provides habitat for diverse wildlife, including a nationally important population of the rare marsh fritillary butterfly, waders, and wildfowl. Public access is limited to existing public footpaths.

Name: Lydden Temple Ewell
Description: Lydden and Temple Ewell Downs is a 63.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-west of Dover in Kent.

Name: Lydford Gorge
Description: Lydford Gorge is the deepest gorge in South West England, featuring ancient woodland, dramatic river features, and the impressive 30-metre Whitelady Waterfall. Visitors can explore walking trails through its rich natural landscape.

Name: Lyme
Description: Lyme, a National Trust property in Cheshire, offers a historic house, formal gardens, and a medieval deer park. Located on the edge of the Peak District, it features extensive moorland and parkland for walking and wildlife spotting, including a herd of red deer.

Name: Lyminge Forest
Description: Lyminge Forest lies within the Kent Downs AONB, offering extensive trails for walking, cycling, and horse riding. It features diverse habitats supporting various wildlife species. Forestry England manages the site for public enjoyment and conservation.

Name: Lymington and Keyhaven Marshes
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Lymington and Keyhaven Marshes is a 738-hectare nature reserve which stretches from Keyhaven along the south coast across the Lymington River in Hampshire.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Lymington Reedbeds
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Lymington River Reedbeds is a 41.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Lymington in Hampshire.

Name: Lynford Arboretum and Water Garden
Description: Lynford Arboretum features a diverse collection of trees, a picturesque water garden, and walking trails. It provides habitat for various bird species, including rare raptors. Visitors can explore a sensory garden and observe wildlife.

Name: Mab Lane Community Woodland
Description: Mab Lane Community Woodland is a 1.5-hectare site in Liverpool, established around 2008-2010 as part of Liverpool's Capital of Culture year. It features native trees and shrubs, wildflower meadows, a community orchard, and seasonal wetland areas, creating valuable wildlife habitats. The woodland offers walking paths and green space for local residents to enjoy nature and was developed through a partnership including The Mersey Forest and Woodland Trust.

Name: Macclesfield Forest
Description: Macclesfield Forest is an upland woodland and reservoir complex on the western edge of the Peak District, Cheshire. Owned and primarily managed by United Utilities, with a section including Trentabank Reservoir managed as a nature reserve by Cheshire Wildlife Trust, it features diverse habitats including conifer plantations and broadleaf woodlands, supporting varied wildlife such as red deer and a large heronry.

Name: Maer Lake
Description: Maer Lake is a nature reserve adjacent to Bude, in Cornwall, England.  It is a wetland meadow with open water, and is an important site for over-wintering birds.

Name: Magog Down
Description: Magog Down is 163.5 acres of former arable land on the Gog Magog Hills, south of Cambridge. Transformed since 1989, it is now a habitat for wildlife, supports species diversity, and offers quiet recreation and educational visits.

Name: Magor Marsh
Description: Magor Marsh is a 36-hectare wetland reserve, located on the Welsh side of the Severn Estuary.  It is managed by the Gwent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Maidenhead Thicket
Description: Maidenhead Thicket is an ancient woodland and common near Maidenhead, Berkshire, managed by the National Trust. It features diverse habitats including mature trees, heathland, and ponds, supporting varied wildlife. Public footpaths offer walking and nature observation opportunities.

Name: Maldon Wick
Description: Maldon Wick is a 6.1-hectare nature reserve in Maldon in Essex.

Name: Malham Tarn Estate
Description: Malham Tarn Estate, within the Yorkshire Dales National Park, encompasses a high-altitude lake. This National Nature Reserve hosts diverse habitats, including fen, woodland, grassland, and limestone pavement, supporting unique wildlife.

Name: Mallards Pike - Forest of Dean
Description: Mallards Pike is a popular recreation site within the Forest of Dean, Gloucestershire. It features a large lake, walking trails, cycle routes, and a cafe. Activities include paddleboarding, kayaking, and archery. Go Ape offers treetop adventures.

Name: Malling Down
Description: Malling Down is an 85-hectare nature reserve on the eastern outskirts of Lewes in East Sussex.  It is managed by the Sussex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Malton NR
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 5 hectares.

Name: Manesty Woods
Description: Manesty Woods is a key wet woodland habitat within Borrowdale, forming part of a wider project aimed at restoring and protecting these unique ecosystems. It supports a diverse range of plants, mosses, fungi, and invertebrates in the Lake District.

Name: Manor Farm
Description: Manor Farm is a 25-hectare nature reserve in Byfleet, Surrey.  It is owned and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Mapledurwell Fen and the Hatch
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 3 hectares.

Name: Mar Lodge Estate NNR
Description: Mar Lodge Estate National Nature Reserve is a vast wilderness covering over 7% of the Cairngorms National Park. It features four of the five highest mountains in the UK and Caledonian pine forest. The estate encompasses wild land and habitats.

Name: Marbury Reedbed Nature Reserve
Description: Marbury Reedbed Nature Reserve is a 6-hectare nature reserve located at the western end of Budworth Mere, north of Northwich, Cheshire, England.  It is managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust under lease from the Royal Society for Nature Conservation, which purchased the land by public subscription in 1934 as a memorial to the Cheshire naturalist Thomas Coward.

Name: March Haigh
Description: March Haigh is a key component of the Landscapes for Water project on Marsden Moor. This initiative aims to restore peatlands to natural conditions, improving water quality and increasing biodiversity. The project reduces flood risk and enhances carbon capture, supporting local ecosystems.

Name: Marden Meadow
