Description: Ancient woodland and former parkland trees on clay soil near Swineshead. This site features a rich mix of ash, oak, and field maple, supporting diverse flora and fauna. Maintained by the Woodland Trust for public access and wildlife.

Name: Swinley Forest
Description: Swinley Forest, a Crown Estate woodland in Berkshire, is managed by Forestry England. It offers extensive trails for walking, cycling, and horse riding, and is known for its mountain biking routes. The forest spans 2,600 acres.

Name: Swithland Wood
Description: Swithland Wood is a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a recently designated National Nature Reserve (NNR) in Leicestershire, East Midlands. This ancient woodland features historic slate quarries and diverse ecosystems. Owned and managed by Bradgate Park Trust, it offers significant habitats for wildlife and is popular for walks.

Name: Sydenham Hill Wood and Cox's Walk
Description: Sydenham Hill Wood is a ten-hectare wood on the northern slopes of the Norwood Ridge in the London Borough of Southwark.  It is designated as a Local Nature Reserve and Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation.

Name: Syderstone Common
Description: Syderstone Common is a 43.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Fakenham in Norfolk, England.

Name: Sydlings Copse
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 22 hectares.

Name: Sylvia's Meadow
Description: Sylvia's Meadow is a nature reserve and a Site of Special Scientific Interest owned and managed by Cornwall Wildlife Trust.  It is a herb rich, 5-hectare site situated near Gunnislake, in East Cornwall, England.

Name: Sywell Country Park
Description: Sywell Country Park is a Green Flag Award winning site in Northamptonshire. Built around a former Victorian reservoir, it provides habitat for diverse wildlife, including overwintering wildfowl. The park offers walking trails, bird hides, a play area, and a cafe for visitors.

Name: Talybont Reservoir
Description: Talybont Reservoir, located in the Brecon Beacons National Park, is a significant water body within the Usk catchment. Designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a local nature reserve, it is central to conservation efforts and supports various wildlife habitats, particularly important for wintering wildfowl and passage migrants. Welsh Wildlife Trust collaborates with Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water on catchment partnership initiatives here, focusing on nature-based solutions and biodiversity enhancement.

Name: Tame Valley Canal
Description: The Tame Valley Canal is an 8.5-mile green corridor in Birmingham, connecting to the national canal network. It traverses industrial landscapes, offering walking and cycling routes, and is a significant wildlife haven within an urban setting.

Name: Tandle Hill Country Park
Description: Tandle Hill Country Park in Oldham covers 110 acres of woodland and grassland, offering panoramic views across the Manchester Plain and Pennine Hills. The park features a children's play area, cafe, and picnic spots.

Name: Tardebigge Reservoir
Description: Tardebigge Reservoir is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in Worcestershire, England. It serves as a feeder reservoir for the Worcester and Birmingham Canal, supporting diverse wetland habitats and birdlife. The area offers opportunities for walking and wildlife observation.

Name: Tarr Steps
Description: Tarr Steps features an ancient clapper bridge crossing the River Barle, set within Exmoor's Tarr Steps Woodland National Nature Reserve. The reserve is owned and managed by the Exmoor National Park Authority, offering diverse wildlife habitats and scenic riverside walks.

Name: Tattershall Castle
Description: Tattershall Castle is a significant red-brick castle built for Ralph Cromwell in the 15th century. It stands in Lincolnshire, featuring a tower with multiple floors and grand fireplaces. Visitors can explore its architecture and history, set within grounds near the Fenland.

Name: Teal Lough NNR
Description: Teal Lough NNR is a lowland raised bog in County Londonderry/Tyrone, Northern Ireland, within the Teal Lough Special Area of Conservation (SAC) and Teal Lough and Slaghtfreeden Bogs Area of Special Scientific Interest (ASSI). It is valued for its unique biodiversity and significant peatland features, representing a crucial conservation area for this rare habitat, and is part of the wider Sperrins Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB).

Name: Tees-Swale: Naturally Connected
Description: Tees-Swale: Naturally Connected is a landscape initiative in the North Pennines AONB. It focuses on restoring and connecting habitats, including peatlands and river systems across the Tees and Swale catchments, enhancing biodiversity and water quality.

Name: Teignmouth & Shaldon Coast
Description: The Teignmouth & Shaldon Coast in South Devon offers coastal walks with views of the Teign Estuary and historic ports. Diverse habitats include saltmarsh and cliffs. Visitors can explore local beaches and learn about the area's natural history.

Name: Telegraph Hill, Hertfordshire
Description: Telegraph Hill is a nature reserve near Lilley in north Hertfordshire.  It is in the Chilterns Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Name: Tentsmuir Point NNR
Description: Tentsmuir Point NNR, on the North East Fife coast, features sand dunes, woodlands, and intertidal habitats. This dynamic landscape is home to seals, migratory birds, and diverse plant life. Visitors can enjoy walks and observe wildlife.

Name: Terrace Meadows SNCI
Description: Terrace Meadows SNCI, a traditional hay meadow in Sherborne, is managed to protect and enhance its rich biodiversity. This Site of Nature Conservation Interest provides important habitat for wildflowers, grasses, and invertebrates. It offers public open space for local residents.

Name: Testwood Lakes
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Testwood Lakes is a 55-hectare nature reserve in Totton to the northwest of Southampton in Hampshire, England.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Tewin Orchard and Hopkyns Wood
Description: Tewin Orchard and Hopkyns Wood is a 4.3-hectare nature reserve in Tewin in Hertfordshire.

Name: Tewinbury
Description: Tewinbury is a 7.5-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near Tewin in Hertfordshire.

Name: Thames Barrier Park
Description: Thames Barrier Park in East London offers landscaped gardens, a rose garden, and wildflower areas providing important urban habitats. It features fountains, a children's play area, and views of the iconic Thames Barrier.

Name: Thames Chase Community Forest
Description: Thames Chase Community Forest spans east London and south Essex. This community forest features woodlands, parks, and open spaces, offering a range of recreational activities. The forest centre provides information, a shop, and a café.

Name: Thames Road Wetland
Description: Thames Road Wetland is a constructed wetland in Crayford, Bexley, filtering surface water before it enters the River Cray. Managed by Thames21, it improves water quality and provides vital habitat for local wildlife. The site helps mitigate pollution impacts on the river system.

Name: Thatcham Reed Beds
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Thatcham Reed Beds is a 67.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Newbury in Berkshire.

Name: The Argory
Description: The Argory is a neo-classical house and 320-acre wooded riverside estate in County Armagh, Northern Ireland. It features an original gas-lighting system, stable yard, and a scenic garden overlooking the River Blackwater.

Name: The Carbon Landscape
Description: Risley Moss Nature Reserve is a significant lowland raised bog and wetland site in Warrington, managed by Warrington Borough Council. It is a Local Nature Reserve, Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), and Special Area of Conservation (SAC), forming a key part of The Carbon Landscape partnership programme. The reserve is vital for biodiversity, carbon capture, and connecting communities with nature in a historically industrial landscape.

Name: The Carrifran Wildwood
Description: The Carrifran Wildwood is a rewilding project in the Southern Uplands of Scotland, managed by Borders Forest Trust. Since 2000, over 600,000 native trees have been planted, restoring woodland and associated habitats. The site focuses on ecological restoration and biodiversity.

Name: The Crumbles
Description: The Crumbles, near Eastbourne, is a unique shingle beach and vegetated ridge formed by coastal processes. Located in East Sussex, it supports a distinctive range of coastal plants and invertebrates, part of the Eastbourne Coastal Local Nature Reserve.

Name: The Dark Peak
Description: The Dark Peak is a rugged moorland landscape within the Peak District, managed by the National Trust. It features extensive peat bogs and heather, vital for carbon storage and flood management. Conservation efforts focus on restoring these habitats, supporting wildlife like mountain hares.

Name: The Ercall
Description: The Ercall is a small hill in Shropshire, England, between The Wrekin and Wellington.  It is an internationally important geological site, part of The Wrekin and The Ercall Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: The Farne Islands NNR
Description: The Farne Islands NNR, off the Northumberland coast, hosts tens of thousands of seabirds, including puffins, and a large grey seal colony. Visitors take boat trips to observe wildlife and the historic lighthouse. Managed by the National Trust.

Name: The Flit
Description: The Flits is a National Nature Reserve in Herefordshire, an area of low-lying grassland, fen, scrub, and woodland on peaty soils within the floodplain of the River Wye. It is notable for its diverse invertebrate community, including many rare flies, spiders, and beetles, as well as numerous butterfly and moth species. While public access is permitted for quiet enjoyment, there are no waymarked trails.

Name: The Forest and the Highlands
Description: The Forest and the Highlands is a 29.74-hectare nature reserve north of East Horsley in Surrey.

Name: The Gill
Description: The Gill is a 12-hectare nature reserve north of Goudhurst in Kent, England.  It is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: The Great Canal Orchard
Description: The Great Canal Orchard in Wolverhampton is a community green space managed by the Canal & River Trust. It features various fruit trees, providing fresh produce for local communities and hosting events. The site is situated along the canal network.

Name: The Great North Bog
Description: The Great North Bog protects 92% of England's upland peat, spanning 7000 sq km across Northern England. This initiative restores degraded peatlands, vital for carbon storage, biodiversity, and water quality.

Name: The Green Park
Description: The Green Park covers 40 acres of mature grassland and trees in central London. Located between Buckingham Palace and Piccadilly, it provides a tranquil, open space popular for relaxation. Part of the Royal Parks, it is a significant green lung for the city.

Name: The Growing Space
Description: The Growing Space is a community garden in Wincanton, Somerset, offering a welcoming environment for local people. It provides opportunities to learn gardening skills, connect with nature, and improve wellbeing. Produce is utilised by the Balsam Centre cafe and distributed within the local community.

Name: The Hudnalls
Description: The Hudnalls is an ancient woodland reserve within the Wye Valley Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, Gloucestershire, representing a vital fragment of the Atlantic rainforest. It is globally significant for its rich lichen, moss, and fern communities, supporting diverse woodland birds and wildlife. The site's varied terrain slopes towards the River Wye.

Name: The Larches
Description: The Larches is a 25-hectare nature reserve north of Detling, which is north of Maidstone in Kent.  It is managed by Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: The Lizard Wildlife Watchpoint
Description: The Lizard Wildlife Watchpoint offers panoramic views of the coast and sea from mainland Britain's southernmost tip. It is a prime location for observing marine life and diverse bird species.

Name: The Loons and Loch of Banks
Description: The Loons and Loch of Banks is a significant wetland on the Orkney mainland. It features wet grassland, reedbeds, and open water, providing habitat for breeding waders and wintering ducks and geese. It is the largest remaining wetland of its type in Orkney.

Name: The Mens
Description: The Mens is a 205.2-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Billingshurst in West Sussex.

Name: The Mere, Ellesmere
HostOrg: Shropshire Council / The Mere Charitable Trust
Description: The Mere at Ellesmere is a glacial lake in Shropshire, forming part of the Shropshire Meres and Mosses Ramsar site. It comprises open water, reedbeds, and woodland habitats, supporting diverse wildlife. The site is popular for walks and wildlife observation.

Name: The Naze
Description: The Naze Nature Reserve is a 45 hectare nature reserve on The Naze peninsula north of Walton-on-the-Naze in Essex.  It is managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust,.

Name: The Park, University of Gloucestershire
Description: The Park, University of Gloucestershire is a 9.5-hectare community green space in Cheltenham, Gloucestershire.

Name: The Pennings
Description: The Pennings is a wet grassland site bordering the River Dove in Suffolk. Historically managed as hay meadow, it features reedbed, fen, and wet woodland. The site supports rich plant and invertebrate life.

Name: The Regent's Park Wildlife Garden & West Pond
Description: Regent's Park hosts a dedicated Wildlife Garden, fostering diverse flora and fauna within London. The park also features the West Pond, an important habitat for aquatic life and birds, contributing to urban biodiversity. It serves as a green sanctuary.

Name: The Sill: National Landscape Discovery Centre
Description: The Sill is an award-winning visitor centre and youth hostel, providing a gateway to Northumberland National Park and Hadrian's Wall. It offers exhibitions, learning spaces, and a cafe, promoting understanding and enjoyment of the landscape.

Name: The Stepping Stones Project
Description: The Stepping Stones Project works to restore habitats and reintroduce species like water voles in Carding Mill Valley, Shropshire. It is a National Trust collaboration with Shropshire Wildlife Trust and the AONB Partnership, focusing on river health and creating connected wildlife sites.

Name: The Vyne Estate
Description: The Vyne Estate, a former Tudor powerhouse in Hampshire, features a historic chapel, extensive gardens, and a tranquil lake. Its wider estate includes wetlands and woodlands, supporting diverse wildlife. Seasonal events and family activities are regularly hosted.

Name: The Warren
Description: The Warren is a 13.5-hectare nature reserve in St Mary Cray in the London Borough of Bromley.

Name: The Wash National Nature Reserve
Description: The Wash National Nature Reserve is England's largest, covering intertidal sand, mudflats, and saltmarsh. It is a vital feeding ground for hundreds of thousands of birds, supporting important populations and England's largest seal haul-out.

Name: The White Cliffs of Dover
Description: Iconic landmark in Kent offering dramatic views across the English Channel. The site features rare wildflowers and butterflies, with walking trails along the cliff tops. It is managed for conservation and public access.

Name: The Workhouse, Southwell
Description: The Workhouse, Southwell, is a preserved Victorian workhouse built in 1824. It offers insight into 19th-century poverty and social welfare history through original architecture. A heritage orchard and meadow showcase traditional local flora and fruit varieties.

Name: The Wou
Description: The Wou, a 20-hectare peatland restoration site located at Moss Peteral near Thirlwall within Northumberland National Park. This site is part of a wider partnership project led by the Northumberland National Park Authority, working with the Border Uplands Peat Partnership to restore vital peatlands in the Border Uplands.

Name: Thelnetham Fen
Description: Blo' Norton and Thelnetham Fens are a 21.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the Norfolk/Suffolk border in England.

Name: Thetford Warren
Description: Thetford Warren is a Site of Special Scientific Interest in Breckland, Norfolk. It features typical Breckland grassland on sandy soils, supporting rare plants and invertebrates. The reserve also contains the ruins of a medieval warren lodge, a Scheduled Monument built in the early 15th century.

Name: Thirlmere
Description: Thirlmere is an active working forest in the Lake District National Park. It serves as a vital catchment for United Utilities, providing water and hydro-electric power. The area offers various footpaths and cycle trails for recreation while focusing on conservation and wildlife.

Name: Thompson Common
Description: Thompson Water, Carr and Common is a 154.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Thetford in Norfolk, England.

Name: Thorley Wash
Description: Thorley Wash or Thorley Flood Pound is a 17.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Thorley, south of Bishop's Stortford in Hertfordshire.

Name: Thornbury Park
Description: Thornbury Park in Isleworth, West London, hosts a TCV Green Gym every Wednesday morning. Volunteers participate in practical conservation tasks, improving the local environment. It offers opportunities to learn new skills and meet people.

Name: Thorndon Countryside Centre
Description: Thorndon Park is a 141.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Brentwood in Essex.

Name: Thorney Island
Description: Thorney Island, a Site of Special Scientific Interest in Chichester Harbour, features extensive mudflats, saltmarshes, and shingle beaches. These support migratory birds and marine life. Public access is limited to a coastal path. The site is managed to conserve its unique ecosystems.

Name: Thornton Wood
Description: Thornton Wood is a 6.24-hectare ancient woodland in Thornton Hough, managed by Wirral Wildlife. It is part of the Dibbinsdale Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). The site features diverse ground flora, including Ramsons, Bluebells, Wood Anemone, and Wood Sorrel, and supports a range of woodland birds and mammals like badgers. The reserve is generally not accessible to the public, but visits can be arranged by participating in organised work parties or specific events.

Name: Thorpe Hay Meadow
Description: Thorpe Hay Meadow is a 6.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Staines-upon-Thames in Surrey.

Name: Thorpe Marsh Nature Reserve
Description: Thorpe Marsh Nature Reserve is a 77-hectare nature reserve located south-west of Thorpe in Balne, north of Doncaster in South Yorkshire, England.  The reserve is managed and maintained by a team of volunteers under the Yorkshire Wildlife Trust as well as Doncaster Metropolitan Borough Council.

Name: Thorpe Marshes
Description: Thorpe Marshes is a 25-hectare nature reserve east of Norwich in Norfolk.  It is managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Thorpe Wood
Description: Thorpe Wood is a maturing woodland in the Tees Valley, planted in 1999 on former arable land. It features over 15 native tree species, a wetland area, and a wildflower meadow. The reserve provides valuable habitats, supporting diverse wildlife including dragonflies, damselflies, and bird species.

Name: Thorswood
Description: Thorswood is a nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust, situated in the Weaver Hills near the village of Stanton, in Staffordshire, England.  It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Threave Garden & Nature Reserve
Description: Threave Estate, near Castle Douglas, focuses on nature recovery across diverse habitats. The site supports significant populations of bats, otters, and ospreys. Conservation efforts involve wetland restoration and native woodland expansion.

Name: Three Groves Wood
Description: Three Groves Wood is a 3.3-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: Thrift Wood
Description: Thrift Wood is a 19.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of Bicknacre in Essex.

Name: Thrunton Wood
Description: Thrunton Wood offers walking and mountain biking trails amidst coniferous forest in Northumberland. Visitors can find challenging routes and enjoy views of the Cheviot Hills and the Northumberland coastline.

Name: Thundry Meadows
Description: Thundry Meadows is a 16-hectare nature reserve in Elstead in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Thurlbear Wood and Quarrylands
Description: Thurlbear Wood and Quarrylands is a 26.7 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Stoke St Mary in Somerset, notified in 1963.

Name: Thurrock Thameside Nature Park
Description: Thurrock Thameside Nature Park is an Essex Wildlife Trust nature reserve located on top of the former Mucking Marshes Landfill in Thurrock, England which will eventually cover 845 acres.  It is next to the River Thames and provides good bird and ship watching.

Name: Thursford Wood
Description: Thursford Wood is a 10-hectare nature reserve north-east of Fakenham in Norfolk.  It is managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Tiddesley Wood
Description: Tiddesley Wood – the Harry Green Reserve is a nature reserve of the Worcestershire Wildlife Trust.  It is situated about 1 mile west of Pershore and 7 miles south-east of Worcester, in Worcestershire, England.

Name: Tile Wood
Description: Tile Wood is a 6.5-hectare nature reserve in Thundersley in Essex.

Name: Tilton Railway Cutting
Description: Tilton Cutting is a 4.4 hectares geological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Tilton on the Hill in Leicestershire.

Name: Tintagel Coast & Barras Nose
Description: Tintagel Coast and Barras Nose feature a rugged coastline surrounding Tintagel Castle in North Cornwall. This exposed headland supports various seabirds and coastal flora. The South West Coast Path traverses the area, offering expansive Atlantic views amidst a landscape rich in Arthurian legend.

Name: Tiptree Heath
Description: Tiptree Heath is a 25 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-west of Tiptree in Essex, England.  It is managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust together with the Friends of Tiptree Heath.

Name: Titford Pools
Description: Titford Pools are large reservoirs in the Black Country, serving the Titford Canal and wider Birmingham New Main Line Canal network. A wildlife haven, the pools offer popular activities like walking, fishing, and boating, providing a vital green space for the local community.

Name: Tollesbury Wick
Description: Tollesbury Wick is a 242.8-hectare nature reserve east of Tollesbury in Essex.

Name: Tollymore Forest Park
Description: Tollymore Forest Park, near Newcastle, County Down, is Northern Ireland's first state forest park. Established in 1955, it covers 630 hectares at the Mourne Mountains' base. The Shimna River flows through it, known for its arboretum and historic follies.

Name: Tophill Low NNR
Description: Tophill Low NNR, managed by Yorkshire Water near Watton, East Yorkshire, is a Site of Special Scientific Interest. It features diverse wetlands, woodlands, and two reservoirs. This popular reserve offers excellent birdwatching opportunities.

Name: Totteridge Fields
Description: Totteridge Fields is a 97-hectare Site of Metropolitan Importance for Nature Conservation in Totteridge in the London Borough of Barnet.  The SINC includes the privately owned Highwood Hill, and at the western end is a seven-hectare Local Nature Reserve owned by Barnet Council and managed by the London Wildlife Trust.

Name: Town Kelloe Bank
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 5 hectares.

Name: Townend
Description: Townend is a preserved 17th-century farmhouse in the Lake District, once home to the Browne family. Visitors explore its historical rooms, extensive library, and traditional Lakeland garden. The site includes a small heritage orchard and an historic barn, showcasing four centuries of rural life.

Name: Townhead Wood
Description: Townhead Wood is a mixed woodland and grassland reserve on the western shore of Loch Leven. Acquired in 2021, it connects existing protected areas. The site supports red squirrels, great spotted woodpeckers, and various woodland birds, enhancing local biodiversity.

Name: Toys Hill
Description: Toys Hill is a high wooded ridge in Kent, part of the Wealden Greensand Ridge. It offers panoramic views across the Weald. The site features ancient woodlands and is rich in wildlife, with public footpaths for exploration.

Name: Trasna Island
Description: Trasna Island, within the Lower Lough Erne Islands SPA, focuses on habitat restoration for breeding waders. LELP volunteers manage the site, which recently celebrated the successful fledging of three Curlew chicks. Work aims to support endangered bird populations.

Name: Tredegar House Parkland
Description: Tredegar House in Newport, Wales, features significant parkland biodiversity. The National Trust works to restore diverse habitats including ponds, wetlands, and species-rich meadows, supporting local wildlife.

Name: Trelissick Maritime Woods
Description: Trelissick Maritime Woods offers tranquil garden and wooded parkland walks with panoramic views of the Fal estuary. Visitors can explore a variety of trails, from gentle strolls among trees and shrubs to longer hikes along the estuary. The site is located seven miles south of Truro.

Name: Trench Wood
Description: Trench Wood is a woodland area part managed by the Worcestershire Wildlife Trust and Butterfly Conservation.  It is located around 6 miles miles north-east of Worcester near the small villages of Dunhampstead and Sale Green.

Name: Trevone Bay
Description: Trevone Bay is situated on the North Cornwall coast near Padstow, featuring dramatic cliffs, sandy beaches, and numerous coves. Part of the South West Coast Path runs along Trevose Head, offering coastal views of the Atlantic and opportunities to spot seabirds.

Name: Trevose Head
Description: Trevose Head is a prominent headland near Padstow, Cornwall, designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). It features coastal grassland, dramatic cliffs, and important seabird breeding sites. Visitors enjoy scenic walks and observe diverse wildlife.

Name: Trimdon Grange Quarry
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 5 hectares.

Name: Trimley Marshes
Description: Trimley Marshes is a 77 hectare nature reserve west of Trimley St Mary, on the outskirts of Felixstowe in Suffolk.  It is managed by the Suffolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Tring Reservoirs
Description: Tring Reservoirs is a group of four reservoirs close to Tring on the border of Hertfordshire and Buckinghamshire, England.  Their purpose is to feed the Grand Union Canal.

Name: Trosley Country Park
Description: Trosley Country Park is a 170-acre site near Meopham on the North Downs. It offers expansive views and significant chalk grassland slopes. Kent County Council manages the park, while Kent Wildlife Trust maintains a vital chalk grassland area within it.

Name: Troup Head
Description: Troup Head is Scotland's largest mainland gannet colony, home to over 30,000 gannets during the breeding season. This cliff-top reserve also supports kittiwakes, fulmars, and guillemots. Seals are often visible below the cliffs.

Name: Trumland
Description: Trumland is an RSPB nature reserve on Rousay, Orkney. It features heathland, wetlands, and moorland habitats. The reserve is home to diverse bird species including hen harriers, red-throated divers, and arctic skuas. Visitors can explore walking trails.

Name: Tuckmill Meadows
Description: Tuckmill Meadows is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) nestled between Shrivenham and Watchfield villages in southwest Oxfordshire. This 15-acre reserve combines floodplain meadows, reedbeds, woodlands, and a stream (Pennyhooks Brook, a tributary of the River Cole). It is home to over 300 plant species, rare insects, otters, and various birds. The site is managed by Earth Trust, in partnership with Vale of White Horse District Council and Friends of Tuckmill volunteers, for biodiversity and public access.

Name: Tuckmill Meadows
Description: Tuckmill Meadows is a valuable wildflower meadow, fen, and wet woodland reserve near Shrivenham and Watchfield in south-west Oxfordshire. It is fed by Pennyhooks Brook, a tributary of the River Cole, supporting diverse plant and insect life, including water voles, rare spiders, and various butterfly species. It is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) for its fen habitat and species-rich grasslands.

Name: Tudhoe Mill Wood
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 38 hectares.

Name: Tunman Wood
Description: Tunman Wood is a local nature reserve with an area of over 53 ha located near Eagle Barnsdale, Lincolnshire.  It is an area of ancient woodland and has existed since at least 1774.

Name: Tunstall Forest
Description: Tunstall Forest is a mixed woodland in Suffolk, East of England, offering walking, cycling, and horse riding trails. Part of the Suffolk Coasts and Heaths Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, it consists of coniferous plantations, broadleaved belts, and heathland areas. It is part of the Sandlings Forest Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and a Special Protection Area (SPA), providing diverse habitats for wildlife, including ground-nesting birds like the Nightjar and Woodlark. It is managed sustainably for timber and recreation.

Name: Turners Field
Description: Turners Field is an 11-hectare nature reserve on the western outskirts of Tenterden in Kent.  It is managed by Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Turners Puddle Heath
Description: Turners Puddle Heath is a nature reserve protecting lowland heath, mire, and bog. It supports scarce wildlife including nightjars, Dartford warblers, sand lizards, and smooth snakes, crucial for biodiversity in Dorset.

Name: Turnford and Cheshunt Pits
Description: Turnford and Cheshunt Pits, a nature reserve in the Lee Valley, features flooded gravel pits. It is an SSSI and SPA, supporting diverse birdlife including overwintering wildfowl and breeding birds. Birdwatching hides and walking paths are available.

Name: Twickenham Rough
HostOrg: London Borough of Richmond upon Thames
Description: Twickenham Rough is a nature reserve in Twickenham, owned by Richmond Council. TCV volunteers undertake coppicing, scrub clearance, and path maintenance to manage the site's biodiversity.

Name: Two Mile Bottom
Description: Two Mile Bottom is a Forestry England site within Thetford Forest, Norfolk. It offers walking, cycling, and horse riding trails amidst woodlands near the Little Ouse River. It serves as a gateway to the wider forest experience.

Name: Two Tree Island
Description: Two Tree Island is a small island lying north-east of Canvey Island and south-west of Leigh-on-Sea in Essex, England.  It covers 257 hectares and is connected to the mainland at Leigh by a single span bridge.

Name: Tyland Barn
Description: Tyland Barn, in Sandling, north of Maidstone, Kent, is the headquarters of the Kent Wildlife Trust.  It has a nature park which is designed to show the variety of habitats in the county, such as a pond, grassland, a chalk bank, a shingle beach, scrub and hedges.

Name: Uffmoor Wood
Description: Uffmoor Wood is an ancient woodland near Hagley, managed by the Woodland Trust for conservation and public access. It features diverse habitats, including broadleaf trees, conifers, and open glades. Visitors can explore a network of walking trails and observe various wildlife, including numerous bird species.

Name: Ullswater Catchment Restoration
Description: The National Trust manages the Ullswater catchment area, undertaking conservation work and restoring habitats. Efforts include tree planting and rewilding valleys to mitigate flood risk and enhance the natural landscape.

Name: Ulverscroft
Description: Ulverscroft is a 56-hectare nature reserve north of Markfield in Leicestershire, England.  It is managed by the Leicestershire and Rutland Wildlife Trust, which shares its ownership with the National Trust.

Name: Umbra
Description: Umbra Nature Reserve is a significant dune system at Magilligan, County Londonderry. It hosts a unique flora, including rare orchids, and important fauna like natterjack toads and diverse bird species. The site holds Ramsar, SAC, and ASSI designations.

Name: Underdown
Description: Underdown is a 1-hectare nature reserve in Farnham in Surrey.  It is owned and managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Uphill Hill
Description: Uphill Hill is a coastal limestone grassland near Weston-super-Mare with views of the Bristol Channel. It features ancient monuments, diverse flora including orchids, and supports various bird species. The site offers walking trails.

Name: Upper Conwy Catchment - Afon Eidda Project
Description: The Upper Conwy Catchment is a landscape of ancient woodland, farmland, and blanket bog in the Afon Conwy valley. It supports diverse wildlife, including red squirrels and otters. The Afon Eidda Project focuses on restoring nature and improving water quality within the sub-catchment area.

Name: Upper Derwent Catchment
Description: Located within the Peak District National Park, the Upper Derwent Catchment is a vital upland area of peatlands and reservoirs. Moors for the Future Partnership undertakes extensive restoration, re-wetting degraded blanket bog habitats to enhance biodiversity and capture carbon effectively.

Name: Upper Derwent Valley
Description: The National Trust cares for the Upper Derwent Valley, an area of picturesque woodlands and extensive peat moorlands. It encompasses the iconic Derwent, Howden, and Ladybower reservoirs, offering walking, cycling, and diverse wildlife discovery.

Name: Upper Ray Meadows
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Upper Ray Meadows is a 181-hectare nature reserve, managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust, south of Marsh Gibbon in Buckinghamshire.  It is composed of a number of areas, one of which, Long Herdon Meadow, is a biological Site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Upper Titchfield Haven
Description: Upper Titchfield Haven is a Hampshire nature reserve in the Meon Valley. It protects fen, reedbed, and wet grassland habitats. The site supports diverse birdlife, dragonflies, and water voles. Accessible trails allow visitors to explore the area.

Name: Upper Waterhay Meadow
Description: Upper Waterhay Meadow is a 2.8 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in north Wiltshire, England, notified in 1971.

Name: Upper Wharfedale
Description: Upper Wharfedale is a glacial valley in the Yorkshire Dales. The National Trust manages 7,000 acres of upland, featuring hay meadows, limestone pavements, and ancient woodlands. It supports rare plants and wildlife like red squirrels. Conservation work maintains diverse habitats.

Name: Upton Broad and Marshes
Description: Upton Broad and Marshes is a 195.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Norwich in Norfolk, England.

Name: Upton Towans
Description: Towan is found in many placenames in Cornwall.  However, The Towans usually refers to the three-mile stretch of coastal dunes which extends north-east from the estuary of the River Hayle to Gwithian beach with a midpoint near Upton.

Name: Upwood Meadows
Description: Upwood Meadows SSSI is an unimproved neutral grassland in Cambridgeshire. Managed by Wildlife BCN, its two species-rich meadows, The Lings and Old Chapel Field, feature green-winged orchid, adder's-tongue fern, oxeye daisy, and yellow rattle.

Name: Uswayford Forest
Description: Uswayford Forest, located within the Cheviot Hills, is a designated Red Squirrel Reserve within Northumberland National Park. Managed by Forestry England, it forms part of the Cheviots Forest Plan, aiming to enhance woodland connectivity and support crucial biodiversity, contributing to regional ecological resilience.

Name: Uxbridge Alderglade
Description: Uxbridge Alderglade is a 2.9-hectare nature reserve in Uxbridge in the London Borough of Hillingdon.

Name: Vane Farm
Description: Vane Farm sits on the southern shore of Loch Leven, a large freshwater lake in Scotland. It offers panoramic views and diverse habitats including woodlands and reedbeds. The reserve provides accessible trails, hides, and a visitor centre, supporting numerous bird species.

Name: Vann Lake and Candy's Copse
Description: Vann Lake and Ockley Woods is a 57.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Ockley in Surrey.

Name: Vell Mill Daffodil Meadow
Description: Vell Mill Daffodil Meadow is a 2.1-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.

Name: Ventongimps Moor
Description: Ventongimps Moor is a moorland nature reserve and Site of Special Scientific Interest, noted for its biological characteristics, in mid Cornwall, England, United Kingdom.  The site, important for the occurrence of the plant Dorset heath, was the first reserve to be purchased by the Cornwall Wildlife Trust.

Name: Vicar Water Country Park
Description: Vicar Water Country Park, north of Clipstone Village, is a former colliery site transformed into a Green Flag park. It now features woodlands, open heathland, and a large lake, offering diverse wildlife habitats and well-maintained paths for walkers and cyclists.

Name: Vinters Valley Nature Reserve
Description: Vinters Valley Nature Reserve is a peaceful haven of woodland, grassland, and wetland in Maidstone, Kent. The River Len flows through the valley, supporting diverse wildlife including birds, mammals, and invertebrates.

Name: Waen Fraith
Description: Waen Fraith is a peatland restoration site within Eryri National Park, Wales. The National Trust, in partnership with Admiral, is restoring 100 hectares to capture carbon and mitigate flood risk. This three-year project blocks ditches to re-wet the peat and remove invasive species.

Name: Waldridge Fell SSSI
Description: Waldridge Fell SSSI is a lowland heath in County Durham, providing a vital habitat for various rare plants and insects. Designated as a Site of Special Scientific Interest, it represents one of the last remaining areas of this unique ecosystem.

Name: Wallasea Island
Description: Wallasea Island, Essex, is a significant conservation and engineering project, forming Europe's largest man-made nature reserve. Created from Crossrail tunnel spoil, it features extensive mudflats, saltmarshes, and lagoons, providing vital habitats for diverse migratory and breeding bird species.

Name: Wallington River Wansbeck Restoration
Description: Wallington, a National Trust property in Northumberland, features a historic house, gardens, and expansive estate. It is currently undertaking a pioneering River Wansbeck restoration project, improving water quality, increasing flood storage, and creating wetland habitats.

Name: Wallis Wood
Description: Wallis Wood is a 14-hectare nature reserve south-east of Ewhurst in Surrey.  It is managed by the Surrey Wildlife Trust.

Name: Walltown Crags
Description: Walltown Crags, a connectivity node in Northumberland National Park, is part of the Hadrian's Wall Wetlands Project. It restores wetlands, peatlands, and grasslands, enhancing biodiversity and wildlife corridors.

Name: Walsall Canal Wildlife Haven
Description: The Walsall Canal runs through a mix of urban and green spaces in the West Midlands. It provides a habitat for various wildlife species, including waterbirds and insects. The canal supports local ecosystems and offers a linear green corridor.

Name: Waltham Brooks
Description: Waltham Brooks is a 47.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-west of Pulborough in West Sussex.

Name: Walthamstow Marshes
Description: Walthamstow Marshes is a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in East London. It features a diverse mix of marshland, rivers, and ditches, supporting unique flora and fauna. Historically, it hosted Britain's first powered flight in 1909 and the nation's first aircraft factory.

Name: Walton Common
Description: Walton Common is a 25.5 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near the village of Walton in Gordano, North Somerset, notified in 1991.

Name: Wandlebury Country Park
Description: Wandlebury Country Park is a historic parkland on the Gog Magog Hills near Cambridge, featuring Iron Age hillfort remains. It offers walking routes, nature trails, and views over the city, managed for wildlife and public enjoyment.

Name: Wangford Warren
Description: Wangford Warren and Carr is a 67.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between Brandon and Lakenheath in Suffolk.

Name: Wanlip Meadows
Description: Wanlip Meadows is a 16.2 hectares nature reserve south of Wanlip and north of Leicester.

Name: Wanstead Park
Description: Wanstead Park hosts floating reedbeds launched by Thames21 in 2025. These reedbeds improve water quality and create habitats for wildlife, supported by volunteers and the City of London Corporation.

Name: Warburg Nature Reserve
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Bix Bottom is a 102.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north-west of Henley-on-Thames in Oxfordshire.

Name: Warburton's Wood Nature Reserve
Description: Warburton's Wood Nature Reserve is a nature reserve near Kingsley, Cheshire, England, managed by the Cheshire Wildlife Trust.  The reserve consists of semi-natural woodland either side of a clough, or small valley, containing a tributary of the River Weaver.

Name: Waresley & Gransden Woods
Description: Waresley & Gransden Woods is an ancient woodland in Cambridgeshire, managed by Wildlife BCN. It is noted for its spring displays of bluebells and wood anemones, mature trees, and diverse wildlife. Waymarked trails are available for visitors.

Name: Wark Forest
Description: Wark Forest is a large working forest located within Kielder Forest Park in Northumberland. Managed by Forestry England, it is known for its diverse wildlife, including red squirrels and ospreys. The area offers various outdoor activities.

Name: Warley Place
Description: Warley Place is a 10.1-hectare nature reserve south of Brentwood in Great Warley, Essex.

Name: Warnborough Greens
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Warnborough Green is a 4.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in North Warnborough in Hampshire.

Name: Warren Bank
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Warren Bank is a 3.1-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south-east of Wallingford in Oxfordshire.

Name: Warrens Wood
Description: Warren Wood is a former ancient woodland plantation near Maidstone, Kent. Dominated by mature oak, hornbeam, and hazel coppice, with some sycamore and ash. It features footpaths and an adjacent public bridleway, with part of it a Local Wildlife Site.

Name: Warton Crag
Description: Warton Crag is a limestone hill in north west Lancashire, England.  It lies to the north west of Warton village, in City of Lancaster district.

Name: Wasdale & Eskdale
Description: Wasdale, in the Lake District, encompasses England's highest mountain, Scafell Pike, and deepest lake, Wastwater. The National Trust manages this valley, undertaking vital conservation work, including high fell path repairs and visitor access.

Name: Washburn Valley
Description: Yorkshire Water, through its Washburn Valley Biodiversity Enhancement Project, improves 200 hectares for wildlife. Efforts include restoring peatland, creating new woodlands, and improving river habitats within the scenic Washburn Valley area.

Name: Waterford Heath
Description: Waterford Heath is a 35.2 hectare Local Nature Reserve in Waterford in Hertfordshire, England.

Name: Watersmeet
Description: Watersmeet is a deep gorge woodland in Exmoor National Park, Devon, where the East Lyn River and Hoar Oak Water meet. Owned by the National Trust, it features scenic walking trails and a historic tea-garden, popular for its natural beauty and diverse wildlife.

Name: WaterWorks Centre Nature Reserve
Description: The WaterWorks Centre Nature Reserve, in East London, features wetland habitats, wildflower meadows, and open water, supporting diverse wildlife. Located adjacent to the Lee Navigation, the site offers walking routes and bird hides for visitors to observe nature, particularly a range of bird species.

Name: Watlington Hill
Description: Watlington Hill offers panoramic views across the Oxfordshire plain, situated high above Watlington. This site features a mosaic of chalk grassland and ancient woodland, supporting a variety of rare plants and insects, including the red kite.

Name: Wattle Wood
Description: Wattle Wood is a 1-hectare nature reserve north-west of Tenterden in Kent.  It is managed by Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: Watts Bank
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Watts Bank is a 1.9-hectare nature reserve south of Lambourn in Berkshire.

Name: Wayland Wood
Description: Wayland Wood is a 31.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest near to Watton in Norfolk, England.

Name: Weald Country Park
Description: Weald Country Park is a large, historic country park in Brentwood, Essex, managed by Essex County Council. Spanning over 500 acres, it features extensive woodlands, lakes, and open grasslands. The park is home to diverse wildlife, including fallow deer and various bird species, and offers visitors a network of paths to explore, alongside popular attractions like the Stick Man sculpture trail.

Name: Weeleyhall Wood
Description: Weeleyhall Wood is a 31 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Clacton-on-Sea in Essex.  It is managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Weeting Heath
Description: Weeting Heath is a 141.8-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Thetford in Norfolk, England, which is managed by the Norfolk Wildlife Trust.

Name: Weir Wood Reservoir
Description: Weir Wood Reservoir is a 153.5-hectare (379-acre) Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) in East Sussex, with an 81-acre Local Nature Reserve at its western end. It is managed in partnership by Southern Water, East Sussex County Council, and The Friends of Weir Wood. The site supports diverse bird species, including overwintering wildfowl and migrating waders. Public access is limited, with bird hides available, particularly at the western end.

Name: Wells Farm
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Wells Farm is a 64-hectare nature reserve on the eastern outskirts of Little Milton in Oxfordshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Welsh Wildlife Centre
HostOrg: Wildlife Trust of South and West Wales
Description: The Welsh Wildlife Centre is a wildlife reserve covering Teifi Marshes, near Cilgerran on the Pembrokeshire/Ceredigion border, Wales.  The site is located close to the Cardigan-Cilgerran Offshoot of the Pembrokeshire Coastal Path.

Name: Wembury Bay
Description: Wembury Bay is a popular Devon coastal site, managed by the National Trust, featuring diverse habitats from sandy beaches to rocky shores. It offers rockpooling, beach walks, and a marine centre focused on education and marine conservation.

Name: Wendover Woods
Description: Wendover Woods is a extensive woodland managed by Forestry England in the Chiltern Hills, Buckinghamshire. It features walking and cycling trails, a café, and a popular treetop adventure course. The site offers diverse habitats and panoramic views across the Aylesbury Vale.

Name: Wenlock Edge
Description: Wenlock Edge is a limestone escarpment stretching for 19 miles in Shropshire. A woodland of ash, lime and hazel covers the ancient coral reef, providing habitat for diverse wildlife. It offers walking trails and is a designated Site of Special Scientific Interest managed by the National Trust.

Name: Wenlock Edge
Description: Wenlock Edge is a 19-mile limestone escarpment in Shropshire, featuring ancient woodlands and grasslands. Designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), it forms part of the Shropshire Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty. It supports diverse wildlife and geological features.

Name: Wentworth Castle Gardens
Description: Wentworth Castle Gardens, in South Yorkshire, is a historic landscape with formal gardens, parkland, and architectural follies. Managed by the National Trust in partnership with Barnsley Council, it focuses on conservation and public access to heritage.

Name: West Blean and Thornden Woods
Description: West Blean and Thornden Woods is a 781-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Canterbury in Kent.  It is part of the Blean Woods Nature Conservation Review site, and an area of 490 hectares is a nature reserve managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.

Name: West Dean Woods
Description: West Dean Woods is a 16.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of West Dean in West Sussex.

Name: West Ham Park
Description: West Ham Park is a historic 31.1-hectare (77-acre) green space in Newham, East London. It features formal gardens, sports facilities, a children's playground, and an arboretum. The park is managed by the City of London Corporation and provides diverse recreational opportunities.

Name: West Runton and Beeston Regis Heath
Description: West Runton and Beeston Regis Heath offers panoramic views of the the North Norfolk coast and a diverse landscape of heathland, woodland, and meadows. It is home to various wildlife species, including butterflies, birds, and deer. The site is popular for walking and nature observation.

Name: West Walk - Forest of Bere
Description: West Walk, within the Forest of Bere, is a woodland site in Hampshire. It offers marked walking, cycling, and horse riding trails through ancient woodland and heathland habitats. Managed by Forestry England, it supports biodiversity and provides recreational access.

Name: West Wickham Common
Description: West Wickham Common and Spring Park, managed by the City of London Corporation, offers heathland, woodland, ponds, and open green spaces in South London. This Green Flag awarded site is a Site of Special Scientific Interest, protecting ancient woodland and providing a refuge for wildlife.

Name: West Wood
Description: West Wood is a 23.6 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Little Sampford, north of Thaxted in northwestern Essex.

Name: Westfield Wood
Description: Westfield Wood is a 5-hectare nature reserve north of Maidstone in Kent, which is managed by the Kent Wildlife Trust.  It is part of the Wouldham to Detling Escarpment Site of Special Scientific Interest and Nature Conservation Review site, Grade I.

Name: Westhay Heath
Description: Westhay Heath is a 25.9 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest 2km west of Westhay village in Somerset, notified in 1990.

Name: Westhay Moor
Description: Westhay Moor is a 513.7-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest 2.

Name: Westhouse Wood
Description: Westhouse Wood is a 2.8-hectare nature reserve north-west of Colchester in Essex.

Name: Weston Big Wood
Description: Weston Big Wood is a 37.48 hectare woodland west of the town of Portishead, North Somerset, England.

Name: Weston Turville Reservoir
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Weston Turville Reservoir is a 19 hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest south of Weston Turville in Buckinghamshire.  It is owned by the Canal & River Trust, and the open water is leased to sailing and fishing clubs while the surrounding land is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Westwood Manor Estate
Description: Westwood Manor is a medieval house in Wiltshire, featuring a beautiful garden and topiary. The property reveals its changing uses, from a medieval hall to a Georgian clothier's home and a 20th-century family residence, with collections of furniture and musical instruments.

Name: Wetley Moor Common
Description: Wetley Moor Common is a Staffordshire Wildlife Trust reserve consisting of ancient common land.  It has been designated a Site of Special Scientific Interest due to its unimproved lowland heath habitat, which represents approximately 10% of the heathland in Staffordshire.

Name: Whinlatter Forest
Description: Whinlatter Forest, England's only true mountain forest, is nestled high in the Lake District National Park. It provides extensive walking and cycling trails, a Go Ape course, and a visitor centre. The forest is home to ospreys and red squirrels, offering stunning views.

Name: Whinlatter Forest
Description: Whinlatter Forest, near Keswick, offers walking and cycling trails with views of Bassenthwaite Lake and surrounding fells within the Lake District National Park. Managed by Forestry England, it provides routes for various abilities and supports a diverse range of local wildlife.

Name: Whirlow Hall Farm
Description: Whirlow Hall Farm is a working educational farm and charity in Sheffield, bordering the Peak District. Managed by the Whirlow Hall Farm Trust, it provides educational experiences for children and young people, particularly those facing challenges, focusing on farming, food production, and environmental awareness. The site includes various livestock and offers public access to a cafe, shop, and playground.

Name: Whisby Moor
Description: Whisby Moor is a small moor situated close to the A46 road, west of North Hykeham, in the North Kesteven district of Lincolnshire, England.

Name: Whisby Nature Park
Description: Whisby Moor is a small moor situated close to the A46 road, west of North Hykeham, in the North Kesteven district of Lincolnshire, England.

Name: White Hill
Description: White Hill is a chalk grassland nature reserve located on a steep south-west facing slope of the North Downs in Kent. It is an important habitat supporting a variety of insects, including the Adonis Blue butterfly, and different plant species. The site is part of the Kent Downs Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

Name: White Horse Hill
Description: High on a chalk downland ridge in Oxfordshire, the Bronze Age White Horse is carved into the hillside. Iron Age earthworks of Uffington Castle surround the chalk figure, while Dragon Hill and Wayland's Smithy are nearby.

Name: Whitecross Green Wood
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Whitecross Green and Oriel Woods is a 63-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest between Oxford and Bicester in Oxfordshire.  It is owned and managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust under the name Whitecross Green Wood.

Name: Whiteford Burrows
Description: Whiteford Burrows is a coastal reserve on the Gower Peninsula in South Wales. It features an expansive sandy beach, a dune system, saltmarsh, and woodland, supporting diverse wildlife. The area is known for its historic cast-iron lighthouse and provides habitats for many bird species and rare plants.

Name: Whiteford Hill
Description: This National Trust site offers open access to ancient woodland and chalk downland within the South Downs National Park in Hampshire. It provides spectacular views across the landscape, encompassing diverse wildlife habitats and features tranquil walking trails.

Name: Whitehaven Coast
Description: The Whitehaven Coast offers dramatic cliff-top walks and panoramic views across the Irish Sea. This area encompasses important maritime grasslands, providing vital habitats for diverse wildlife and unique coastal flora, accessible via maintained public paths.

Name: Whitehouse Lagoon
Description: Whitehouse Lagoon is an international wetland and vital migratory stopover on Belfast Lough, part of RSPB Belfast's Window on Wildlife. It hosts diverse bird species year-round. Two hides offer observation points for visitors overlooking the lagoon.

Name: Whitehouse Meadow
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 1 hectares.

Name: Whiteleaf Hill
Description: Whiteleaf Hill offers panoramic views across the Chilterns, featuring a prehistoric barrow and the striking Whiteleaf Cross carved into the chalk hillside. The site includes woodlands and open grasslands, supporting diverse wildlife. Popular for walking and wildlife spotting.

Name: Whitelee Moor
Description: Whitelee Moor is nature reserve of the Northumberland Wildlife Trust, in Northumberland, England, near Carter Bar.  A large part of the moor is blanket bog.

Name: Whitmoor and Rickford Commons
Description: Whitmoor Common is a 166-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest on the northern outskirts of Guildford in Surrey.  It is part of the Thames Basin Heaths Special Protection Area and the 184.

Name: Wicken Fen
Description: Wicken Fen is a national nature reserve where traditional fenland habitats are preserved, supporting over 9,000 species. Actively expanding, it features waterways, grazing marshes, and reedbeds within a significant wetland landscape.

Name: Wicken Fen National Nature Reserve
Description: Wicken Fen National Nature Reserve, including Baker's Fen, is a precious wetland habitat in Cambridgeshire. It supports diverse wildlife, from rare insects to birds, and is an active site for conservation research and species reintroduction.

Name: Wicken Fen National Nature Reserve
Description: Wicken Fen is one of Europe's most important wetlands, offering a rich habitat for over 9,000 species. Visitors can explore boardwalks, enjoy boat trips, cycle routes, and views from the tower. Adventurers' Fen is part of this diverse nature reserve.

Name: Wightwick Manor and Gardens
Description: Wightwick Manor is a Victorian house in Wolverhampton, West Midlands, showcasing the Arts and Crafts movement. It features interiors and collections by William Morris, De Morgan, and Rossetti. The gardens reflect the Arts and Crafts style.

Name: Wigpool
Description: Wigpool is a 7.5-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire in the Forest of Dean, England.

Name: Wild Haweswater
Description: Wild Haweswater is a partnership between United Utilities and the RSPB, restoring natural processes and improving biodiversity in the Haweswater valley. The project focuses on rewilding a large upland area, enhancing habitats for wildlife like red squirrels and rare birds.

Name: Wilden Marsh
Description: Wilden Marsh is a nature reserve of the Worcestershire Wildlife Trust.  It is situated between Kidderminster and Stourport-on-Severn, in Worcestershire, England, immediately east of the Staffordshire and Worcestershire Canal, and alongside the River Stour.

Name: Wilderness Island
Description: Wilderness Island is the 2.7 hectare island between the Wandle and Wrythe in Carshalton in the London Borough of Sutton.

Name: Wildmoor Heath
Description: Wildmoor Heath is a 91-hectare lowland heathland reserve located south of Crowthorne in Berkshire, managed by BBOWT. It is part of the Thames Basin Heaths Special Protection Area and a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI). It provides habitat for rare species including nightjar, woodlark, Dartford warbler, adders, and sand lizards.

Name: Wildmoor Heath
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Wildmoor Heath is a 91-hectare nature reserve south of Crowthorne in Berkshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Wildwood Discovery Park
Description: Wildwood Trust is a woodland discovery park in Herne, near Canterbury in Kent, England.  It features over fifty species of native British animals such as deer, badgers, wild boar, and brown bear.

Name: Willesley Wood
Description: Willesley Wood is a maturing woodland, flower meadow, and wetland site near Ashby-de-la-Zouch, Leicestershire, managed by The Woodland Trust. Part of the National Forest, it features a diverse mix of tree species, including oak, ash, and hazel, supporting a rich understorey and varied wildlife. The site offers tranquil paths for visitors.

Name: Williamthorpe Nature Reserve
Description: Williamthorpe Nature Reserve, a former colliery site, is a haven for wildlife managed by Derbyshire County Council. It features diverse habitats including grasslands, wetlands, woodlands, open water, and extensive reed beds. The reserve supports a rich variety of wildlife, including amphibians like frogs, toads, and newts, and is a key site for dragonflies and damselflies during summer months. Over 200 bird species have been recorded, with regular visitors such as Teal, Tufted Duck, and Pochard, and nesting Mute Swans. Sedge and Reed Warblers can be found in the reed beds, while Southern Marsh and Common Spotted Orchids bloom in late spring. In the evenings, Pipistrelle, Daubenton's, and Noctule bats hunt for insects. Historically, the largest pond was fed by warm mine water, influencing its ecosystem.

Name: Willow Tree Fen
Description: Willow Tree Fen is a local nature reserve with an area of over 112. 0 ha located near Bourne and Spalding, south of the River Glen, England.

Name: Willowmead
Description: Willowmead is a 1.5-hectare nature reserve in north Hertford.

Name: Wimbledon and Putney Commons
Description: Wimbledon and Putney Commons span 1,140 acres of heathland, woodland, and grassland in South West London. Managed under an 1871 Act of Parliament, the site supports diverse wildlife and offers recreational opportunities for visitors.

Name: Wimpole Estate
Description: Wimpole Estate in Cambridgeshire is a National Trust property encompassing a mansion, gardens, parkland, and a working farm. It focuses on conservation efforts, including the Green Recovery Project and wood pasture restoration.

Name: Windmill Hill
Description: Windmill Hill is a young woodland with recent tree planting, offering open views across the surrounding countryside. It features mixed deciduous species and a pond, providing habitats for various wildlife. The site is accessible via public footpaths.

Name: Wingate Quarry
Description: Wingate Quarry is a former limestone quarry, now a Local Nature Reserve in County Durham. It features flower-rich grassland supporting bee, fragrant, and frog orchids. Butterflies like dingy skipper, common blue, and small copper thrive here.

Name: Wingate Quarry LNR
Description: Wingate Quarry LNR is a 65.5-acre (26.5-hectare) Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and Local Nature Reserve, managed by Durham County Council. It is renowned for its nationally scarce magnesian limestone grassland and scrub habitats. The reserve supports diverse flora, including over 34 species of wildflowers such as common spotted orchid, birdsfoot trefoil, quaking grass, and butterwort. It is also home to protected species like great crested newts, and various butterflies including dingy skipper, brown argus, and the translocated marbled white butterfly.

Name: Winks Meadow
Description: Metfield Meadow is a 1.3-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Halesworth in Suffolk.

Name: Winmarleigh and Cockerham Moss
Description: Winmarleigh and Cockerham Moss is a nature reserve of the Wildlife Trust for Lancashire, Manchester and North Merseyside, west of Garstang and between the villages of Winmarleigh and Cockerham, which is being restored to its former state of peatland.

Name: Winnall Moors
HostOrg: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust
Description: Winnall Moors is a 64-hectare nature reserve in Winchester in Hampshire.  It is managed by the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Wildlife Trust.

Name: Winsford Gardens
Description: Winsford Gardens is a Victorian public park in Penge, South East London, operating as a Green Gym since 2011. Volunteers meet weekly to perform conservation and gardening tasks. The group manages and maintains the park's Green Flag award.

Name: Winterton Dunes
Description: Winterton Dunes is a nationally important dune system and beach in Norfolk, designated as a National Nature Reserve. It is home to one of the largest grey seal colonies in England and supports diverse flora and fauna, including natterjack toads and various bird species. Managed for conservation, it sees high visitor numbers.

Name: Wisley and Ockham Commons and Chatley Heath
Description: Ockham and Wisley Commons is a 266-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Woking in Surrey.  It is also a Local Nature Reserve and part of the Thames Basin Heaths Special Protection Area.

Name: Withdean Woods
Description: Withdean and Westdene Woods is a 7.9-hectare Local Nature Reserve in four separate areas in Brighton in East Sussex.

Name: Witherslack Mosses
Description: Witherslack Mosses are a fragmented wetland west of the Kent estuary in Cumbria, England, within the Lake District National Park.  They consist of three raised bogs, the remnants of a formerly extensive, estuarine bog, which have been protected under the Habitats Directive as a Special Area of Conservation.

Name: Witley and Milford Commons
Description: Witley and Milford Commons is a heathland National Nature Reserve in Surrey. It features diverse habitats including heathland, woodland, and ponds, supporting varied wildlife. Visitors can explore walking trails.

Name: Witton-le-Wear (SSSI)
Description: Witton-le-Wear is a Site of Special Scientific Interest located in the valley of the River Wear, immediately east of the village of Witton-le-Wear in County Durham, England.  It is important as the only extensive body of biologically significant open water in West Durham.

Name: Wivenhoe Woods
Description: Wivenhoe Woods is a mixed ancient woodland near Colchester, Essex. It features mature oak, hornbeam, and sweet chestnut trees. In spring, the woodland floor displays bluebells and wood anemones. Birdlife is abundant along the circular path.

Name: Wokefield Common
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 60 hectares.

Name: Wolseley Centre
Description: The Wolseley Centre is a visitor centre and nature reserve of the Staffordshire Wildlife Trust, in Staffordshire, England, about 2 miles north-west of Rugeley, and about 7 miles south-east of the county town of Stafford.

Name: Wood of Cree
Description: RSPB Scotland's largest ancient woodland, Wood of Cree protects oak, birch, and alder trees. It features stunning displays of bluebells in spring. The reserve is a vital habitat for various birds, including pied flycatchers, redstarts, and wood warblers, offering rich wildlife watching opportunities.

Name: Woodberry Wetlands
Description: Woodberry Wetlands is a nature reserve and designated Site of Metropolitan Importance on the site of the East Reservoir in the Manor House area in the London Borough of Hackney.  The site opened to the public for the first time in 200 years on 1 May 2016.

Name: Woodchester Park
Description: Woodchester Park is a secluded valley in the Cotswolds featuring a Victorian Gothic mansion, five lakes, and extensive woodlands. The estate is managed for nature conservation, offering walking routes amidst diverse habitats and historical landscape features.

Name: Woodchester Park
Description: Discover an unfinished Victorian mansion, nestled in a hidden valley. Explore miles of walking trails through ancient beech woodlands, past lakes and ponds. Spot wildlife and enjoy a tranquil landscape.

Name: Woodford Bottom and Lamb's Pool
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Woodford Bottom and Lamb's Pool is a 3-hectare nature reserve south of Sibford Ferris in Oxfordshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Woodhall Spa Airfield Nature Reserve
Description: Royal Air Force Woodhall Spa, or more simply RAF Woodhall Spa, is a former Royal Air Force satellite station located 2 miles north of Coningsby, Lincolnshire and 16 miles southeast of Lincoln, Lincolnshire, England.

Name: Woodham Fen
Description: Woodham Fen is an 8.1-hectare nature reserve in South Woodham Ferrers in Essex.

Name: Woodham Walter Common SSSI
Description: Woodham Walter Common SSSI is an 80-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest in Danbury in Essex.  The site includes six nature reserves within the Danbury Ridge Nature Reserves, managed by the Essex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Woodland Trust - Chalkney Wood
Description: Chalkney Wood is a 72.6-hectare (179-acre) biological Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) near Earls Colne, Essex. It is owned and managed by Essex County Council (25 hectares) and Forestry England (48 hectares). The wood features ancient woodland, coppiced sweet chestnut, and a mix of broadleaf and conifer trees, providing habitats for diverse wildlife and offering walking trails.

Name: Woodland Trust - Joyden's Wood
Description: Joyden's Wood, near Bexley, Kent, is an ancient woodland managed by the Woodland Trust. It features diverse tree species and supports varied wildlife. Public footpaths offer walking and recreation. Historical earthworks are also present.

Name: Woodland Trust - Round Wood
Description: Round Wood is a 7.5-hectare maturing woodland in Doncaster, South Yorkshire. It features a diverse mix of native broadleaf trees and accessible paths. The wood provides a valuable habitat for local wildlife and offers public access.

Name: Woods Mill
Description: Woods Mill is a 19-hectare nature reserve south of Henfield in West Sussex.  It is managed by the Sussex Wildlife Trust.

Name: Woodside
Description: Parndon Wood, near Harlow, is an ancient woodland managed by Harlow Council. It features varied tree species, hazel coppice, and a pond, supporting diverse wildlife, including woodland birds and invertebrates. Public access is available for quiet enjoyment.

Name: Woodsides Meadow
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Woodsides Meadow is a 4-hectare nature reserve south of Wendlebury in Oxfordshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Woodwalton Fen
Description: Woodwalton Fen is a National Nature Reserve within the Great Fen project. It features wet woodland, reedbed, and unimproved fen grassland, providing habitats for diverse wildlife. This internationally important site is actively managed to preserve its unique fenland ecosystems.

Name: Woody Bay
Description: Woody Bay is a secluded cove on the Exmoor Coast in North Devon, featuring a pebble beach, cliffs, and a waterfall. Part of the National Trust's managed Exmoor coastal area, it offers dramatic scenery and access via coastal footpaths.

Name: Woolacombe & Morte Point
Description: Woolacombe & Morte Point is a dramatic headland on the North Devon coast with spectacular views. The area features rugged cliffs, sandy beaches, and coastal footpaths, managed for conservation and public access.

Name: Woolbeding Countryside
Description: Woolbeding Countryside spans 500 acres near Midhurst, West Sussex. It features ancient woodlands, wildflower meadows, and open parkland. Visitors explore waymarked trails, enjoying diverse wildlife and panoramic views across the Rother Valley.

Name: Woolsthorpe Manor
Description: Woolsthorpe Manor, Isaac Newton's birthplace, features the room where he formulated gravity and light theories. The famous apple tree, inspiring his gravity insight, remains in the orchard. This National Trust site is a Grade I listed building.

Name: Woorgreens Lake and Marsh
Description: Woorgreens Lake and Marsh is a 9-hectare nature reserve in Gloucestershire.  The site is owned by the Forestry Commission and is managed by the Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust in partnership with the Forestry Commission.

Name: Worcester & Birmingham Canal Urban Biodiversity Spine
Description: The Worcester & Birmingham Canal links Worcester and Birmingham, passing through urban and rural landscapes. A new project, the 'Urban Biodiversity Spine', focuses on enhancing biodiversity and community engagement within Worcester, working in partnership with local organisations.

Name: Wormley-Hoddesdonpark Wood North
Description: Wormley-Hoddesdonpark Wood North is a 143.9-hectare woodland area in Hertfordshire which has been designated as a biological site of Special Scientific Interest.

Name: Wotton Hill SSSI
Description: Wotton Hill is a hill on the edge of the Cotswold Hills in Gloucestershire, England, 0.5 miles north of Wotton-under-Edge.

Name: Wrabness
Description: A local nature reserve of approximately 24 hectares.

Name: WWT Llanelli Wetland Centre
Description: WWT Llanelli Wetland Centre, near Llanelli, Carmarthenshire, south Wales, is a large nature reserve. It features a rich mosaic of lakes, pools, streams, scrapes, lagoons, coastal grazing marsh, scrub, and reedbed habitats. The site supports an extraordinary variety of wildlife, including numerous bird species, otters, and dragonflies.

Name: WWT London - Dragonfly Festival Hub
Description: WWT London Wetland Centre in Barnes hosts the Dragonfly Festival. Visitors explore its 105-acre urban wetland, engaging in pond dipping, guided walks, and crafts. The event highlights dragonfly life cycles and habitats, showcasing WWT's conservation work.

Name: WWT Welney Wetland Centre
Description: WWT Welney Wetland Centre is located in the Ouse Washes, a major wetland landscape in the Fens. The centre provides crucial habitat for thousands of migrating birds, including swans, geese, and ducks. Visitors can observe wildlife from hides and attend daily bird feeds.

Name: Wybunbury Moss
Description: Wybunbury Moss is a National Nature Reserve (NNR) and a rare example of a raised lowland bog in Cheshire. It features diverse Sphagnum mosses, rare plants, and invertebrates on a floating peat raft. It is owned and primarily managed by Natural England, with Cheshire Wildlife Trust also acting as a managing partner.

Name: Wye National Nature Reserve
Description: Wye National Nature Reserve is a chalk grassland site in Kent, recognised for its rich biodiversity. Primarily owned and managed by Natural England, it features rare orchids and wildflowers, supporting various insect species. The reserve offers walking trails and panoramic views of the surrounding landscape, providing a habitat for wildlife.

Name: Wykeham Forest
Description: Wykeham Forest, near Scarborough, is a mosaic of woodland and open space. It features the Raptor Viewpoint, offering views of birds of prey, and a diverse range of flora and fauna. The forest provides trails for walking and cycling.

Name: Wymeswold Meadows
Description: Wymeswold Meadows is a 4.5-hectare nature reserve east of Wymeswold in Leicestershire.

Name: Wymondham Rough
Description: Wymondham Rough is a 6. 0 hectares biological Site of Special Scientific Interest east of Stapleford in Leicestershire.

Name: Wyrley & Essington Canal Local Nature Reserve
Description: The Wyrley & Essington Canal is a Local Nature Reserve in the West Midlands, offering habitats for dragonflies, damselflies, and water voles. It provides routes for walking, cycling, and boating, forming part of the national cycle network.

Name: Yeading Brook Meadows
Description: Yeading Brook Meadows is a 17 hectare Local Nature Reserve in Yeading in the London Borough of Hillingdon.  It is owned by Hillingdon Council and managed by the London Wildlife Trust.

Name: Yearsley Woods
Description: Yearsley Woods is a tranquil mixed woodland located near Yearsley village, within the Howardian Hills AONB. It offers numerous walking, cycling, and horse riding trails. Two free car parks provide access to the site, which is open all year round.

Name: Yeavering Bell
Description: Yeavering Bell is a prominent Iron Age hill fort in the Cheviot Hills, Northumberland National Park. It is the largest hill fort in the region, featuring well-preserved ramparts and visible settlement remains. The site offers expansive views.

Name: Ynys-hir
HostOrg: RSPB (Royal Society for the Protection of Birds)
Description: Ynys-hir is an internationally important reserve on the Dyfi Estuary. It features saltmarsh, wet grassland, and woodland, providing habitat for migratory birds and other wildlife. Visitors can explore trails and hides.

Name: Yockletts Bank
Description: Yockletts Bank is a 25.4-hectare biological Site of Special Scientific Interest west of Stelling Minnis in Kent.

Name: Yoesden
HostOrg: Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust
Description: Yoesden, often known as Yoesden Bank, is a 13-hectare nature reserve in Bledlow Ridge in Buckinghamshire.  It is managed by the Berkshire, Buckinghamshire and Oxfordshire Wildlife Trust.

Name: Zennor Head & Gurnard's Head
Description: Dramatic coastal stretch on the Penwith peninsula, from Zennor Head to Gurnard's Head. Features granite cliffs, coves, and ancient field systems. Home to a variety of wildlife, including seabirds and grey seals.
